An agricultural worker initially sought treatment for knee pain at a medical center, only to later report being struck by a wooden sweet potato bin at work. After being treated at a workers' compensation clinic and cleared for full duty, the worker tragically passed away from unknown injuries a few days later. The employer was not informed of the worker's death until three weeks later.
An alleged report was received of an employee being struck by a forklift while backing up was received.

An decedent was trying to move 16 sheets of drywall (12' x 4' x 1/2") that were stacked on their side from one door jam to the other.  He ended up getting pinned between the door jam and the 16 sheets of sheetrock killed him.

An elder care employee drowned in a lap pool at her employer's private residence after suffering a heart attack. The employee, who was 58 years old and 5 feet 10 inches tall, was found unresponsive and floating face down in the pool several hours after going for a swim. Her lungs were filled with water and she had vomited in the pool, indicating a possible struggle before her death.

Due to exposure to high heat while working on a roof, an employee became dizzy and had to be assisted to an aerial lift by coworkers before being taken to the ground for rest. The employee later reported backing his vehicle into another vehicle after feeling too hot and believing he had passed out. Several hours after leaving the worksite, the employee became ill and was hospitalized, ultimately passing away at 4:50 a.m. on June 30, 2016, with the cause of death being listed
An employee  became flushed in appearance and started exhibiting heat exhaustion illness. This was the employee's first day on the job at a foundry.

The employee was part of a crew removing netting from nectarine trees when he started feeling ill while on a ladder. He informed his coworker and was told to rest under a tree, but soon began convulsing. He ultimately succumbed to a heat related illness on his second day of working in extreme temperatures, with the cause of death being heat stress.

During machine loading, a malfunction caused a part to drift and trip a sensor, activating a mis-programmed mechanical clamp that ultimately led to an employee's left ring finger being amputated down to the first knuckle.

An employee accessed the 1/12 pitch roof to assess storm damage on the west rake edge. While testing a bent piece of metal, he lost his balance and fell to the asphalt below. The employee suffered head and rib fractures, along with a collapsed lung, and was hospitalized as a result of the fall.

The employee was attempting to retrieve a fallen tarp from the top of a Summit 1995 open top trailer using a fixed ladder. As they reached for the tarp, the employee lost their balance and fell 8 feet 2 inches to the ground, resulting in a fatal injury.

An employee and coworker were directing traffic on a two lane road where one lane had been closed. They were alternating the flow of traffic when a vehicle driven by an outsider hit the employee, resulting in fatal injuries.

During a demolition of the outside refractory wall in the regenerator, a worker was fatally injured when part of the crown collapsed and buried them under bricks. The worker suffered a head injury resulting in a brain injury, as confirmed by the coroner's report.

While working on building a three car garage attached to a single family residential house, an employee and three coworkers were installing wood within the roof trusses, which were approximately 11 feet high. The roof trusses, each weighing 333 pounds and measuring 36 feet long, collapsed, crushing the employee between them and resulting in a fatal injury.

While installing air conditioning equipment in an attic, an employee and coworker placed large components of the equipment on plywood decking installed on the ceiling joists. However, a loose coupling on an electrical conduit inside the attic caused compromised wires, resulting in the conduit becoming energized. Despite not turning off the power to the conduit before entering the attic, the employee was electrocuted when he came into contact with the energized conduit.

During the installation of skylight panels, an employee wearing fall protection equipment accidentally stepped into the opening and fell to the concrete floor below, possibly striking a scissor lift. Despite using safety measures, the employee tragically suffered fatal head and neck injuries from the fall.

An employee and coworker were instructed to apply straw using a Finn Corporation Straw Blower at a construction site. While the coworker operated the pickup truck towing the blower, the employee stood on the bed of the truck. The coworker accidentally drove the truck up a hill with the employee on the bed, causing the employee to fall and suffer injuries. The incident investigation revealed that the coworker was unaware of the employee's presence due to the truck bed being filled with straw bales.

One employee and a coworker climbed a 35-foot ladder to the warehouse roof to cover the skylights with saran wrap. They initially worked together, but eventually separated. The employee fell through a skylight on the eastern part of the roof, plummeting 35 feet to the concrete floor below. Despite efforts to save him, the employee passed away in the hospital emergency room.

An employee and coworker were in an unprotected excavation when a wall partially collapsed, causing the employee to be struck by falling soil material. The employee suffered bruised legs and body but was treated and released from the hospital. Two surveyors from another company were also injured in the same incident, with one being released after treatment and the other hospitalized for three days.

During the process of adding a tire to a scrapped semi-trailer, an employee accidentally caused the trailer to shift, resulting in his left pinky finger getting amputated at the tip. The incident occurred while using a metal pry bar to help leverage the tire into place.

Two employees were assigned to clear a sewage line in a manhole outside of building "G". One employee entered the manhole while the other stood outside as an attendant. The employee inside the manhole was later found injured with severe injuries after being struck by an unidentified vehicle. Emergency medical services were called, and the employee was transported to Memorial Hospital with a skull fracture.

An employee and a coworker were changing settings on a robot system for a reboot when the coworker pressed the wrong button, causing a plate on the lift table to fall and injure the employee's right ring finger, resulting in a partial amputation.

An employee and coworker were cleaning wine making equipment in a warehouse that was set up as a wine cellar. The employee fell while rinsing out one of the large wine tanks, injuring his back, neck, and elbow. He was hospitalized for sixteen days and received treatment for his fractures.

During a routine measurement confirmation task, an employee and coworker were near an open and unguarded stairwell where stairs had yet to be installed. While focusing on blueprints and a masonry wall, the employee accidentally stepped into the open stairwell and fell 11 feet to the ground below. As a result, the employee suffered multiple fractures, including in his shoulder, ribs, and lower back, requiring hospitalization.

An employee and a coworker were emptying a trash cart into a dumpster. During emptying, one of the employee's hands became pinned between the edge of the dumpster and the trash cart. A portion of one of his finger tips was amputated, which he was hospitalized and received treatment.

During a work task, an employee had his finger under the shear guard as a coworker activated the machine, causing the employee's middle finger on his right hand to be amputated at the first knuckle. The employee was immediately taken to the hospital for treatment of his injuries.

During a boring operation, an employee and coworker were in an open excavation installing steel casing pipe. They struggled to remove a lifting strap from the pipe and called for a crane to help. Unfortunately, the crane's cable touched overhead power lines, electrocuting the employee.

During the unloading of glass crates inside a trailer, an employee and a coworker were working when a 3,500 lb crate of glass started tipping towards the employee. In an attempt to prevent the crate from falling, the employee used his back to support it, but the weight ultimately caused him to fall forward. Tragically, the falling crate struck the employee, resulting in his death.

While installing a gas fireplace on a two-story house under construction, an employee and coworker used a 24-ft fiberglass extension ladder and two fiberglass step ladders (8-ft and 4-ft), as well as hand tools. The employee was descending from the roof porch when he fell to the ground below, sustaining multiple fractures. He was air-lifted to the hospital but unfortunately died from his injuries on September 18, 2015.

An employee and coworker were installing wooden stair steps on a U shaped staircase inside a university dining facility that was still under construction. The employee fell from a height of 9 feet and 9 inches while installing the second step, resulting in a fractured skull. There was no railing or fall protection in place at the time of the incident.

During a work task to remove a large tree trunk, an employee and a coworker were inspecting the limbs when one suddenly broke, causing the trunk to roll onto the employee's leg. The employee suffered a fractured left leg and had to be hospitalized for treatment.

During the process of removing a wire rope sling from a bundle of granite slabs using a crane, the employee bent over in front of the slab rack. The coworker, operating the crane, unintentionally shifted the crane west, causing the bundle to topple over onto the employee, resulting in fatal injuries from being trapped under 1,200 lbs of stone. The employee passed away from the injuries sustained on December 18, 2015.

While assisting a coworker in moving a heavy modular cabinet with a forklift, an employee's right middle finger got caught and wedged in the top drawer of the cabinet, resulting in amputation. The employee did not require hospitalization for the injury.

An employee and a coworker were moving plants into a greenhouse to protect the plants from the weather. The employees were loading the plants into a bucket attached to a bobcat and transporting the plants to the greenhouse. The bobcat backed over the employee. The employee was killed.

While pumping liquid manure from a manure pit to a tanker trailer at a client's farm, an employee climbed to the top of the trailer to check the liquid level. Unfortunately, he slipped and fell to the ground, sustaining head and neck injuries. Despite efforts to save him, the employee later passed away from his injuries.

During the removal of metal decking material on a roof, an employee fell through a hole in the roof and landed on a cement floor, resulting in their death. The incident occurred as the employee and a coworker were lifting the decking material, and the employee fell through the 3 ft by 3 ft hole in the roof.

During the removal of pitch pans on an air-conditioning unit on a roof, an employee fell through the roof and suffered fatal injuries. The coworker who went off the roof to get tools and equipment found the employee after the fall. The employee sustained blunt force trauma to the head, neck, and trunk, resulting in their death.

During a routine jump start of a transporter, an employee was struck and pinned by a coworker driving the second transporter, resulting in a severe leg injury with muscle tearing off the bone. The incident occurred with TLD transporter #14031, model #TF 20 GR, serial #TF 186.

Two workers were tasked with installing pressure gauges on a steel piping system containing corrosive Green Liquor at high temperatures and pressures. During a safety briefing, they were informed about performing a hot tap while the liquid was flowing and the required personal protective equipment. Unfortunately, during the task, the employee sustained chemical and thermal burns when Green Liquor sprayed on him due to a malfunction while attempting to close a valve. He was hospitalized for his injuries.

During testing of a newly installed actuator on a dust collector, an employee had his right index finger inadvertently pressed against a rubber seal. The coworker cycled the pneumatic cylinders, causing the metal rings to close and amputate the tip of the employee's finger. The equipment was operating at a pressure between 95 and 100 p.s.i. at the time of the incident.

An employee and a coworker were transporting two trash containers using a manually-powered carriage. While at the dumpster area, the employee stepped on a 1 inch roofing nail, puncturing his left foot. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.

While trimming fronds off a palm tree, an employee was on a ladder using a chainsaw while a coworker collected the fallen fronds. The employee had a rope attached to him and the tree as a safety measure. Suddenly, the employee fell 25 feet to the ground and suffered blunt force trauma to his abdomen. The incident may have been related to power lines in the area.

An employee and coworker were unloading a large, heavy wall truck panel from a trailer, which was not adequately secured. As they moved the panel to the front of the trailer, it caused the other panels to collapse, fatally injuring the employee and injuring the coworker.

While working on a farm, an employee and coworker were pushing a grain auger by hand in the rain. The auger made contact with power lines, causing the coworker to be thrown several feet away and survive, while the employee tragically was electrocuted.

While working on a farm, an employee and coworker were preparing to set up a radar gun on a tractor attached to a seed planter. The coworker assumed the employee had left and unknowingly ran over them with the planter as they were checking the wire connection between the planter and tractor. The employee's son described this as normal prep work before seeding the farm.

While wrapping up switch gear tests, an employee disconnected an electrical conductor from a 480V panel, causing an arc flash that pushed him back against a wall. The coworker ran from the room and returned to find the employee unresponsive on the floor. Emergency services were called, but the employee later died from his burn injuries.

Two Spanish-speaking employees were working on renovating a two-story residential building by insulating the attic and walls and installing drywall. One employee attempted to turn on the incomplete HVAC unit in the attic using an extension cord and was electrocuted.

While attempting to move a steel truss to the south side of the building, an employee and foreman used a come-along to slide the truss along steel beams located above concrete. The employee, who was not properly secured to the structure, fell 17 feet 2 inches to the ground, resulting in multiple fractures and facial injuries. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.

A fatal incident occurred when an employee was struck by a tractor truck at a FedEx facility. The employee was disconnecting an air hose from the trailer when the tractor unexpectedly moved forward, causing the employee to be struck in the head and killed. The incident took place while the trailer was being stationed at its designated place.

During the set up of the press apparatus, the stainless steel shaft was being pressed into the aluminum block with 2,000 psi of pressure. However, the shaft shattered unexpectedly, causing a piece to strike and become lodged in the employee's abdomen. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.

The employee and business owner was cleaning the pool and spa when he slipped off a concrete ledge and hit his head. He was found unresponsive and pronounced dead at the hospital by the coroner after an autopsy, who suggested Myocardial Infarction as a possible cause of the slip.

An employee and co-worker were installing 3/4 inch thick by 3 ft wide by 8 ft long plywood close to the edge on the second floor. The employee stepped on the edge of the plwood he was nailing and fell 10 ft on the wooden stairway steps below. The employee cracked his rib. cracked his rib.

During a tree bucking operation, an employee was crushed by a 12 foot subtrunk when his coworker made a cut that separated it from the main trunk. The employee was working underneath the subtrunk, towards his coworker who was working on the main trunk at the time of the incident.

During a switching operation in a steel mill railyard, an employee attempted to jump onto a moving railcar and fell, resulting in severe injuries to their left leg which led to amputation. Tragically, the employee succumbed to their injuries and passed away.

An employee and two coworkers were moving roofing material to the roof of a 3-story apartment building using a truck-mounted conveyor belt. While on the roof, the third coworker on the truck bed fed material onto the conveyor belt. During the process of taking down a 90-ft "Poplar" Tree with an excavator, an employee crossed over to the left side of the machine while all other coworkers were standing behind it. As the tree started falling, a branch struck the employee in the back of the head, resulting in a fractured skull and fatal injuries.

An employee and coworkers were in the trench attempting to locate and clean sections. The trench wall on west side under the street collapsed into trench 11-ft. deep excavation.  The employee was killed due to asphyxiation. A back hoe was running near the excavation at the time of collapse.

During a construction project on Highway 220 in Summerfield, an employee was fatally struck by a Cat 330CL excavator while working in a trench with coworkers. The employee had exited the trench and was standing near a trench roller when the excavator pivoted, causing the tragic accident. It was uncertain whether the employee was hit by the bucket or the superstructure of the excavator.
An employee and coworkers were paving a parking lot. The employee was too close to a backhoe which ran over his foot. The employee fractured his ankle for which he was hospitalized.

An employee and coworkers were working in a trench to install a water line offset as part of a road widening project. The trench was deep and wide, with vertical walls and cohesive soil. After connecting the new and existing lines, the workers exited the trench to prepare for the next step. However, one worker re-entered the trench for unknown reasons and was struck by a collapsed wall, resulting in fatal injuries.

An employee and crew were laying pipe in east bound easement of FM 2252. The employee backed into a roadway and was struck by rear wheels of 18 wheeler truck. The employee was hospitalized and treated for fractured right leg.

After clocking out, two employees walked to their vehicles in the parking lot. One employee waved goodbye to the other as they drove off, but the coworker later noticed the employee still in his truck. The employee attempted to climb over a chain link fence and fell onto rocky ground before coming to a stop on the driveway near the gate.

While performing preventative maintenance on the baggage conveyor behind the ticket agent counter, an employee's right ring finger was amputated when it was caught in the unguarded chain and sprocket drive of the conveyor while it was running. The employee and his coworker had pressed the emergency stop button and removed the stainless steel cover to access the mechanics of the conveyor before the incident occurred. Despite the serious injury, the employee did not require hospitalization.

An employee and his coworker were moving a heavy 1,305 pound burner tip on a four wheeled cart. The cart's wheels got stuck in a pavement depression, causing the burner tip to tip forward and trap the employee beneath it. The employee suffered fractures in both ankles and was hospitalized for treatment.

During a tree cutting operation, an employee and his coworker were attempting to guide a falling tree away from utility lines using a tag line. Unfortunately, the falling tree hit a dead tree, causing it to break and a portion of it struck the employee in his back, shoulder, and chest. The employee was immediately hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.

An employee and his coworkers were installing a concrete storm water management riser in a water retention pond. The employee slipped and fell 10 feet down to a mud and gravel surface after standing on a narrow "waler" board. He sustained 2 fractured ribs and a back injury, resulting in hospitalization and release the next day.
An employee and the road packing equipment he was driving, slid down an embankment and flipped over. The employee was crushed and killed.

During the delivery of material to a commercial roofing job site, an employee and three coworkers used a safety monitor for fall protection. However, strong gusts of wind lifted the roofing material, causing it to strike the employee and push him off the roof. Despite having fall protection in place, the employee fell around 17 feet to the concrete, resulting in a broken elbow and fractured leg.
During a rope shortening operation on a freight elevator, an employee was struck by a cable after a shackle loosened, resulting in a bone fracture. He was hospitalized for treatment.
An employee and two coworkers were engaged in cutting down a tree. The tree fell and landed on the employee, crushing and killing him.

During the process of removing traffic control cones/barrels, an employee parked in a pickup truck on/near the shoulder of an on ramp with two coworkers removing cones/barrels behind the truck. Unexpectedly, the employee began reversing at a high speed, crossing into oncoming traffic in the open lane, resulting in a fatal crash. It is suspected that a medical condition may have been a contributing factor to the accident.

During the demolition of Q decking, an employee fell from the structure approximately 16-ft above the ground and landed on the pavement below, resulting in a fractured head and ultimately leading to their death. The employee was working with two coworkers at the time of the incident.

During a routine task of retrieving a balloon dam from a failed 48 inch line, an employee and two coworkers encountered a hazardous situation. The employee entered the line, made his way down to the damaged balloon, but was overcome by an unknown substance and lost consciousness while trying to climb back up. Tragically, the employee was killed from asphyxiation during the incident.

During horse training, an employee was thrown from his horse after a nearby wood chipper spooked the animal. He suffered multiple rib fractures on his right side and required hospitalization for treatment.

Three employees were cleaning the tube side of a reboiler unit inside a two-story building at an ethanol plant. The employer had warned them that hot water would be released during the operation, but there were no safety procedures in place. When the reboiler opened, 150-degree water sprayed onto one of the employees, causing second-degree burns to their shoulders, thighs, arms, hips, and back. The employee had to be hospitalized for their injuries.

The employee arrived at the business to drop off a trailer and pick one up. After dropping the trailer, he moved his truck to the bottom of the parking lot without a trailer attached. While kneeling in front of the truck, it began to roll forward, pinning him underneath the tire, leading to blunt chest trauma and his subsequent death.

An employee assembling a grill panel on a semi-tractor started having difficulty breathing and walked out of the shop. The owner approached the employee as the employee started shaking and collapsed.  The employee died from a heart attack.

An employee assembling a grill panel on a semi-tractor, had difficulty breathing, and walked out of the shop.  The owner approached the employee who started shaking and then collapsed. The employee died from a heart attack.
An employee assisting his coworker disconnected a trailer from a truck and was crushed between both objects. The employee was killed due to crushing injuries.
An employee assisting the loading of a flatbed trailer fell and fractured his skull.

An employee assisting with cutting activities was performing cutting operations near a 275 gallon used oil container. Sparks struck the oil container, causing an explosion. The employee sustained burns to the hands and lower body parts.

During a robbery at an auto parts store, two armed men demanded access to the cash register and safe. The safe had a time-lock feature that delayed opening for 10 minutes. The employee tried to explain this to the gunmen but it led to a struggle, resulting in the employee being shot and killed.

An employee ate dinner at the mess and then returned to his bunk room.  The employee complained of chest pain.  Safety personnel were called and were talking to the employee when he collapsed.  The employee died from cardiac arrest

An employee at a worksite was loading a skid steer onto a trailer manually due to heavy fluid leakage. The skid steer was attached to another truck with a chain and was on an incline with the engine off. While attempting to adjust the hydraulic controller inside the skid steer, the employee accidentally triggered the bucket to come down and was fatally crushed in the chest area, resulting in severe injuries and death.

The employee was covering an unsecured diamond steel floor plate with another metal plate when they stepped onto the unsecured plate and fell through. The steel plate struck the employee, fracturing their ribs and causing internal injuries. Tragically, the employee was killed by the weight of the steel plate.
An employee attending to the donation center fell from a trailer and sustained shoulder and neck injuries.  The employee died.

An employee backed his truck onto a trailer hitch and attached the cables.  While raising the trailer supports into travel position, the truck rolled back, pinning the employee against the adjacent trailer and crushing his chest.
An employee became light headed while pulling stock from a rolling stair tower and collapsed.  The employee was hospitalized and found to be endemic.

An employee became stuck in oven area when the second set of doors became jammed. As the employee worked to free himself from the area, he burned one of his hands and lower forearm. He was hospitalized for his injuries. his injuries.
An employee became unconscious while hiking and died.

An employee fell from a balcony railing while attempting to access a ladder, resulting in a two-story fall onto concrete. The employee suffered lacerations and a fractured elbow, requiring hospitalization.

An employee began work in an orange orchard. The employee was found unconscious by a coworker on the ground next to one of the orange trees. The coworker began performing CPR and emergency services were called, but the employee did not regain consciousness.

An employee fell to their death while being lifted in a personnel platform attached to a crane operated by the company owner. The employee was performing tree cutting duties when the hook unscrewed from the crane, causing the platform to fall to the ground. The employee suffered fatal injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by emergency responders.

The employee was struck by a mechanical arm of the entertainment machine "Skyfall" while attempting to pick up a fallen object for a client. The employee sustained severe bruising on the head and chest, leading to his unfortunate death.

An employee called her husband, reporting chest pains and feeling unwell while sitting in her car. Her husband found her unconscious with vomit outside the car, prompting him to call 911. Responders arrived within 15 minutes, but the employee tragically passed away at the hospital within an hour of being found.

An employee came in contact came in contact with 7,200 volt power line that was approximately 1 foot above the building. He fell approximately 14-15 feet to the concrete floor below. He sustained blunt force trauma to head and neck and was killed. It had been raining that day and the roof was wet.

An employee who came to work on Sunday to clean became ill with respiratory issues and was taken to the hospital by ambulance. Despite efforts to save him, he went into respiratory and cardiac arrest and later passed away. The cause of death was suspected to be from possible chemical exposure to chlorine.
An employee carrying a load of pistachios, struck a 70kV utility power pole and was killed.
An employee checking an air pump amputates her finger when the tip of her index finger is caught in a moving piston.

An employee cleaning a swimming pool was electrocuted and drowned after a faulty pool pump diverted electric power to the pool. The employee was found near the pool ladder and it was discovered that the neutral ground had become severed in a buried location, causing the circuit breaker to malfunction and not trip. The tragic incident highlights the importance of regular maintenance and safety checks in all work environments.

An employee was inspecting/repairing a heat valve in the Heating and Refrigeration Plant's T-3 Bag Room when he fell almost 10 feet to the concrete floor after losing his balance on a Werner-A-Frame Ladder. The employee sustained a laceration to the right eye, and pain to the left wrist and right knee as reported by the Chicago Fire Department's EMS.

An employee climbed a communication tower and was in position waiting for an antenna to be hoisted up for installation. The employee fell approximately 100 feet to the ground. The employee suffered from blunt force trauma and was killed.

An employee climbed a crane ladder 277 ft to perform a shift change. After being briefed by a co-worker, he suddenly fell unconscious and ultimately died from a possible heart attack. CPR was performed until emergency medical services arrived.

During a routine roofing job, an employee tragically fell 25 feet to the ground from a 40-foot metal extension ladder. The employee had climbed the ladder to hand tools to the owner of the company on the roof before the accident occurred. The fall resulted in the employee sustaining fatal blunt force trauma to the face, arms, and body.

During a tree cutting job at a customer's home, an employee climbed a 70-foot oak tree and began the process of cutting it down, starting with a face-cut. However, when the employee started on the back cut, the tree split down the side, causing the top portion of the tree to fall to the ground and pull the employee into the tree. Despite wearing personal protective equipment and having a safety line, the employee suffered blunt trauma to the abdomen and tragically died at the hospital.

While on top of a mobile home in tow, an employee grabbed an ATT/Comcast line to lift it for clearance. Unfortunately, the employee's head touched an energized overhead power line, resulting in a fatal exposure to live current. This incident led to the employee's clothes catching fire and ultimately causing their death from high voltage electrical current and the fall from elevation.

An employee climbed onto a jet ski float to stabilize the load on elevated forklift forks. Once the employee climbed onto the forks, the forks were raised to approximately 6 ft. above the ground when the load shifted and the employee fell. The employee was killed from a fatal head injury.
An employee climbed onto a storage rack.  The employee was not using fall protection. The employee fell off the storage rack and suffered three broken vertebrae and a fractured skull.

During an inspection, an employee climbed onto a crane catwalk from an aerial lift to check the collector's shoe. Standing on a wooden platform made of 0.625 inch plywood, the platform cracked and broke in the center, causing the employee to fall 27 feet to the ground. The employee suffered fatal trauma to the head and upper extremities.

An employee climbed over a guardrail and reached down to clear jam.  The employee's finger was caught in the conveyor belt system and amputated the employee's fingertip.  The employee was hospitalized.
An employee climbed over a guardrail on the sixtieth floor and jumped, landing on the street below. The employee fell approximately 950-ft and was killed on impact.

An employee climbed to the highest point of a stacker conveyor to grease the head pulley.  Concurrently, a coworker turned on the conveyor, causing the employee to fall to the ground and suffer a fatal head trauma.
An employee climbed to the roof of an apartment building and collapsed, his death was later determined to be heat related.

An employee tragically fell from the top ramp of a vehicle transport trailer while attempting to drive a vehicle down the ramp for delivery. The fall resulted in the employee sustaining fatal injuries, including head trauma, spinal trauma, and broken ribs.

An employee was killed while unloading steel pipes from a semitrailer. The employee released the ratchet chain binders on the load of pipe, causing it to roll towards him as he tried to escape. The pipe fell onto the employee, resulting in fatal crushing injuries.
An employee climbing a ladder fell and fractured his skull. The employee sustained severe brain swelling and was killed from brain damage.
An employee climbing an extension ladder to frame around a wood stove "B" vent on a roof, fell from the top of the 23-foot ladder to the ground.  He sustained head trauma and was killed.

An employee clocked out from a normal shift at 4:30 p.m. The employee was found unconscious on a sidewalk. The employee was transported by emergency response services to a medical center and the employee later died.
An employee collapsed and died when moving items.
An employee collapsed from a heart attack while working in a permit-required confined space. Atmospheric monitoring showed no signs of oxygen deficient atmosphere. The employee died.

An employee complained of feeling unwell at work and went to his car to rest. A coworker brought him a cold drink, but when he returned with it, the employee had become unresponsive. It was later discovered that the employee had died of a massive heart attack, with severe blockages in his main coronary artery and other occlusions.
An employee contacted live lines while working on a power line. At approximately 12:30 p.m. on January 16, 2017, the employee died due the shock he received.

An employee crawled underneath a truck to manually manipulate the transmission in order to put the truck into reverse. The truck rolled backwards onto the employee catching him between the tire and pavement. The employee was killed.
An employee crushed his thumb while working with a press brake. The employee was hospitalized and treated for fractured thumb.

An employee was carrying a piece of Tyvec for installation when he accidentally stepped into a floor opening and fell between the three stringers for the stairs. He landed on the concrete floor and a piece of lumber, suffering three broken ribs, a fractured hip, and internal bleeding. He required hospitalization and had to have his spleen removed as a result of the injuries sustained.
An employee died from a blood clot that ended up causing their heart to stop.
An employee died from complications of acute respiratory distress syndrome. The employee's death was determined to be due to natural causes.
An employee died from smoke inhalation after blunt force injuries to the head. This was a case of homicide and arson.
An employee died of unknown causes at work.
An employee died while unloading a trailer. The employee was found lying face down. The employee died from complications of hypertension and pneumonia.
An employee driving a dump truck rolled over and was killed.

An employee driving a forklift with a load of boxes stood up and leaned forward to read the manifest on the boxes on the pallet. The employee was killed when the forks unexpectedly lowered onto his neck.
An employee driving a golf cart at the terminal yard, crossed  an intersection and the employee was struck and killed by tractor trailer.

An employee driving an all terrain vehicle (ATV) home from work had an accident on a public road. The employee struck his head on the asphalt and was killed from a brain injury. The details of the accident are unknown.

An employee drove a delivery vehicle from La Palma to Fullerton.Another coworker (driver) found the employee slumped over the steering wheel while parked at a satellite delivery site. The employee died of natural causes (atherosclerotic and hypertensive cardiovascular disease).

An employee drove his truck to a worksite to pick up an empty trailer.  The employee had walked about 100 feet from the dock area when he suddenly collapsed.  Emergency Services responded within five minutes and the employee was pronounced dead at the scene due to a massive cardiac arrest.

The employee was tragically killed when he was struck by a coworker in a semi-trailer truck while bending down next to his own truck in the warehouse yard. The incident occurred despite the yard being adequately lit, with the coworker failing to see the employee in his path. The employee suffered multiple blunt force trauma injuries as a result of the accident.

While unloading lumber from a forklift on the third floor of a residential construction site, an employee fell approximately 30 feet to the ground. Emergency services were called and the employee was taken to Westchester Medical Center for treatment of multiple fractures. The employee was not utilizing any fall prevention methods or wearing a fall arrest system at the time of the incident.
