An employee was using a steel pipe wrench on a platform to break a connection from the kelly. The driller accidentally shifted gears in the wrong direction, causing the wrench to strike the employee in the head, resulting in a fatal skull fracture and brain hemorrhage.

An employee fell approximately 13 feet from a scaffold while removing banding from a cube of bricks. He struck a wooden patio with loose bricks and fractured his spine, leading to hospitalization for treatment.

An employee was standing on a scaffold system while signaling a crane to place pre-fab roof panels into place. The scaffold was unguarded and the employee fell to the ground, suffering internal injuries and a lacerated heart, resulting in his death.

An employee was standing on a scaffold, cutting trees branches. When the branch fell from the tree, it caused the employee to fall from the scaffold.  The employee struck the concrete slab below, suffered brain damage and was killed.

An employee was standing on a shelving unit that was between 11 and 15 feet above ground level. One of the shelves support beams became dislodged, causing the employee to fall to the cement floor below.  He sustained a broken left wrist, which he was hospitalized and received treatment.

An employee was standing on a steel grate that slipped off the supporting beam and fell to the lower level 18 feet below. The employee was wearing a personal fall arrest system but was not tied off. The employee sustained a fractured skull, severed spinal cord, and he was hospitalized.
An employee was standing on a step ladder while pulling off the visqueen hanging from the ceiling.  He lost his balance and fell 3 or 4 feet. He injured his left wrist and arm.

An employee was standing on a tree limb, approximately 12 feet above the ground, to retrieve a broken branch. The limb he was standing on broke and the employee fell to the ground, fracturing one of his legs.
An employee was standing on an A-Frame ladder cutting tree branches when he is struck in the head by a branch. The employee was killed.

During hedge trimming, an employee fell 10 feet from an extension ladder that was being supported by the dense hedge. The employee suffered a fractured left wrist and was admitted to UCSD Medical Center. They were discharged on February 17, 2017.

An employee was servicing a truck on a five feet high surface of lavatory waste when he lost balance and fell over the side of the truck. The truck had no guard rails in place, causing the employee to suffer head contusions, four fractured ribs, and a fractured thumb. The employee was hospitalized as a result of the injuries sustained in the fall.

During an inspection of a garbage truck, an employee's left thumb was caught in the side door latch of the truck while standing on a fixed ladder. Losing his balance, the employee fell off the ladder, resulting in the amputation of his left thumb. The employee was taken to the hospital for treatment of his injury.

An employee was standing on the forks of the forklift that were being lifted up.  The employee was crushed between the forklift backrest and the truck as the forklift moved forward.  The employee was killed from crushing injuries to the head.
An employee was standing on the main floor of a one story plus basement single family residence when the trusses collapsed.  The employee was crushed when the trusses collapsed.

An employee was fatally injured when they were caught between the tailgate and body of a garbage truck while it was being lowered. The incident occurred as the coworker was dumping a load of garbage and moved the truck forward to clear the pile. The employee was standing close to the rear tires on the passenger side of the truck during the operation.

An employee was standing on the steps of a semi truck while removing stickers from the drivers-side window and windshield. The employee either slipped or tripped off the truck steps and fell backwards to the asphalt, striking his head and was killed.

An employee was standing on top of a 10 foot wall.  The employee stepped down to a nine foot level and misjudged the distance.  The employee fell to the ground below injuring his neck, and was killed.
An employee was standing on top of a 40 cubic yard dumpster to remove debris. The employee fell off the dumpster and sustained multiple injuries to the face, head, wrists, and neck.
An employee was standing on top of a rail and truck.  The employee fell and received a compound fracture to his right ankle.
An employee was standing on top of trailer covering a load of wood dust with a tarp.  The employee fell from the top of the trailer and was killed when his head hit the ground.
An employee was standing on tree limb appx. 20 feet high while cutting tree branches. The employee lost his balance, fell to the ground, sustained head trauma, and died.

During maintenance on an electrical power line, an employee and coworker were setting up a digger truck to replace a 30 foot electrical pole. The operator of the truck accidentally made contact with the power line, causing it to energize and resulting in the employee being electrocuted. Tragically, the employee was killed in the incident.

The employee was fatally injured when two 400 lb granite slabs fell off a truck during loading and landed on them. This tragic incident occurred due to a strong gust of wind blowing the unsecured slabs off the rack. The employee was struck in the legs and abdomen, ultimately resulting in their death.
An employee was standing when they were struck by a vehicle and was killed.  No further specifics were included in the initial report.

An employee was stapling a metal sign using a metal sign stitcher (or stapler). During work, one of employee's thumb was struck by a staple, resulting in lacerations to the area. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.

An employee was stapling a metal sign using a metal sign stitcher (or stapler). During work, one of his thumbs was struck by a staple, resulting in lacerations to the area. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.

An employee fell from a ladder while stapling a plastic sheet onto a metal frame on a greenhouse structure, landing on a wooden bench before hitting the pavement. The employee suffered a fractured back and was taken to the hospital by a coworker.

An employee was starting a chainsaw so he could trim branches from tree trunk in the street. The Employee was bent over the chainsaw when the 50-ft. tree trunk rolled over on top of him.  The employee suffered crushed sternum, broken ribs, and broken femur and was killed.
An employee was starting the Becca solvent recycler to recover ethanol when the material flashed and burned the employee's arms, chest and legs.

The employee was found unresponsive between the roller and band while starting up the oven for snack food production. It appeared that the employee was pulled into the ingoing nip point and killed. There was no guarding in place for the nip point at the time of the incident. The employee's right upper arm was caught between the roller and band, and his left arm was caught at the elbow.

An employee was steadying a steel 2 yard container on the lift-gate of a 2005 Ford F550.  The container rolled off the lift-gate while the employee attempted to hold it back.  The container fell onto the employee, crushing his head and leg.  The employee was killed by trauma to the head.

An employee collapsed and died while stirring BASF Master Seal waterproofing chemicals with a drill powered by a generator. The employee was not wearing respiratory protection. The employer initially reported the employee had an epileptic seizure with a possible head injury, but the cause of death was unknown.

During stocking materials in a warehouse, an employee was struck on the neck by a falling shelf that was knocked over by a powered industrial truck operating nearby. The employee suffered lacerations to the neck and was hospitalized for treatment.

An employee was stocking office supplies in the warehouse.  The employee became ill and went into the restroom to rest. The employee was found nonresponse.  The employee sustained a ruptured dissecting thoracic aorta and had hypertensive cardiovascular disease. disease.

An employee fell from a two-step A-frame mobile ladder while stocking shelves at work, resulting in fractures to her tibia and patella on her left side. She was hospitalized and required surgery as a result of the incident.

An employee was killed while straightening steel plates on a hydraulic press brake. A steel block and a piece of steel banding material were placed on top of the plate, but when the press was activated, the shim broke apart and caused pieces of metal to strike the employee in the abdomen, resulting in fatal puncture wounds.

An employee was straightening out a piece of wood from the unscramble.  The employee reached over the machine and caught his left hand in the sprocket and chain.  The employee amputated their index finger and middle finger from their left hand.

An employee was stretching a protective membrane over the top of a commercial roof structure.  The employee fell approximately 28 feet from the roof and struck the ground.  The employee was killed as a result of their injuries.

An employee was stretching out a foam hose on a roof top.The employee fell through a skylight and fell approximately 34 feet to the concrete floor.  The employee suffered internal bleeding and was killed.
An employee was stringing electrical cords on the roof for charging batteries and fell through a skylight.  The employee struck the concrete floor and was killed.
An employee was stringing electrical cords on the roof to charge batteries and fell through a sky light.  The employee was killed when they struck the concrete floor.
An employee was stringing electrical cords on the roof to charge batteries and fell through a skylight to a concrete floor.  The employee was killed by the fall.

While setting up a new production run, an employee was using a chain puller known as a "puller dog" to string wire through a wire drawing machine. The employee opened a small door to check on the wire wrapped around the capastan block when the wire came loose from the puller dog, causing the chain to strike the employee in the face and hands. The employee was subsequently taken to the hospital for medical treatment.

An employee was stripping a bathtub in an apartment using Napco White Lightning Low Odor Stripper. The employee was found dead slumped over the bathtub. The employee inhaled methylene chloride, which was in the Napco White Lightning Low Odor Stripper.

An employee was stripping a live energized 120V 12 gauge with non-insulated Milwaukee multi-tool wire strippers and electrocuted themselves wile touching a surface that grounded them, completing the circuit through his body.

An employee was stripping titan slab formwork from an aluminum forms system. The employee fell while working at the edge of a shaft which was protected by guardrail but somehow the employee fell in spite of this.  The employee was killed from blunt injuries to head, neck and torso.
An employee was struck and killed by a garbage truck.
An employee was struck and killed by a train while trying to cross the railroad tracks on a roller.
An employee was struck and killed.
An employee was struck and killed. The employee sustained blunt force trauma to the head.
An employee was struck by a forklift and killed.  No further information was available from initial reports.
An employee was struck by a forklift and sustained a knee injury.

On May 30, 2017 at 5:30 am, an employee was struck by a forklift as it was backing out of a truck being loaded with wooden pallets. The employee sustained multiple injuries to his left leg, knee, and foot. Tragically, he passed away at home later that day, with the cause of death being reported as his lungs filling with fluid and suffering a heart attack.
An employee was struck by a minivan while mowing grass with a zero-turn mower.  The employee received trauma to the head and was killed.

An employee was hit by a moving vehicle while checking the transmission fluid level in a Nissan pickup truck at the employer's parking lot. Despite trying to stop the truck, the employee was knocked down and run over, resulting in serious injuries. The employee later died from blunt force trauma, with the investigation revealing the truck had transmission issues prior to the incident.
An employee was struck by a truck while walking through the yard. The employee was hospitalized and died from injuries.

An employee was struck by a upended log. The employee broke both of his arms, all of his ribs, punctured his lungs and injured his eye socket. The employee was transported to the hospital and later died on July 27th 2016, at 5:39 pm.
An employee was struck by a vehicle while preparing to direct traffic departing the school. The employee was airlifted to the hospital where he was pronounced dead.
An employee was struck by an automated forklift causing blunt force trauma to his chest and neck.  The employee was killed.

An employee was struck by lightning while working on a roof.  While retrieving a pneumatic nail gun from the roof he was struck by lightning. The employee endured burns as he was electrocuted and fell from the roof.
An employee was struck in the back of the head by an alder tree. She received chain lacerations to the front of the head above the eyes and was killed.

An employee was stung by a bee while standing near the dock performing routine job functions outdoors.  The employee suffered an anaphylaxis reaction and died as a result.  There was no known history by either the employer or family that this employee had a history of such reactions to bee venom.

During a class of children, an employee suffered a severe allergic reaction to peanuts after a child touched their face and arms with peanut residue from candy. The employee had to be rushed to the hospital due to difficulty breathing, putting their life in danger.
An employee was supervising crews that were harvesting vegetables.  The employee was ill and became dizzy, fainted, lost consciousness, and died.

An employee was tasked with filling an electrical trench using a soil compactor and backhoe. However, the employee was found lifeless in his hotel room by his supervisor, having not shown up for work that morning. The employee ultimately passed away from unknown causes.
An employee was sweeping a floor. The employee backed off the open side of a receiving dock to a lower level concrete floor and sustained a concussion and bleeding on the brain.

The employee was sweeping sawdust between two CNC routing machines when they tripped on a conduit, falling and hitting their head on one of the machines. Sadly, the employee passed away due to the injuries sustained from the fall.

An employee was sweeping snow from the top landing of a building entrance when he fell down the stairs.  After falling down six steps, he crashed through a glass window. He received a laceration to his neck and was killed.
An employee was sweeping the mud and debris left from the trucks on the median of a highway.  A private citizen driving a car struck him.  The worker flew 20 yds and was killed instantly.

An employee was sweeping trash from around a 7-yard dumpster when he was struck by it.  The employee was taken to the hospital and had several fractures to his lower body.  He died later while at the hospital.

An employee was sweeping water from an elevated location when he slipped and fell 12 feet to the ground.  The employee sustained a broken rib, which he was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.

During a metal roof building repair job, an employee was found unconscious by a coworker while sweeping and cleaning up debris. The coworker immediately called 911 and began CPR, but unfortunately the employee could not be revived and passed away on the scene, possibly due to a heart attack.
An employee was swimming and was within 10 to 15 feet from reaching the final destination when he drowned.

During a collet change on the HAAS ST-10 machine, a coworker accidentally started the machine without warning. The employee was struck by a wobbling aluminum bar stock, resulting in a severe laceration and shattered bone in their thumb.

An employee was tagging and wrapping pallets and using the PIT to transfer to the warehouse. The employee was looking to see the pallets left on the front area and was struck-by the pallet transfer car. The employee died from crushing injuries to the chest and upper torso.
An employee was taking a break, walking to or from the bathroom. The employee fainted and fell backwards, he hit his head on the floor and was killed from a head laceration.
An employee was taking a knife out of a cardboard sheath, the knife cut through the cardboard sheath, and the employee's hand was cut.
An employee was taking a restroom break while harvesting oranges. Upon returning to the orange orchard, the employee suffered an apparent heart attack, fell to the ground and died.

An employee was taking a water break at the jobsite.  When he didn't return to work, coworkers sought him out and found him unresponsive in the jobsite equipment trailer.According to the autopsy report, the employee's death was caused by coronary artery thrombosis (heart attack).

An employee was taking his lunch break and began to feel numbness and pressure on his chest.  No further details were provided in the initial accident report to detail the extent of injuries or the result thereof.  The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was taking measurements and fell.  The employee fractured both ankles when they landed on the floor. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.

An employee was taking measurements for a roofing and solar project at a residential house. The employee fell approximately 9 ft. to the ground below while descending the portable ladder. He suffered fractured arms and laceration to forehead.

An employee was taking measurements for a trim board of the dormer on the 12 by 12 pitch roof.  The employee fell 26 feet to the ground before continuing the fall another 10 feet to the bottom of a basement window egress pit.  The employee was killed.

An employee was taking out recycling at a facility. As he stomped on a card board box to break it down, he lost his balance, fell, and hit his head. He suffered a skull facture and bleeding on the brain. He later died of complications from the fall on January 12, 2017.
An employee was taking out the garbage. The employee suffered an apparent heart attack after which he fell off the loading dock and died.
An employee was taking out the side walls of an old boat house. The structure collapsed striking the employee and pinning him down. The employee was killed from asphyxia from the wooden structure.
An employee was taking photos of the work completed on a cell tower and fell 220 feet.  The employee was killed at the scene.

An employee was taking the gear box of an shredder to replace its bearings. As the shredder was raised approximately 3 feet above the ground by a jack and blocks, a malfunction occurred. The shredder fell and struck the employee in the head, killing him.

An employee was working on the roof of Bldg105, taking waste to the dump box and cleaning the area. They complained of feeling hot and were given water to drink and a makeshift shade area to rest in. After feeling better, they continued working but later started vomiting and eventually succumbed to heat stress/heart attack.
An employee was talking on a cell phone while a bulldozer was backing up. The employee was struck and run over by the bulldozer and her head was crushed.
An employee was talking to a coworker. When the employee turned from the nurses station to walk away, she fell, breaking her left hip and pelvis
An employee was talking to a youth. The decision was made to restrain the youth. The employee was killed from unknown an injury.

During a conversation with a co-worker while waiting for information from a mechanic, an employee suddenly collapsed. Despite immediate 1st Aid and CPR efforts, the employee tragically passed away due to a heart attack. In the process, the employee sustained a fractured sternum and ribs.

During a conversation with a coworker filling a high pressure oxygen bottle, the coworker tried to speed up the process which resulted in the booster over pressurizing and igniting, causing burns to the employee's arms and chest. The employee had to be hospitalized and treated for their injuries.

An employee was taping the end of a roll of paper that was still moving. His left middle finger became pinned between the equipment's stop bar and the roll of paper, which weighed 7,000 pounds, resulting in its amputation. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.
An employee was taping, mudding, and smoothing drywall while on a rolling scaffold. The employee fell from the scaffold, suffering a hemorrhagic stroke and epidural hematoma, and was killed.
An employee was tapping a new connection into a pad mounted transformer. A tool contacted an energized part and caused an arc flash. The employee sustained second and third degree burns to the face.

During a valve replacement operation, an employee's right leg was accidentally struck by the valve as it dropped off while he was trying to turn it. The impact caused his previous knee replacement to break a couple of inches below the knee. The employee was hospitalized for treatment and recovery.

An employee successfully replaced a coil on a steel roll-forming machine using a 7.5 Ton Trambeam crane. However, while feeding the coil chain through the coil and lifting it with the crane, the chain became stuck between the mandrel and the coil. In an attempt to free the chain, the employee placed his left hand inside the mandrel, resulting in the amputation of the tip of his left middle finger.

The employee was tasked with installing recessed ceiling lighting but was discovered deceased under the house by the homeowners. They were found adjacent to a live 120 volt junction box and live open wire. It is unclear why the employee was under the house, but a live exposed 120 volt Romex wire was found on the ground near where they were discovered.

The employee was tasked with cleaning production and bag house and was using a JLG man lift to access the upper level of the framework around the cyclones. They tied a 100-foot fire hose to the basket of the man lift and as they backed up the machinery with no slack in the hose, the basket was pulled down causing the employee to fall to their death.

An employee was tasked with cleaning spilled plastic resin with a broom and vacuum.  The employee was later found by a coworker was unresponsive.  The employee was presumed dead due to a heart attack.

The incident occurred when an employee failed to follow lockout/tagout procedures while replacing a bolt on a pneumatic cylinder of a Sutton press. As a result, the press cycled and the employee's right thumb was struck by the ram, resulting in the amputation of his thumb.

The employee, who was wrapping shrink wrap around used water heaters for recycling, experienced chest pains and left-side numbness while taking a break. Tragically, the employee suffered a heart attack and passed away.
An employee was tearing boards off the walls of the garage with a hammer. The roof of the garage fell onto the employee and struck his head. The employee was killed.
An employee was tearing off old roofing material on an industrial building.  The employee fell through a 27 feet roof onto a concrete floor and was killed from multiple injuries.

An employee was tearing off the roof and slipped. The employee was wearing fall protection and the rope caught the gutter and swung the employee into the stairs. As a result the employee broke his ankle. The employee was not hospitalized.
An employee was tearing shingles from a roof when he fell 16 feet to the ground. He struck his head and died. The incident investigation revealed that the worker was not wearing fall protection.

During a test drilling operation for sinkhole activity, an employee accidentally made contact with a high voltage power line, resulting in severe internal injuries from a 7,026 volt shock. Using a drilling machine without proper identification, the employee crawled a few feet to safety before collapsing and going into cardiac arrest. Unfortunately, the employee passed away on July 7, 2016 without regaining consciousness.

During testing of a shoring cylinder, an employee's fluid hose became caught in the testing machine, resulting in the employee becoming entangled with the equipment. In the process of freeing himself, the employee sustained an amputated middle finger and lacerated ring finger.

An employee was testing a solenoid on a small piece folder (for folding patient gowns).  The unit was running and the back half of the wrench he was using was pulled into the folder along with his hand. The roller on the piece folder crushed the employees hand.

Tragically, an employee acting as a fire watch at a work site was killed when a coworker operating an excavator accidentally swung the equipment and struck them in the head with a transport stand for a vibratory hammer. The coworker had not noticed the employee within the swing radius of the hammer, resulting in the fatal incident.

While inspecting the framing work on the third floor, an employee fell approximately 28 feet to the concrete basement floor after stepping through a plastic covering over a floor hole. The employee sustained a skull fracture from a sprinkler pipe and was killed as a result of the fall.

The employee, who was alone at the site, was tasked with moving a scrubber between units in a duplex house. The next day, he was discovered in a construction dumpster below a balcony, which was missing part of its guard rail. It is believed that he fell from the balcony to his death.

An employee was the rolling stock operator for a locomotive operation at a lumber mill. The employee slipped trying to board a moving railcar, fell under the railcar,was run over, and died. was run over, and died.

During a firefighting operation to extinguish a chimney fire in a burning basement, an employee was the second man on a fire hose. The coworker operating the nozzle noticed that the employee had disappeared from the line and called out his name. Tragically, the employee was found to have died from asphyxiation due to exposure to superheated combustible products. This incident was documented in Reports 82509 and 82372.

An employee serving as the second man on a fire hose during a chimney fire in a burning basement was tragically killed. The coworker on the nozzle noticed the employee was missing and later found out that the employee had succumbed to asphyxiation from superheated combustible products. See Report 82509 for more details.

During a firefighting operation, an employee was serving as the second man on a fire hose aimed at a burning basement. The nozzle man discovered the employee missing and upon investigation, it was found that he had tragically succumbed to asphyxiation from the superheated combustible products in the basement. The employee's life was lost in the line of duty while trying to extinguish the fire.

An employee was threading material from a curing vault to the dryer.As material was cut, it created a pinch point between the material and roller. The employee's hand was wrapped into the roll along with his forearm, breaking his arm in two places. h his forearm, breaking his arm in two places.
An employee was throwing debris into a dumpster. The employee fell about 27 feet to the pavement below. The employee sustained broken bones and was killed.
An employee was throwing trash bags and boxes into a dumpster. A bag hit the top of the dumpster and struck the employee, causing him to fall to ground. He sustained a fractured right hip and femur.

The employee was tightening a hydraulic hose on a 1980 Ford F-350 dump box when they turned the fitting the wrong way, causing the dump box to lower onto them. The employee was caught underneath the box and tragically killed by asphyxiation.

An employee was tightening bolts on a column next to I-Beam at a height of approximately 18 ft. The employee climbed out of the basket onto the I-Beam. After losing his balance, the employee fell to the cement ground and died from multiple blunt force injuries.

During a routine maintenance task, an employee was injured when a machine assembly tipped over and pinned him beneath it. The incident occurred as a coworker was removing wire rope rigging with an overhead crane, causing the clevise to catch the machine. The employee suffered a fractured rib and vertebra, requiring hospitalization and treatment.

During a routine maintenance task, an employee's hand got caught between drill rods and the drill rig when the operator unknowingly moved the drill. The employee suffered a dislocated wrist and had to undergo surgery to repair ligament damage.

During maintenance work, an employee was tightening the bolts on the manhole cover of an oil tank when a spark ignited flammable vapors, causing the tank to explode. The employee suffered second degree burns to the face and respiratory system before succumbing to injuries from the blast.
An employee was tightening up u-bolts on the top of a tanker truck.  The employee fell from the truck and was killed when his head struck the concrete floor, fracturing his skull.
An employee was told to "roll-up" for the day. The employee fell off the roof and struck the concrete surface below and was killed.
An employee was topping a tree using a chain saw.  The employee was pulled into the tree by his lanyard when the tree split.  The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.

An employee was topping off wine barrels while standing on a 12 foot mobile ladder.  The employee fell from the ladder and landed on the floor and a wine barrel rack.  The employee sustained multiple injuries that included fractured wrist, and ribs and a blood clot in his head.

The employee was working on torqueing bolts and safety wiring on a transmission in the left wing of a Boeing 737, standing about 10 feet high on a 6 foot A-frame ladder. They were found lying on the ground next to the ladder, indicating a possible fall. Unfortunately, the employee was killed by blunt force trauma to the back of the head and a broken nose.

During a car wash cycle, a driverless car veered off the conveyor track system and the employee attempted to enter the car. In the process, he accidentally shifted the car into reverse and was found between two vertical mitters near the tunnel entrance with serious head injuries, ultimately resulting in his death.

While towing a trailer-mounted welding machine at a metal fabrication shop, an employee's trailer became detached from the Daewoo PIT they were using due to incorrect attachment bolts. The employee tried to stop both the trailer and the PIT as they rolled down a slope, but tragically slipped and was struck by the 9,590 pound PIT, resulting in fatal injuries.

During a training session, an employee's fingers were crushed by a sewer drain cleaner machine when the cutter bit bound up and caused the rod to wind up. The employee had to undergo surgical amputation of the tip of his index and middle fingers and was hospitalized as a result of the incident.

During a training session on blackberry plants, an employee suddenly collapsed and was unresponsive after complaining of chest pain. Emergency services were called and CPR was administered, but unfortunately, the employee was unable to be saved and was pronounced dead due to a heart attack.
An employee was transferring ethanol from storage tanks to a semi-trailer tanker. The ethanol ignitied and the employee was killed from burns.

An employee was transferring hot water wash from one tank to another, when he was splashed with the water. The water measured between 140 degrees and 150 degrees Fahrenheit and he was burned. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.

During a metal parts transfer for powder coating, a heavy bin being supported by a powered industrial truck fell onto an employee's back as they were reaching inside. The impact caused a fractured vertebrae, resulting in partial paralysis from the chest down for the employee.

During a storm with wind gusts exceeding 40 mph, a large pine tree was knocked over and struck an employee who was transferring propane from a delivery truck to a residential LPG tank. The employee was pinned against the LPG tank by a branch of the fallen tree, resulting in a laceration to the head, concussion, and a fractured sternum. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.

An employee was transporting a compressed gas cylinder.  The compressed gas cylinders fell off the landing and struck the employee in the right leg and fractured his right ankle. employee in the right leg and fractured his right ankle.

During the transportation of a Mercury Mountaineer, an employee mistakenly put the tow truck into reverse instead of park. The truck began to roll backwards, causing the employee to try and jump back into the truck, resulting in being run over. Unfortunately, the employee later died at University of Louisville Hospital.

An employee traveling on an ATV from a building to his work area at a facility drove off an embankment next to a parking lot, landing in a creek 50 feet below. Tragically, the employee was killed in the accident.

During a ride in a golf cart, an employee was ejected after the driver swerved to avoid hitting a small animal. The employee landed on the road, hitting their head on the asphalt and sustaining fatal injuries resulting in their death.
An employee was traveling north bound and drove down an 8 foot embankment, crashed into a parked BNW Train, and started a fire.  The employee was killed during the fire.
An employee was traversing an elevated floor, when the surface gave way. The employee fell through floor and struck some equipment below, fracturing two of his ribs and sustaining a punctured lung.
An employee was tree trimming when he fell from a height.  He was killed by his injuries two months later.
An employee was trimming a ponderosa pine tree when the tree broke and fell.  The employee fell to the ground as well and suffered blunt trauma to their skull, killing the employee.
An employee was trimming a tree and fell from the tree to the ground.  The employee was killed when he struck the ground.
An employee was trimming a tree using a articulating bucket truck.  The employee fell 30 feet from the bucket and struck the ground, fracturing their leg.
The employee was trimming branches near a high voltage power line when a branch swung into the line, electrocuting them while they were still holding it.
An employee was trimming branches from a tree with a chain saw. The employee fell from a basket at a height of 30 feet. The employee was killed by the fall.
An employee was trimming branches when they fell from an elevated bucket to the ground.  No further specifics were provided in the original report.
An employee was trimming limbs from an oak tree. The employee fell from a limb into a bush where a branch penetrated the employee's neck and killed him.

The employee was trimming palm trees on a 28 foot aluminum extension ladder near a 7.6 kV power line when one of the prongs made contact, causing him to receive an electrical shock. He fell from the ladder, fracturing his skull and face, and suffered internal bleeding which ultimately resulted in his death.
An employee trimming branches from a silver maple tree fell 15 feet to the ground when the articulating boom truck bucket tipped, striking their head. The employee was killed instantly.

An employee was trimming tree tops from a maple and hickory tree when the maple tree broke below the rope anchorage point. The employee fell approximately fourteen feet, landing on a chain saw and the ground, sustaining a fractured vertebrae.

The employee was trimming trees and removing vines using a climbing rope when his primary climbing rope was accidentally cut through by a hand saw, causing him to fall 40 feet to the ground. The employee sustained severe injuries including a broken neck, head trauma, brain trauma, and multiple broken ribs.
An employee was trimming trees at a residence.  The employee was working from a lift and contacted the power lines.  The employee was electrocuted.
An employee was trimming trees using a power pole and touched the electrical line. The employee was electrocuted and killed from contact with the electrical line.

The employee was trimming trees and fell while working on a tree approximately 100 feet tall. He sustained multiple fractures to his face, arms, hands, legs, torso, and skull. It was discovered that he was not wearing fall protection during the incident.

During a routine tree trimming task, an employee wrapped the descending line around a sturdy branch to prepare to come down. However, the branch broke, causing the employee to fall 40 feet to the ground. The employee sustained serious injuries including a fractured pelvis, broken vertebrae, fractured rib, collapsed lung, and a broken elbow, and was hospitalized for treatment.

An employee was trimming willow stock to specific size. The employee was cutting with a pneumatic cutters. His finger was caught by the cutters and his fingertip was amputated. The employee was not hospitalized.
An employee was trouble shooting a float on a vaporizer tank. The auto igniter activated which ignited propane vapor causing burns to the lower legs and torso of the employee.

The employee was troubleshooting equipment at a waste management facility when his hand got caught in the broken guard of the electric motor. This resulted in serious injury, requiring hospitalization and treatment. The incident highlighted the importance of equipment maintenance and safety measures in the workplace.
An employee was trouble shooting power outlets that were not working in a classroom. The employee died after electrocution when checking the main conduit feeding the outlets.

The employee was troubleshooting an end former machine without lockout/tagout procedures in place. While trying to figure out why a part was getting stuck, the machine's cylinder cycled and amputated the tip of the employee's pinky finger. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injury.

During troubleshooting of a 480v switch gear, an employee used a screwdriver inside the energized equipment. The screwdriver caused a short between the bus bar and the frame, resulting in an arc flash. The employee suffered burns to his face and hands and was hospitalized as a result of the incident.

During troubleshooting a crimping machine malfunction, an employee's right index finger was amputated when it was unintentionally placed too close to the machine. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injury.

During troubleshooting of a Delta wood planer, the employee removed the guards and accidentally placed their hand on the motor, making contact with the planer knife while it was running. The employee suffered the amputation of five fingers on their right hand as a result of the incident.

The employee was conducting maintenance on a hotel air conditioning and heating unit without following proper lockout/tag out procedures. As a result, he received a fatal electrical shock from the system while using unsafe tools. The shock ultimately led to the employee's death, impacting his liver and lungs.

During troubleshooting of termination machine 4-2, an employee's right hand index finger was partially amputated when it got caught between the bottom nest and the terminal block during a machine cycle. The employee was taken to Elmhurst Memorial Hospital Emergency Room for treatment and hospitalization.

An employee was trying to fix a paper jam in a machine, following proper safety procedures. However, when he used his hand to separate stuck parts, the force caused two fingers on his right hand to be amputated.

While troubleshooting an automated blow molding machine, an employee's right hand was crushed and his ring finger amputated when it became caught in the moving parts of the machine. The employee was using hand tools to make adjustments with the safety door sensor bypassed and receiving assistance from the machine operator. The operator shut down the machine immediately after the incident occurred.

During troubleshooting of an energized electrical circuit, an employee received a shock and fell from a ladder, resulting in a fractured eye socket, lacerations, broken vertebra, broken back, and a broken wrist. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.

While troubleshooting an inoperable taxiway edge light assembly at Westchester County Airport, an employee was electrocuted with approximately 5,000 volts AC while disconnecting the assembly with the electrical system still energized. The employee tragically lost their life during the testing process.

While exiting the bot charging station on level 4, an employee's hand got caught between the structure and the multilevel vehicle conveyor (MVC) that was in operation. The employee suffered fractured fingers on his right hand and a laceration on his right arm during the incident.

An employee was troubleshooting light fixtures in the pool deck adjacent to the recreational and spa building. Maintenance activities were performed without deenergizing the equipment. The employee was electrocuted when making contact with exposed live wires.
An employee was troubleshooting some electrical issues with the animatronics equipment and fell into it. The employee was electrocuted and killed on-site.

During the troubleshooting of a North-South Sheeter Machine, an employee's right hand was amputated when it came in contact with the drive gears due to a misalignment of cutters. The incident occurred while the employee was visually inspecting the cutters and inadvertently placed their hand in the small gap between the frame top and the overhead enclosure.

An employee was troubleshooting the new Hamer mulch packaging line with the guards off. The employee reached into the running machine to pull out a stuck bag of mulch and his finger was pulled in between the rollers of the machine. The employee amputated the tip of their left index finger.

An employee was troubleshooting the switch operation of a piece of equipment. As the employee observed the operation of the switch, two of his fingers became caught in equipment's electric motor belt and both were amputated.
An employee was trying to access the roof of a vacant building to take asbestos samples.  The employee fell from the ladder to the ground, and was killed by head trauma.

The employee incorrectly added horizontal bracing instead of the required vertical bracing under the floor, attaching a U channel to the floor purlins from a step ladder. The floor was switched from wood to concrete without updating the prints, which called for a wood floor. The floor purlins were installed on 16 inch centers instead of the specified 12 inch centers. The collapse of the steel floor and concrete resulted in the employee being crushed and killed.

An employee was trying to climb down a Werner D162X aluminum ladder from the roof.  The employee and ladder fell 9 feet onto the metal flatbed of a truck, striking his head on the truck's bed. The employee was killed.
An employee was trying to correct a product on the line and the tire exploded. The impact of the explosion pushed the employee to the floor, hitting his head. The employee was killed.

The employee attempted to dislodge a chainsaw from a tree branch by jumping onto it, disconnecting his safety rope in the process. When the branch failed to break off completely, the employee turned to reposition himself but was struck by the branch, causing him to lose balance and fall 40 feet to the ground. The employee sustained fatal injuries to his head, extremities, organs, and spinal cord from the fall.

An employee was trying to find the source of face water seepage in a trench. The face of the excavation partially collapsed knocking the employee down and trapping him. The employee suffered multiple fractures to lower left leg and was hospitalized.

The employee was attempting to repair a cement saw on a truck by changing the fuse on the generator. When trying to change the fuse, the employee's arm accidentally came into contact with the leads on the generator, resulting in a fatal electrical shock. The employee tragically lost their life during the incident.

An employee was trying to light the burner on the fire pit. The excess gas built up in the pit and the igniters lit the gas. The employee suffered third degree burns to the left arm and first degree burns to the face for which he was hospitalized.

An employee was searching for two manholes on site to verify their installation, as they were sometimes covered up by landscaping. After finding one manhole, the employee used a shovel to open the lid and look inside with a flashlight. While trying to determine the position of the next manhole, the employee lost consciousness and fell into a 24-foot deep manhole. The cause of the employee's death is pending investigation by the medical examiner.
An employee was trying to pull a laundry bin cart back in the parking lot after loading a few tree branches onto it. The employee collapsed to the ground and was killed by a heart attack.

An employee attempting to stabilize a load of freight inside a trailer climbed on top of the load and instructed a coworker to move it while they were on top. The employee fell approximately 5 feet onto the trailer floor, sustaining several fractured ribs. Despite being hospitalized, the employee passed away several days later due to complications from their injuries.
An employee was injured when a tie-down strap snapped while trying to tow equipment, causing the metal hook to strike them in the head. The employee was hospitalized as a result of the incident.

An employee was turning a master valve on a gas wellhead when it exploded and threw the employee a distance away.  The employees pants caught on fire during the wellhead explosion and suffered third degree burns to both legs. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.

During the process of unclogging a jam on a conveyor belt, an employee was struck by the rotating spindle head of a boring machine while performing housekeeping tasks on an FIDIA GTF 40 machine. The employee sustained a laceration to their right shoulder as a result of the incident.

The employee was attempting to start the vehicle by hitting the starter solenoid with a metal file while under the truck. When the vehicle started unexpectedly, it was in gear and crushed the employee's neck and head, resulting in their death from head and neck trauma. Tragically, the incident proved fatal for the employee.

An employee was underneath an elevated forklift.  The chain sling being used with the overhead gantry crane failed at the coupling link and the forklift fell on the employee. The employee's upper body was crushed and the employee was killed.

An employee was unhooking a load by removing the sling from the wood piling. As the employee released the sling from the load, the hook swung a few feet and struck his hard hat. The employee received head injuries and was killed.
An employee was unhooking a water hose from the milling machine. The Employee was crushed between water truck and milling machine when the water truck moved forward and the employee was killed.
An employee was unjamming a machine, fell from the machine, and struck elbow and head against the floor. The employee sustained blunt force trauma to the elbow and head and died.

An employee was unjamming blockage in a grain chute leading to an elevator leg.  The employee somehow entered the grain chute leading to the elevator leg and slid head first down the chute into the operating leg.  The operating elevator leg buckets struck employee in the head and decapitated him.

An employee was unjamming boards on the band saw conveyor. The employee removed a guard on the ventilation duct and reached in to remove sawdust from the ventilation port and contacted the moving band saw. The employee sustained lacerations to his left forefinger and ring finger.
An employee was unjamming plastic in a grinder by wiggling the grinder blades manually.  The grinder unjammed and the employee's middle, ring, and pinky finger on left hand were amputated.

An employee was unloading 5 gallon paint buckets from a basket that was boomed up to the fifth level balcony via a JCB rough terrain forklift.  The employee fell 50 feet and struck his head on the ground when the elevated work platform he was working on became unstable and rotated.

During unloading operations, an employee was fatally injured when a powered industrial truck he was operating rolled forward, pinning him between a mini-dumpster and a trash compactor. The inadequate functioning of the parking brake led to the tragic accident, resulting in the employee sustaining fatal abdominal injuries.

An employee was unloading a customer order from an elevated height.  The employee fell and suffered a contusion to their head and fractured their right hip. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.
An employee was unloading a feed truck at a hog lot while standing on a ladder.   The employee fell and hit the left side of their head on the back end of the trailer, killing the employee.

An employee at a mechanic's shop was unloading a semi-truck trailer using a powered industrial truck when he noticed an object in his way. As he got off the forklift to move it, he became pinned between the forklift and the trailer, resulting in crushing injuries that tragically led to his death.
An employee was unloading a rail car of fertilizer. He entered one of the unloading compartments to break up clumped material and was engulfed. The employee was asphyxiated and was killed.

During the unloading of a rail car, an employee noticed a buildup of urea product underneath one of the cars. While attempting to break up the material with his right leg, the employee slipped and his foot and leg became trapped in the auger guard, resulting in amputation.

An employee was unloading a stamped part from press.  The employee's right pinky finger was caught between coil steel and edge of stamping die. As the employee was removing the finished part from the machine press which was locked, the employee's pinky finger was amputated. amputated.

An employee was unloading a truck on the general merchandise docks.  The employee complained of chest pains, then sat down on the floor. An EMS was called.  The employee told the EMS he had a previous heart attack and that he had taken his prescribed glycerin pill.

An employee was unloading a vehicle from the over the cab platform. The employee was fatally crushed between the winch cable and the flatbed when the free wheel was activated and the Honda Accord rolled off the top platform on to the drive way.

An employee unloading automobiles from a car hauler trailer fell approximately 8 feet off the side of the trailer, landing on the pavement. The employee suffered multiple injuries including a fractured foot and left shoulder, damaged tendons in the left knee, dislocated left shoulder, and possible neck injury. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.

The employee was tragically killed while unloading cases of diesel exhaust fluid from a pallet into a van, as the forklift he was operating rolled forward and pinned him between the forklift and the van. The forklift had been parked on the sidewalk perpendicular to the van at the time of the incident.

An employee was unloading drill rods from a Ditch Witch drilling machine when their right hand got caught between the metal rod and a metal side of the machine, resulting in a serious injury. The employee was rushed to the hospital and required hospitalization for treatment.

While unloading frozen buns from a semi-trailer at a fast food restaurant, an employee was found unresponsive by their co-driver. The employee was transferred to a trauma center via medical helicopter after sustaining injuries to the head, eye, and ear. The injuries included hemorrhaging and a fracture to the skull.

An employee fell approximately 11.5 feet from a self-loading Knuckle boom while unloading logs from a logging truck. The employee was not wearing a seatbelt and possibly hit the logs on the way down, resulting in fractured ribs and a sore wrist.

An employee unloading porcelain slabs from a forklift at a loading dock with a coworker suffered a fractured leg when five slabs weighing 388 lbs each fell on him. Emergency personnel were called and the employee was hospitalized and treated at Regional Medical Center of San Jose.

An employee was unloading salt wastewater from the oil fields.  After unloading the truck, the employee went to use the bathroom located next to the hooking valves for unloading.  The bathroom caught fire and the employee was killed from after-burns to 90 percent of his body.
An employee was unloading some material when he was struck by a cherry picker and fractured his foot.  The employee was hospitalized and treated for fractured foot.

An employee was unloading steel pipes from a trailer flatbed platform.  The employee fell from the flatbed trailer and injured their head on ground surface.  The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.

An employee was unloading sulfuric acid from a truck into a customer's tank. The hose connection came loose on the truck and sulfuric acid spilled onto the employee. The employee sustained chemical burns, primarily to the forearms.

An employee was unstopping a sewer line.  The employee climbed an 8 foot ladder to access a crawl space in the ceiling that was 11 feet from the ground.  The employee fell from the crawl space and hit the wall before landing on the floor.  The employee died from brain swelling while in a coma.

While unloading a trailer of steel pipes at a road construction site in Minnetonka, an employee was fatally crushed when one of the pipes fell off the trailer. The load consisted of 18 pipes, each weighing 2,500 lbs, stacked in three rows. The employee released the last strap holding the load, causing the accident. Tragically, the employee succumbed to chest and head injuries at a nearby hospital.

An employee was untarping the tractor trailer. Someone driving another vehicle backed into the employee pinning him between both vehicles. A coworker called emergency medical services and they arrived and the employee was declared deceased on scene.

An employee was untying tarp straps on a 57 foot by 54 foot by 14 foot stack of hay. During movement of the tarp the hay stack shifted, causing bales of hay to fall onto the employee. The employee was killed from blunt force trauma to head and body.
An employee was urinating in a bath tub. The employee then sustained a heart attack. The employee suffered from cardiovascular disease and a ruptured aortic dissection.

An employee fell off the east edge of a 4-story commercial roof while using a 100 foot measuring tape to measure the area for the installation of Photovoltaic panels. The roof was equipped with a 1-foot parapet and the fall was approximately 44 feet above the ground level. Tragically, the employee was killed in the incident.

During the transfer of steel sheets using a magnet with a hook lifting device, one of the sheets measuring 18 inches by 18 inches fell onto the air wand being used to blow compressed air. This caused the employee's right index finger to be crushed, leading to a partial amputation.

An employee using a 1964 F750 truck and a 1965 Bronco 85 Elbow aerial lift to remove shrubs was catapulted into the air after wrapping a nylon strap around a shrub and attempting to pull it from the ground. The employee landed on the concrete road, was unresponsive when EMS arrived, and was pronounced deceased after being transported to the local hospital.

During the process of using a 3 foot air wand to clean a steel beam emerging from a shot blasting machine, an employee accidentally placed his hand on the roller bed. This resulted in the employee's right middle finger being amputated at the tip, while the index finger sustained abrasions.

An employee using a hoist to lift a Ford F-250 truck to change the front axle springs was pinned and crushed when the chain holding the vehicle broke. The employee did not remove the tires to access the springs and was working over the passenger's side spring when the accident occurred. As a result, the employee tragically died from asphyxia under the weight of the truck.

The employee was using a 7" mud box while on an 18' ladder to apply joint compound to drywall at a height of 14'. He fell from the ladder approximately 10' to the floor below, landing on the mud box and striking his head. The employee suffered severe head trauma and tragically lost his life in the incident.

During a woodworking task, an employee's right hand accidentally came into contact with a bandsaw blade, resulting in a severe cut at the knuckle where the pinky finger joins the hand. The employee had to be hospitalized for treatment following the incident.
An employee was using a bandsaw to cut meat, and the tip of his left thumb contacted the saw blade, amputating his thumb. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.

An employee was using a battery operated drill to drill a hole on a wooden joist about 109 inches above the floor. The employee's right hand slipped from a drill grip, and the tip of his right hand glove got caught in the drill head. The entanglement caused amputation of the right ring finger.

An employee was using a blue cart to move donations up a ramp and into the warehouse for sorting.  The environmental conditions at the workplace included high temperatures.  The employee was killed by cardiac arrest.

An employee was using a brake press to crimp a bar of metal to be applied to the end of a print blanket (cloth-like material used in printing operations). During operation of the press, one of his fingers was crushed, resulting in its amputation.

An employee was using a brake press to form small metal parts. During operation, the employee's left middle finger was crushed between the material being formed and the front of the ram. His finger was amputated and he was hospitalized for treatment.

During the operation of moving bundled rebar with a bridge crane, the soft steel wire used to suspend the load failed, causing the bundle to disengage and strike an employee. The employee suffered a compound fracture to his lower left leg as a result of the incident. Moving forward, it is important to use appropriate lifting devices and ensure the safety of all employees during material handling operations.

An employee was sweeping the floor of a warehouse aisle marked by shelving units when they were struck by a forklift retrieving a product. The employee suffered a shoulder injury and had to undergo surgery after being hospitalized.
An employee was using a bucket truck to take down a tree limb. The tree limb fell the wrong way and struck the employee. The employee was killed.

While operating a Built-rite SCP HP firewood processor, an employee got trapped in the rotating infeed roller while working near the rear infeed roller and log transfer deck. The worker sustained fatal injuries as a result of the incident.

During a tree-cutting operation, an employee using a chainsaw sustained a deep cut to his leg when the chainsaw kicked back while attempting to cut a stump. The injury resulted in damage to a tendon, surrounding muscles, and bone. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.

During tree cutting operation, an employee was struck and killed by a tree top that was catapulted 50 feet into the air after coming into contact with a power line. The employee was using a chainsaw to cut the tree, which had fallen on top of the power line. The treetop snapped while being cut, causing the tragic accident.

An employee cutting down trees on a bluff with a chainsaw had a tree become stuck in another tree. While attempting to cut down the second tree to free the first, the employee was struck by the falling tree, causing them to fall from the bluff and land on their back on a tree below, ultimately resulting in their death.
An employee was using a chainsaw to limb the tops of felled trees.The employee was struck and killed by a tree limb. The employee was struck and killed by a tree limb.limb.

During use of a chop saw to cut lumber blocks, an employee accidentally activated the saw's foot pedal while reaching for a scrap piece. This resulted in the amputation of the employee's right middle finger when the saw blade contacted his hand.
An employee was using a concrete saw to cut cement to install underground pipes.  The employee was killed from carbon monoxide poisoning.

An employee was using a crane to haul a wire rope. During transport, the chain that was taking the weight of the crane cable loosened. The cable slid down and became entangled with one of the employee's thumbs.  His thumb was amputated, which he was hospitalized and received treatment.

The employee was using a drill press to drill holes in copper tubing for air conditioning units when her glove got caught in the machine. Her hand became pinned between the drill's housing, resulting in the amputation of her pinky and index fingers, as well as lacerations on her middle finger.

An employee was using a drill press. During operation of the equipment, one of the employee's gloves became caught in the press, causing the drill bit to contact his hand.  The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for injuries to his hand.
An employee was using a fixed, scissors-type platform to unload a truck.  The employee fell off the platform to the surface of the parking lot, suffered head trauma and was killed.

An employee operating a forklift in a baler room raised the forks approximately 12 feet while in motion, causing the forklift to become unstable. The employee fell and struck his head on the cement floor, resulting in a concussion and skull fracture. He was hospitalized for treatment.

A tragic incident occurred when an employee was crushed by falling gypsum board while using a forklift to stack them in a warehouse. The employee had built a single stack of 12 lifts of sheetrock and was attempting to build a second stack when several lifts from the first stack fell onto the forklift cab, crushing the overhead guard and fatally injuring the employee.

An employee was using a forklift truck to unload a metal ramp from a flatbed truck and the forklift truck turned over, pinning the employee under the counterweight. The employee was hospitalized and died two weeks later on June 11, 2016. He received serious crushing injuries to the pelvic area.

During metal cutting with a hand grinder, a bucket of magnesium chips caught fire from a spark and the employee carrying it outside sustained burns to his head and hands, necessitating hospitalization.
An employee operating a high lift fork truck in a warehouse freezer had their foot crushed in a collision with another fork truck. They were hospitalized and received treatment for their injuries.

The employee was using a Hobart Corporation meat cutting saw to slice boneless beef when his right hand struck the blade during the last cut. This resulted in the amputation of his right index finger and severe laceration to his right middle finger. The model number of the saw involved in the incident is 5614 and the serial number is 27-1073-431.

An employee was using a Hobart meat grinder machine to cut spare ribs. As he fed a portion of spare ribs into the grinder, the employee's right middle finger contacted the blade amputating the finger. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injury.

The employee was using a Hobart tenderizer machine to shred crab meat when her right hand got caught in the machine, causing severe lacerations and fractures to her fingers. Despite the presence of a guard, the rotating knives pulled her glove into the machine, resulting in the injury.

An employee was using a Hobart Vertical bandsaw to cut thin portions of steak.  During cutting, a portion of bone became caught and the employees left hand contacted the saw blade. The employee was hospitalized, were he was treated for an amputated left middle finger.
An employee was using a hoist to move equipment. During lifting of loose materials, a steel beam struck the employee in the head. He was hospitalized and treated for a head injury.

During the use of a Hologic table saw, an employee's glove touched the saw blade, resulting in his hand being pulled into the machine and one of his fingers being amputated. Investigation later found that the blade guard was not adjusted correctly, leading to the accident.
An employee was using a jackhammer inside a disconnected and removed asphalt silo. A large piece of asphalt fell from above the employee. The employee was struck by falling asphalt and killed.

An employee was injured while attempting to deliver a bucket of contact cement to coworkers working on a roof. While ascending a ladder to access the roof, he lost his balance and fell, resulting in a fractured tailbone. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.

An employee fell from a ladder while trying to access an exhaust fan, hitting his head on a metal brace. He suffered a concussion, laceration to the head, and fractured ribs, requiring hospitalization and treatment.

An employee was using a leaf blower while walking on the roof without fall protection to clean debris from a gutter. The employee slipped and fell off the roof, fracturing his forearm, skull, and facial bones.

An employee was using a Lincoln Electric Power MIG welding machine on an empty 55 gallon drum when an explosion occurred. The employee's left ear drum ruptured and he received second degree burns to the left side of his neck.
An employee was using a meat band saw to slice meat when his right hand slipped and contacted the blade. He amputated his right index finger, which he was hospitalized and treated for.

An employee was using a mini excavator to remove shale material from a hill side. The excavator slid off of the ledge and rolled down the hill side. The employee was not wearing a seat belt at the time of the accident. The employee sustained massive head and chest trauma.

An employee was using a miter saw to cut a wood skid to a length of 24 inches. During operation, one of the employee's gloves contacted the saw blade and was pulled into the saw. One of his fingers on that hand was amputated.

An employee was using a mounted under-the-table top router to cut pieces of wood and caught the tip of her finger with the router bit.  The employee amputated the tip of her finger and was hospitalized.

An employee was using a mounted under-the-table top router to cut pieces of wood and caught the tip of her finger with the router bit.  The employee amputated the tip of her finger and was hospitalized.

An employee was using a Nuclear Moisture Density Machine to test asphalt when worker operating a Case PT240 roller struck and ran over the employee, crushing his leg and pelvis. The employee was killed.

During a wood cutting task, an employee was injured when the panel saw kicked back and contacted his abdomen. This was due to a loose hold down on the table not securing the wood properly. The employee required hospitalization and treatment for his injury.

An employee was using a Patty-O-Matic patty forming machine.  The employee bypassed guard where patties come out and his finger was caught in the machine.  The employee partially amputated the tip of their right middle finger. The employee was not hospitalized.

An employee was using a Pem machine to insert a pem.  The employee activated the machine while their thumb was below the ram.  The employee amputated their thumb when cut by the Pem machine ram. The employee was not hospitalized.

During a woodworking task, an employee's fingers came into contact with a planer blade, resulting in the amputation of his right middle finger and lacerations to his index and ring fingers. The employee required hospitalization and treatment for his injuries.
An employee was using a platform scaffold to install roof sheeting operations when he fell and fractured his hip. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.

An employee was using a pneumatic nail gun to perform sheathing work on the east facing exterior of the residential building from a portable extension ladder.  The employee fell and landed on some water pipes approximately 12 feet when the ladder collapsed.
An employee was using a power stocker lift to stock merchandise.  The employee fell from the lift and was killed.

An employee was using a press brake to bend a 12 guage aluminum sheet. While the press was in the intermediate position, the employee's right thumb became caught in the press clamp and his thumb was amputated.

An employee using a pressure washer to sanitize a conveyor system had their arm pulled into the machinery when the spray wand became stuck between the sprocket and belt of the conveyor. The employee suffered a severe injury, with the skin on their arm being removed. They were promptly taken to a nearby hospital for treatment.
An employee was using a propane torch to heat the core of a precast tank. During heating a fire occurred. The employee sustained second and third degree burns from the fire.
An employee was using a pulley to direct the fall of a tree. He was in the danger zone and was struck by a tree as it fell.  The employee was killed.

An employee was cleaning the leveler rollers on a Duece Press with a rag when their arm was accidentally pulled into the rollers. The rag got caught, resulting in the employee suffering a degloving injury from shoulder to elbow. The employee was immediately hospitalized and received treatment for their severe injuries.

An employee was testing a truck after replacing the hydraulic tank using a remote control. While walking around the vehicle, a Linde forklift unloading paver products accidentally ran over the employee's left foot, causing a broken pinky toe.

During a metal cutting operation, an employee's hand accidentally came into contact with the press clamp of the shear machine, resulting in the crushing of his fingers despite the presence of a guard. As a result, the employee had to undergo amputation of the second and third digits of his fingers.

An employee was using a shop-vac to remove caustic liquid spillage from one machine to dump in a retention pit. The chemical sodium hydroxide "lye" spilled on the employee causing chemical burns to his left leg. The employee was not wearing PPE.

An employee was using a spatula to break up dried Tetrazene that was lying inside the vacuum receiver. The employee was standing over the vacuum receiver when the Tetrazene exploded, killing the employee.

During a routine task of loading materials onto a truck using a stand-up forklift, an employee encountered a malfunction with the controls of the vehicle. Unable to slow down or stop the forklift, the employee attempted to use his foot to halt the vehicle, resulting in a serious injury with multiple broken toes on his left foot. The employee was taken to the hospital for treatment and evaluation following the incident.

An employee was using a table saw for crosscutting wood for making a tool.  The employee removed a scrap of wood without turning the table saw off and the employee's finger was caught by the saw blade.  The employee partially amputated a finger and was hospitalized.

An employee was using a table saw to cut a piece of wood when his left hand came into contact with the blade. He sustained a laceration to his left hand, which he was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury. The incident investigation revealed that the saw guard was not in place.

An employee was using a table saw to cut pieces of metal. As he cut a portion of the metal, the saw kicked back, sending the metal back towards the employee's right hand. The employee sustained partial amputations of his right index finger and thumb.

The employee was using a tape measure inside of an unprotected excavation when it collapsed, striking him in the midsection and burying him. The impact of the falling earth crushed his internal organs, including rupturing his aorta, causing severe internal bleeding and ultimately resulting in his death.
During pipe cutting with a torch cutter, sparks ignited an employee's sweatshirt, causing burns on his back and neck. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.

During a task of cutting off steel bolt heads, an employee using a torch fueled with oxygen and acetylene accidentally caused a fire when opening the oxygen hose. The flames spread to the employee's clothing, causing burns to the left side of his chest and stomach. The employee was hospitalized for treatment of his injuries. A subsequent investigation determined that a leak in the oxygen hose was a contributing factor to the incident.

An employee was using a tube cutter to cut a piece of silicone tubing. As the employee measured the tubing, she inadvertently depressed the machine's foot pedal, activating the machine. Her right index finger was contacted by the blade, amputating her fingertip.

An employee using a vacuum lifting device to lift stone slabs from a machine table had their finger pinched between the machine table when the device came loose. The employee suffered a distal pad amputation of their right middle finger without bone loss, but did not require hospitalization.

The employee was using a vehicle mounted bucket lift to remove a gas pump topper when his neck became caught between the bucket edge and the canopy above. Despite efforts to lower the bucket using controls, the employee was unable to free himself and tragically died of asphyxiation.

An employee was using a vertical band saw to cut meat. As the employee placed his finger under the meat to move it towards the blade, the tip of his right ring finger contacted the blade and was amputated.

While cutting pork chops with a vertical bandsaw, an employee removed the manufacturer-supplied pusher plate and set the saw to a cutting thickness of 0.04 inches. As she was cutting the final piece of meat, the pork bone got caught in the blade, pulling her left hand into the saw and resulting in the tip of her left middle finger being severed. The incident investigation showed that the pusher plate should have been used, especially when cutting at thicknesses less than 2 inches.

The employee was using a Wander Disc Grinder to remove burrs from a piece of steel when the steel slipped and the employee's left thumb came into contact with the abrasive surface of the grinder. As a result, the thumb was fractured, disjointed at the knuckle, and de-sleeved.

An employee was washing excess concrete off the street using a water hose that was connected to a concrete truck. Witnesses saw him fall to his knees and then collapse with his eyes rolling back into his head. Emergency medical services were called, but the employee tragically died, possibly due to a heart attack.

The employee was using a Webb mill to fly cut a part and left the machine running as he briefly walked away. Upon returning, his left glove came into contact with the rotating drill bit, resulting in the amputation of the tip of his index finger.
An employee was using an 8-foot ladder to change air filters. The employee fell 8 feet from the ladder onto the floor and was killed.

During an attempt to haul equipment down a steep slope with an agricultural tractor, the transmission failed, causing the tractor to accelerate uncontrollably. The employee operating the tractor was unable to stop it, leading to the tractor flipping over along with the equipment being hauled. The employee sustained serious crushing injuries to his left arm and had to be hospitalized.
An employee was using an air compressor, when the air compressor exploded. The employee was killed in the explosion.

While cleaning a press trimmer with an air wand, an employee noticed a piece of veneer stuck in the dust collection collar. In an attempt to remove the piece, the employee reached into the area while the trimmer blade was still operating, resulting in a severe injury. The employee suffered an amputation to the right middle finger and an avulsion to the pointer finger.

An employee was using an alligator shear to cut a wire, when his right index finger was pinched. Contact with the alligator shear resulted in the finger being amputated. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment.

A worker using a rivet buster to chip concrete from a column on a scissor lift got their hand caught between the machine and the guardrail when the tool malfunctioned while trying to dislodge it from steel rebar. The worker suffered an avulsion injury to their right ring finger and required hospitalization for treatment.

An employee using an Apollo radial arm saw to cut lumber had his right hand accidentally come into contact with the still-spinning blade while attempting to remove accumulated scrap wood. As a result, his right thumb, index, and middle fingers were cut down to the tendon. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.

An employee was wrapping a wooden pallet of floor tiles with an automatic shrink wrap machine when he stood too close to the rotating table. The pallet struck his right shin, resulting in a fractured bone and ultimately causing his death.

An employee was using an electric Skil Saw and was cutting a 23 foot wide by 41 foot long wooden roof eave.  The employee completed cutting the roof section and fell off a 6 foot step ladder, hitting their head on the ground and is killed.

An employee became stuck in an elevator while traveling from the fifth to the seventh floor of a building. The elevator suddenly dropped from the sixth floor to the second floor without stopping in between. The employee was hospitalized for seven days for treatment of knee tremors, general weakness, and disorientation.

The employee was using an impact wrench when two welded studs broke, causing a 3,000 pound part to fall on top of them while they were working underneath it. The part was upside down and supported only by the two butt welded bolts at the time of the accident. Tragically, the employee was crushed and killed in the incident.

During the operation of an overhead crane to manipulate a metal invar, the hook attached to the invar detached causing it to strike the employee's upper left arm. This resulted in a broken humorous bone for the employee, who was hospitalized for treatment.

During a routine task of moving metal plates with an overhead crane, an employee was struck by the load when the plates slipped out of the lifting device. The impact resulted in the employee sustaining multiple injuries, including a broken right forearm and several lacerations to both arms.
