The accident occurred when an employee was using an oxygen-acetylene cutting torch to remove a boom support stand from a truck-mounted hole digger. The employee's head became trapped between the boom and the truck's headache rack, resulting in fatal head trauma. The boom was not properly secured before cutting, leading to the tragic incident.

An employee was using axle die cutting machine while talking to his supervisor and shop foreman. The employees fifth index finger on his right hand was smashed while using Axle die cutting machine. The employees pinky finger was amputated but he was not hospitalized.

An employee was using high pressure water hose to excavate dirt. The left foot of the operator of the high pressure water vac truck slipped into the water stream and this caused an amputation of the employee's left foot middle toe.

During the process of using a chainsaw to cut down a tree, an employee was hit on the head by a falling dead branch while standing about 15 feet away from the tree stump. The employee suffered fatal head injuries as a result of the incident.

An employee was removing fish parts from a fillet machine using his hands without following lockout/tagout procedures. The machine's filet knife cut the employee's right middle finger, resulting in hospitalization and treatment for his injury.
An employee was using his hands to separate aluminum bars, when his left middle finger became caught between the bars. His finger was amputated, which he was hospitalized and received treatment.

An employee was using machinery to install headers on pipes. For an unknown reason, the employee placed his hand in the opening of the pipe, resulting in his right hand being caught by the rotor of the machinery.  One of his fingers on his right hand was amputated, which he was hospitalized for.

During a routine operation to coat a roll of sheet aluminum, an employee's right arm became caught between the structural steel of the machinery and a roller carriage, resulting in a fractured right humerus. The incident occurred while the employee and coworkers were attempting to fix a lost tail of the coil. The roller was sent upward due to a loss of air pressure in the tower, leading to the injury.

An employee was using saddle strap for trimming branches of a tree.The tree split causing it to pull the employee into the tree trunk.  The employee was crushed by the weight of the tree and was killed.

An employee was working with shovels to remove soil and rock for plumbing installation in a building. The employee reported feeling unwell and overheated after 1.5 hours of work and went to his car to cool down. Tragically, the employee succumbed to heat stress and died.
An employee was using the counter top cutter. The employee was crushed on chest between the machine moving part and the wall. The employee was killed.
An employee was vacuuming and breaking up some tetrazine.  The employee was killed when an explosion occurred that blew out the frangible wall and damaged equipment within the room.

An employee with a prior breathing condition was vacuuming inside a residence when she began experiencing trouble breathing. Despite using her inhaler, the employee's condition did not improve. Simultaneously, the owner of the residence required physical restraint and was taken to an urgent care clinic for treatment. The owner was later admitted and treated for asthma exacerbated by possible exposure to pesticide.

While visually inspecting a gauge of a diaphragm pump behind a powder coating booth, an employee was struck in the left eye by a loose return hose of the pump, causing a severe laceration. The incident occurred as the pump was moving recycled powder from the booth to a fluidized bed. It was noted that the employee was wearing safety glasses during the inspection.
An employee was visually inspecting a vehicle in the company parking lot.  The employee displayed symptoms consistent with those of a stroke.  The employee died from a suspected stroke.

An employee slipped on the floor while inspecting a printing press and accidentally put his hand in between two operational rubber rollers. He activated the kill switch on another press to stop it and emergency services were called to the scene. The injured employee was transported to Memorial Hospital in Rock Springs, WY and later transferred to U of UT Hospital in SLC, UT for treatment of a crushing hand injury with skin damage.

The employee was waiting for a sensor fault on the A900 robotic cell to be cleared, but decided to enter the cell with seven robots present to attempt to fix the issue herself. Unfortunately, one of the robots became activated and caught the employee from behind, crushing her ribs and shoving her into a jig, resulting in her death.

The employee was found dead on the floor of a scissor lift while waiting for the superintendent to begin installing pipe hanging for natural gas. Despite efforts to revive the employee, they were pronounced dead at the scene due to a heart attack. Emergency Medical Services were called to the site in response to the incident.

An employee was waiting on the ground level for a coworker to lower a couch over a second story balcony railing. The employee was struck by the falling couch. The employee sustained a fractured arm and leg and a bruised knee.
An employee was walking a log on a vessel. He stumbled and fell into an open hatch. The employee fracture his neck and died a few days later.
The employee was walking across a driveway being paved when a dump truck backed up over him, resulting in multiple fractures and major trauma that ultimately proved fatal.
An employee was walking across a tarmac. The employee was struck by a top loader and was crushed by the material handling equipment.

The employee was walking across a concrete floor when he stepped on a plywood covering an opening to a basement stairway. The fiberboard sheet was not secure, causing the employee and a section of fiberboard to fall through the opening into the basement. The employee suffered from multiple blunt force trauma to the head and tragically was killed as a result of the incident.

An employee was walking across the floor. The employees foot got caught in a hole in the floor and he tripped and fell onto his shoulder on the concrete flooring. He suffered from broken bone in shoulder. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.
An employee was walking across the substructure, fell to the ground, and was killed.

An employee was walking across the yard after a safety meeting.  The employees right knee collapsed and the employee fell, striking his head into the pavement.  The employee suffered neck injuries and was hospitalized, where he passed away on April 21, 2017.
An employee was walking along a bridge and was struck by passing motorist and killed.

An employee was walking along a row of grapes that he had finished picking and was counting the number of trays he had placed on the ground to  record them for payment. As he was walking along the row he collapsed. The employee died of an apparent heart attack.

An employee was walking along side a Ranco Bottom dump trailer at the dump gate controls. The employee was run over by the back left trailer wheels and was killed. The employee's lower body to middle of shoulder blades was crushed.

An employee was walking along side the paver. A truck delivering asphalt bumped the employee on his back causing him to fall against the paver.  The paver pulled him under the machine and  he was killed.

The incident involved an employee inventorying materials while walking along a steel channel at floor level. The employee suddenly twisted, breaking his right leg femur and falling to the floor, resulting in serious injuries. Despite undergoing surgery, the employee passed away shortly after due to prior medical conditions including kidney and bone cancer.

During a routine task of guiding copper pipes with a forklift, an employee's foot was crushed when the forklift driver accidentally ran over it after a brief stop. The employee sustained multiple fractures and ripped flesh, requiring hospitalization and treatment.
An employee was walking along the side of a truck carrying trash.  The employee was struck by a passing truck, and died.
An employee was walking and experienced a heart attack.
An employee was walking and was crushed by a tractor harvest machine.
An employee was walking and was struck by a standup truck. The employee suffered a fractured right ankle.

An employee was walking around the 1st floor level.  In the dark unfinished stair tower, the employee walked off of the concrete landing into the lower level basement. The employee received severe head trauma resulting in death.
An employee was walking away from a coworker and fell through a floor opening.  The employee suffered several fractured ribs and shoulder.

An employee was walking backward toward the edge of a roof, to place a roofing materials in place. The employee tripped and fell over the edge of roof. The employee fell 16 feet to the paved ground level below and was killed.
An employee was walking behind a moving payloader.  The employee was struck by the payloader and the employee was killed.
An employee was walking down a dirt road. He was struck by a loader and subsequently caught under its front tire, which fractured his skull. The employee was killed.
An employee was walking down a ramp leading from the building. The employee tripped and fell. She suffered a bruise on her forehead. The employee did not use the handrail when she tripped and fell.

The employee was struck in the head by a piece of metal ejected from an exploding Baldor motor being troubleshot by a contractor. The motor over revved, causing the motor shiv to explode and the motor to violently come apart. The employee suffered a severe skull fracture and was killed in the incident.

An employee was walking down an interior hall near the restrooms.While walking down the hall, the employee tripped on the carpet rubber commercial rug mat and fell, fracturing his right hip. The injury required surgery and the employee died from surgical complications.

An employee was walking down steps from the parking lot to the Leggett Special Events Center. The employee was descending the steps when he fell from the last step striking his head on the concrete. The employee suffered from head trauma and was killed.

An employee was walking down the hallway from his office to get some cleaning supplies from a storage room. The employee apparently collapsed and a coworker found him laying on the floor. The employee was taken to the hospital still faintly breathing and he died at the hospital.

An employee walking from a parked tractor trailer to the office was struck by a driver from another trucking company. The driver was unaware he had hit the employee until police found evidence under his trailer. The incident had no witnesses.
An employee was walking from the electric shop when he was struck and run over by a Dodge pick-up truck that a coworker was driving.  The employee was killed.
An employee was walking from the employee parking lot to the office building and was struck by a company bus driven by a coworker. The employee sustained brain injuries and the employee was killed.

An employee was walking from the facility to his vehicle parked in the facility parking lot.  As he passed a delivery truck, he somehow was caught under the rear tires and was run over.  The employee suffered contusions, bleeding, and fatal internal injuries.

An employee was walking from the meat cooler to the meat department carrying a bag containing three chickens.  The employee lost his footing, slipped, and fell to the floor, hitting his back and shoulders first and then the back of his head.  The employee died later from head impact trauma.

While walking from the restaurant dining area to the kitchen, an employee tripped on a rolled-up carpet in the vestibule, resulting in a broken orbital lobe and laceration to the right eye. Sadly, 48 hours later, she collapsed at home and passed away after undergoing an emergency craniotomy for bleeding on the brain. The kitchen vestibule had a ceramic floor.

An employee was walking from where he had been finishing concrete to his personal vehicle, talking on a mobile phone. He passed behind a Komatsu Loader (Model W320-7) as it was backing up and was run over. The employee died approximately 4 hours later while undergoing surgery.

An employee was walking in a parking lot to locate an empty trailer when he was struck by a truck. The employee was pinned between the truck and a trailer, sustaining fractures to his chest and face. He was hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.
An employee was walking in an aisle of the shoe department and tripped over a carton of shoes.  The employee fractured their femur when they fell to the floor.

An employee was walking in an area where forklifts were operating, when he was struck by a forklift. The employee sustained fractures to both his feet, which he was hospitalized and received treatment.
An employee was walking in front of a co-worker. The employee got hit by a 12-foot fiber glass stepladder. He suffered head injuries for which he was hospitalized.

During a work incident, an employee was walking in front of a GEHL rough terrain forklift to stabilize a piece of equipment being carried on the forks by a sling and shackles. Unfortunately, the employee tripped and fell, resulting in the forklift rolling onto his leg and hips. The employee sustained fractures to his foot, leg, both hips, and pelvis and had to be hospitalized for treatment.

An employee was walking in the break down lane of a road behind a bucket truck with a cable reel when the truck over took the employee, striking the employee in the back and head, knocking the employee to the ground, and running over the employee. The employee was killed.
An employee was walking in the parking lot and was struck by a pickup truck. The employee was killed from a head injury and bruised leg.

An employee was walking into a facility when he was hit by a forklift.  The employee was admitted to the hospital for 4 days and released.  While at home, the employee was not feeling well and returned to the hospital where he passed away from a blood clot. a blood clot.

An employee was killed when a rough terrain forklift backed over him while he was looking at his phone in the yard. The forklift operator had the boom up, reverse alarm activated, and was looking back while reversing, but did not see the employee behind him. Despite the loud reverse alarm, the accident resulted in the tragic death of the employee.

An employee was walking near a dock when he was struck by a forklift that was driving in reverse out of a trailer. The employee sustained a broken leg, which he was hospitalized and underwent surgery.

An employee was walking next to his tow truck along the shoulder towards a disabled vehicle to load it on his tow truck. The employee was struck by a minivan, suffered crushing injuries, and had one of their legs amputated when struck.  The employee was killed.

An employee was walking North on the Route 7 south break down lane. As the employee was walking, a Bucket Truck backed into and over the employee.  The employee received injuries to his back and head. The employee was killed.

During a routine inspection, an employee fell and fractured his right leg while walking on a metal platform. The accident occurred when he turned around near a step down and lost his balance. He was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.

An employee was walking on a structural I-beam at an asphalt company.  The employee was attempting to clear a jam from a recycle material chute when he fell approximately 17 feet to the ground, resulting in a fractured skull and broken leg.  He died later from his injuries.

An employee was walking on ice to the edge of open water during an ice water training class. The employee fell into the open water when the ice gave way, fracturing her right ankle. The employee was not hospitalized.

An employee was walking on purlins of a roof, lacing insulation, when a portion of the 2 inch by 4 inch purlin broke. The employee fell to the ground and fractured his neck. He was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.
An employee was walking on the curb and fell.  The employee fractured his knee as a result from the fall. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.
An employee was walking on the decking when air compressor became unattached from a crane and fell on the employee. The employee killed sustained blunt force trauma to the head.

An employee was walking on the dirt trail with a measuring tape and shovel.   A piece of heavy equipment KOMATSU WA320-7 was carrying a 60 inch pipe that struck the employee in the head, and than ran over him.  The employee was killed.
An employee was walking on the roof moving a temporary portable power distribution system. The employee fell 40 feet throughan unprotected skylight and was killed.
An employee was walking on the sales floor main aisle/walkway going back to the break room.  The employee slipped and fell on laminated floor tiles. The employee received a broken left femur.

An employee was walking on the second floor of an apartment building under construction, when he fell through an opening and was killed. The incident investigation revealed that the opening was intended for installation of a garbage chute.

The employee was fatally struck and run over by a refrigerated box truck as she walked in front of it while it was backing up. The driver of the truck stated that he felt a bump and discovered he had backed over the employee when he got out to investigate. The employee was pronounced dead at the scene by emergency officials.

An employee was walking outside from one building to another to pick up materials. The weather was dark, rainy, and windy. A forklift operator was driving between buildings to pick up materials when he struck the employee. The employee was killed.
An employee was walking through a parking lot and was struck by a vehicle. The employee was killed.

An employee was walking through a work area. The employee lost his balance and rolled right ankle over, falling and tearing his achilles tendon in his right foot. The employee later died from a blood clot.

The incident involved an employee who was walking through their work area and suddenly received an electric shock, rendering them unconscious. Despite not touching any equipment at the time, the employee was incapacitated. Coworkers who responded did not witness anything unusual, and the investigation was unable to determine the cause of the shock.

An employee was walking through the plant when he was struck by a Kawasaki front end loader.	The employee suffered multiple fractures to his lower extremities, damage to internal organs, and he was hospitalized.

An employee was walking through the surgical patient recovery area after checking on a patient. The employee stepped on her scrub pant's leg resulting in her falling onto the floor. She sustained a fractured left femur.

An employee was walking throughout the scrap yard talking with coworkers.The employee was struck by attachment on the boom of a track hoe (Deere 330LC excavator).The employee was killed from his injuries. (Deere 330LC excavator).The employee was killed from his injuries.injuries.
An employee was walking to car in parking garage, when he slipped on wet paint and struck his head. The employee was hospitalized and treated for a head injury.

An employee was walking to her car while on a work break. As she crossed the facilities parking lot, she was struck by a car. She sustained contusions and bruises to her torso and back, which she was hospitalized and received treatment.

The employee was fatally struck by a tractor trailer at the marine terminal while crossing in front of it. The employee was not wearing reflective clothing at the time of the incident. The truck driver, who was entering the terminal, was self-employed.
An employee was walking to his work area in a shipyard.  The employee slipped and fell, fracturing his right ankle for which he was hospitalized.

The employee was checking on the Lincoln Windrow elevator machine when he noticed the wing gate had closed. As he tried to open it, his leg got caught in the elevator, resulting in the amputation of his right leg and ultimately leading to his death.

An employee was walking to the clinic parking lot.  The employee tripped and fell over a parking block.  The employee suffered multiple injuries that included a fractured left arm, fractured nose, and bruised right arm. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.

An employee was preparing to apply waterproofing on a sixth floor balcony where a scaffold system was set up. The employee fell approximately 54 feet to the ground level when he stepped on planks that were not securely in place, resulting in fatal injuries.
An employee was walking to the worksite from the parking area, collapsed, and suffered a heart attack.
An employee was walking toward her vehicle. The employee tripped on the section of raised concrete in the walkway. 	She fractured her left leg femur for which she was hospitalized.
An employee was walking towards or away from a truck.  The employee collapsed from a heart attack.  Emergency services responded but the employee could not be revived.

While attempting to investigate a machine shut down, an employee's left foot fell through a dislodged drain cover and slipped into a U-channel transporting boiling water/steam at 250 degrees. The employee suffered second degree burns to their foot and ankle, requiring a skin graft.

The employee collapsed and was unresponsive after leaning against a guard rail near repair line 2. Despite efforts from coworkers and a police officer performing CPR, the employee was declared deceased at the hospital due to a heart attack.
An employee was walking towards the yard office.  The employee was struck and killed by a jockey truck.
An employee was walking towards truck yard office. The employee was struck by a truck driver. The employee suffered multiple trauma to the body and was killed.
An employee was walking under a tanker truck. The employee was struck by the tanker truck and the employee suffered from broken hip and pelvis and was killed.

An employee was walking up a hill on a private road to check the facility grounds.  The employee slipped and fell on black ice, fracturing his femur.  The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.

An employee was walking up exterior steps of a building, carrying plans for a new project.  Upon reaching the top of the steps, the employee reached for the door handle, but fell backwards instead. He fell, received head trauma, and was killed.

The employee was walking up the stairs to the second floor when they suddenly passed out and fell down a flight of stairs. As a result, the employee suffered severe injuries including abrasions to the head, fractured ribs, sternum, and subgaleal hemorrhage. Tragically, the employee later died due to the injuries sustained in the fall.

During a routine maintenance task to repair water valves, an employee slipped off a narrow retaining wall and fell 10 feet to the ground below. The fall resulted in a broken hip that required surgery. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for their injuries.
An employee was was guarding and patrolling a new home under construction. The employee traveled into the home and on the way out, slipped and fell down stairs and injured his hip.

An employee was washing brick and lowering a EZ scaffold. The end guardrail became dislodged and the employee started to grab the flag shaped guardrail. The employee, tripped and fell off of the scaffold. The employee was killed from spinal and internal injuries.

An employee was washing the siding of a building. The left wooden pump jack pole, constructed of 2 by 4's, collapsed/snapped at one of the joints causing the employee to fall from the scaffold plank on to a paved driveway. The employee sustained fractured skull and was killed.

An employee was injured when a forklift driver accidentally pinned them against a pickup truck while loading materials. The employee sustained injuries to their pelvis and ribs and was taken to the hospital for treatment. The incident occurred as the forklift operator was backing away from the truck after loading materials onto it.

An employee was overseeing the placement of propane tanks on a flatbed trailer using a truck mounted crane. While unhooking the rigging from the tanks, a mishap occurred causing the tanks to fall off the trailer. The employee was struck by one of the tanks, resulting in their death after being taken to the hospital.
An employee was waterproofing a wall with Tyvek home wrap plastic sheeting.  The employee fell 6 feet onto a concrete walkway and fractured their skull.

An employee performing traffic control attempted to stop a semi-truck from hitting a low power line by waving a flashlight. Unfortunately, a vehicle traveling in the opposite direction struck the employee, resulting in his death from severe injuries including leg amputation, multiple fractures, and head trauma.

An employee fell from a 60 to 65-foot mast while waxing a sailboat on the upper dock area. They hit their face on the lower dock surface before rolling into the water and drowning. Responders found the employee floating face down in the water.

While weeding a grape vineyard field, an employee suddenly collapsed about 150 feet into the field. Despite immediate efforts by coworkers to transport the employee to a hospital ten minutes away, they were pronounced dead at 11:27 a.m. due to cardiac arrest.
An employee was weeding along a highway, when an automobile left the highway and traveled through the grassy area, striking the employee. The employee was killed.
An employee was weeding an asparagus field using a long handled hoe.  The employee ran 48 feet, collapsed to his knees, and fell to the ground.  The employee suffered from cardiomyopathy.

An employee was weeding and shoveling. While working in the field, he lost feeling in his right arm and left leg. His jaw twisted to the side when he felt dizzy and confused. He suffered from an apparent heat stroke and died.
An employee was weeding in a tobacco field with a hoe.  The employee was overcome by heat, and died from hyperthermia.
An employee was welding a bracket on top of a chemical tank used to store sodium hydrosulfide solution. The tank exploded. The employee was chemically burned and killed.

An employee was welding an overhead structure   from a scissor lift platform, at the height of approximately 18 feet. When the employee moved the platform, his head became caught between the scissor lift railing and the structure. The employee was killed when his head and face were crushed.
An employee was welding in the alkylation "alky" unit at petrochemical refinery.  An Isobutane fire occurred resulting in burns.

An employee was finishing up welding support brackets to an aluminum module when he made contact with an energized conductor while rolling back his MIG welding systems. The contact resulted in the employee being electrocuted.

A tragic incident occurred when an employee was struck by a bundle of fencing material that slid off a flatbed trailer while another coworker was offloading bundles of fencing pipes with a forklift. The injured employee suffered several fractures and unfortunately succumbed to his injuries. The employee's death was a devastating loss for the company and his colleagues.

During winterization of a Volvo L70G front end loader, an employee replaced factory hydraulic hoses with winter grade ones. However, they removed too many hoses, causing the mast to lose hydraulic pressure and collapse on top of the employee. Tragically, the employee was killed when impaled through the lower abdomen by the front end loader.

An employee was wiping and cleaning the machine. The employee entered the back of the machine while the machine was powered on and got caught by the turret arm of the CNC Lathe machine. The employee was pinned, crushed and killed inside machine.

During a routine pipe wiping procedure in the oil and gas industry, a pipe string suddenly broke below the hole and violently whipped upward, striking an employee on the right side of his head. The force of the impact was fatal, resulting in the tragic death of the employee.

An employee was wiring switches (no power) to a tool fixture.When the employee stood up, he struck his head on the cross bar of a metal fixture.  The employee apparently died from a heart attack. ar of a metal fixture.  The employee apparently died from a heart attack.a heart attack.

An employee in a Latin grocery store was assisting customers in the meat department when his middle finger on his right hand was amputated by a meat band saw while cutting meat. The investigation showed that proper guarding was not in place.

An employee was working alone testing chemicals in the laboratory.  The employee was standing between two load bars when the automatic crane moved, crushing him between the load bar and a crane hook. The crane moved products to the different dip tanks in an anodizing line. The employee was killed.
An employee was working alone to repair Elevator #17.  The elevator carriage crushed the employee.

An employee working alone at a woodshop mezzanine was lowering boards without fall protection, resulting in a fall through an unprotected opening. The employee sustained lacerations, a hematoma, and contusions, requiring hospitalization for two days. The task of receiving and cutting materials at the mezzanine edge was performed intermittently.

While working alone on a residential lot clearing debris from a hurricane, an employee was cutting down a dead pine tree when the top portion unexpectedly fell onto him, resulting in fatal injuries including blunt force trauma to various parts of his body and multiple fractures.
An employee was working an elevated surface and was cleaning some scrap metal from an unguarded edge.  The employee fell approximately 18 feet and was killed.
An employee was working as a cashier at a food mart and was shot during a robbery. The robber shot thru a bullet proof glass killing the employee.
An employee was working as a cashier. Three armed robbers came into the store, threw a bag at the cashier, and told him to get the money.  The employee was shot moments later by one of the robbers.

The employee, working as a firefighter and EMT, was in the passenger seat of an ambulance responding to a call when it collided with a backhoe owned by another town. The ambulance struck the backhoe's boom, bucket arm, and bucket in the eastbound lane of the road. The employee sustained severe trauma to multiple body parts and tragically lost his life in the incident.
An employee was working as a flagger as part of a road construction crew.  The employee was struck by and killed by a passing motorist who did not follow the employee's directions.
An employee was working as a flagger on the west end of a road project.  The employee was struck by and killed by a vehicle driven by an individual who was under the influence of illegal substances.

An employee was working as a garbage worker and walked to some trash cans that were standing behind a garbage truck.  The employee was struck by the garbage truck and crushed under the rear tires as it was driven while in reverse.  The employee was killed.

A residential spray foam insulation employee complained of stomach pain and went home early from work on Thursday March 17, 2016. The employee called in sick the next day and was later found to have passed away in the Intensive Care Unit on Sunday March 20, 2016. The coroner determined that the employee died from blunt force trauma to the abdomen, likely sustained from a fall from an extension ladder erected on a mobile scaffold platform.

While working as a laborer at a berry farm, an employee pruning blackberries under plastic canopies became dizzy and disoriented after eight hours of work. He collapsed and lost consciousness, leading coworkers to provide first aid and call emergency medical services. Paramedics arrived within eight minutes of the call, but sadly, the employee was declared dead at 3:32 p.m. The cause is suspected to be heat stroke, although it has not been confirmed.

During logging operations, an employee was struck and killed by a 22.6-meter-long log that rolled down the mountain after being unhooked near the landing chute along with another log. Despite one log being secured by a coworker, the loose log tragically hit the employee, who was working as a logger, while he was choking logs at the bottom of the mountain.

A loss prevention officer at a Georgia store confronted a customer who was attempting to leave without paying for three boxed television sets. The customer did not have a receipt and when asked to follow back into the store, he turned around and shot the employee in the torso, ultimately killing him.

During a routine maintenance task of changing light bulbs in the facility, an employee fell 12 to 14 feet to the ground while standing on a wooden job built scaffold work platform placed on the forks of a forklift. The employee suffered fractured wrists and bruised ribs, requiring a 3-day hospital stay for treatment.

An employee working as part of the grounds crew fell off a 32-foot extension ladder while carrying beverages to roofers and struck his head on the concrete below. Tragically, the employee was killed in the fall.

An employee operating a frontend loader while plowing snow in a commercial parking lot experienced mechanical problems with his machine. After completing work, he collapsed while walking to his pick-up truck, and was later found under the frontend loader by a passerby. Despite medical intervention, the employee tragically passed away in the hospital due to internal abdominal bleeding. The exact cause of death was pending toxicology report results.
An employee was working as a security guard at the facility. Two armed persons entered the facility and shot the employee to death.

A state trooper participating in a physical training test for a position on the Vermont State Police tactical service unit collapsed and died during the evaluation process. He was completing a grueling course that included various physical activities. Despite efforts to revive him, he was pronounced dead at the hospital, with the cause of death being exertional heat stroke.

A stevedoring outfit employee working as a supervisor was fatally injured when a bale of recycled cardboard, weighing approximately 454 kilograms, fell on him during a loading operation. Despite being rushed to the hospital, the employee succumbed to his injuries. The incident occurred when the forklift operator lost control of the load, leading to the tragic accident.

An employee working as a table game dealer complained of shortness of breath while dealing blackjack at Pit Number 9. Despite having a history of asthma, the situation worsened during transportation to the hospital, and he became unresponsive. Efforts to revive him at the hospital were unsuccessful, and he tragically passed away.
An employee was working as a teacher in the 2 year old classroom, when a child bumped into the back of her legs. The employee fell striking her arm, back, and head on the ground, killing her.

The employee was found unconscious with his head inside the manhole of a separator tank while gauging the depth level. Despite emergency services responding promptly, the employee was pronounced dead at a local funeral home. This incident highlights the dangers of working in the oil and gas industry and the importance of following safety protocols.
An employee was working as a window washer for a janitorial service. He was washing windows, when he fell from a 10-story building and he was killed.

The employee was working underneath a truck, removing bolts holding the transmission in place without a jack to support it. When the transmission was unbolted, it fell onto the employee, causing a head contusion and ultimately leading to his death.

While moving temporary road signage, an employee fell out of the back of a truck after being struck by a fabric sign due to strong winds. Unfortunately, the employee suffered fatal injuries from the fall onto the pavement, resulting in head, face, neck, and body trauma.

An employee was tragically killed while operating a Yanmar Ex3200 compact tractor with a belly mower and front end loader on a slope between 27.5-30 degrees. The tractor began to slide and flipped multiple times, ejecting the employee who was not wearing the seatbelt or using the roll over protection structure. The tractor was operating beyond its recommended capabilities and did not have rear ballast as outlined in the operator's manual.

During a road construction project, an employee complained of not feeling well while working with a paving crew. He was told to sit in an air conditioned truck, but was later found unresponsive when the crew returned. Emergency services were called and the employee was rushed to the hospital, where he passed away 17 days later.

An employee was working as part of a road crew to remove a mudslide from a closed highway.  The employee was struck by a 2000 Freightline 3-axle dump truck while it was backing up and the employee was killed.

While cleaning roof gutters at a residential dwelling, an employee fell approximately 10 feet from an A-frame ladder and was taken to the hospital. despite medical efforts, the employee tragically passed away three days later.

An employee was working as part of an electrical team installing electrical wiring for the operation of a tower crane.  The employee was struck in the back by a large retaining pin that weighed approximately 40 pounds, when it fell from the top of the crane, killing him.

During a hot air balloon landing, an employee working as the ground crew held on to the basket after passengers exited. The balloon unexpectedly lifted off, causing the employee to fall approximately 100 feet as he lost his grip. Sadly, the employee succumbed to multiple traumas from the fall.

While working as a maintenance supervisor at a resort, an employee was assisting a tree service company in unloading logs from a dump truck. A log being dumped bounced on the pavement and struck his left leg, causing a fractured left tibia and fibula. The employee was hospitalized for treatment after the incident.

An employee working as a roofing contractor fell approximately 2.4 to 2.7 meters onto a back stair landing after stepping on rotted wood at the edge of a roof. He sustained a facial fracture upon landing and was treated and released following the incident.

The plant manager of a chemical wholesaler arrived at the facility and was informed that an empty container was being filled with the wrong chemical. When he went to investigate, the container exploded, causing severe injuries that resulted in the amputation of his right arm and leg. The container had been filled with a deadly mixture of sulfuric acid and bleach.

The employee was working at a 80 ton press when a piece of material became jammed. Despite the press being shut off, the feeder continued to feed material, causing the employee's right index finger to become caught and resulting in the amputation of his first knuckle.

An employee working in a lemon orchard with his wife and coworkers suddenly fell unconscious after complaining of chest pain and tightness. Despite efforts from his son and paramedics, the employee tragically passed away at the scene. The cause of death remained unknown during the investigation, although the hot and humid weather conditions were noted.

An employee was working at a commercial construction site, installing a HVAC unit. In the process of moving material to the roof with the use of an aerial lift, the employee made contact with an overhead power line and the employee was killed.

An employee working on the construction site of a four-story building fell approximately 20 feet to the level below while looking for a brace to install plumbing in a column on the third floor. The employee sustained fractures to his pelvis, lower back, and left wrist, resulting in hospitalization and surgery. The incident investigation revealed that the employee fell through a sheet of plywood covering an opening intended for a stairway shaft, where a support had been removed and shifted before the employee's fall.

An employee was working at a construction site when the hydraulic system of a Bobcat Skid Loader failed.  The employee had his arm trapped between the bucket arms and the body of the Bobcat when it fell on top of him. The employee was killed from his injuries.

An employee at a construction site was preparing to install sheeting on a building's roof when a piece of plywood he stepped on gave way. This caused him to fall 19 feet through the roof's trusses, resulting in a fatal head injury. The incident investigation concluded that his death was a result of the fall.

The employee working at a facility fabricating metal tanks fell approximately 1.5 meters to a concrete floor while checking the quality of a storage tank dome. His head struck the concrete floor, resulting in a concussion. Despite being hospitalized, he ultimately passed away due to his injury.

The employee was struck in the head by a falling drill while working at an underground wet utilities facility. Despite wearing a hardhat, he suffered a serious head injury and had to be hospitalized for treatment. The incident occurred as he was observing a coworker performing grade checks at the base of a building.

During routine work on an aerosol machine assembly, an employee's finger was amputated when it became caught between the conveyor and running turntable. The incident occurred because there was no safety guard installed to prevent such accidents. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for her injuries.

An employee working at a farm in Mabton, WA was found dead in a shed or garage where he had been painting a car without proper ventilation or a respirator. Despite showing no signs of illness earlier in the day, the worker had some underlying medical issues. The county sheriff reported the employee's death.

An employee operating a standup forklift at a commercial building collided with a stationary forklift, resulting in a serious foot injury. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment. Investigation showed that the employee was not wearing steel-toe shoes, which could have prevented the injury.

The employee working at the gas station tripped over a curb while walking to assist a customer at a fuel pump, falling and striking the customer's vehicle. He suffered a broken hip and required emergency surgery for treatment, resulting in hospitalization.

While working at a golf course, an employee retrieved the mail from the facility mailbox using a golf cart. Upon returning to the office parking lot, the employee backed the golf cart into a designated spot and accidentally trapped his left foot between the vehicle and a cement curb. This resulted in multiple lacerations to his left heel.

An employee at a hospital specializing in treating mentally ill individuals with criminal backgrounds was injured while part of a team administering calming medication to an agitated patient. The employee was struck in the face by the patient, resulting in an orbital fracture to his left eye and other injuries. He was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.

An employee was working at a hydroelectric dam that was owned by an electric power authority. He was performing routine maintenance on a main lead and switch gear. The equipment was energized at 13.8 kilovolts (kV). For an unstated reason, he was electrocuted.

An employee was working at a jobsite. The employee pried free an air lift (jack) from underneath the ICC bar of a 40 foot container chassis and the jack toppled over onto his leg. The employee was transported to a medical facility and treated for a fractured leg.

During a shift at a lumber plant, an employee was tasked with spraying a smoldering retort tank with water from a catwalk. The combination of cedar dust, cedar oils, and water caused an explosion, leading to a fire. Tragically, the worker fell from the catwalk and succumbed to their injuries after hitting the concrete floor below, resulting in their untimely death.

An employee at a manufacturing facility operating a vacuum thermo-forming machine was injured when his head was pinned between the machine's platen and frame while trying to remove a hose. A coworker came to his aid and emergency services were contacted. The employee underwent surgery for injuries including a lower jaw fracture, lacerations, and the loss of four teeth. Investigation revealed insufficient training on machine safety.

While working at a manufacturing plant over the weekend, an employee accidentally stepped onto a steel beam, resulting in a fall. The fall caused the employee to roll through an opening under a conveyor and fall an additional 14 feet to the concrete floor, leading to serious injuries including fractured ribs and vertebrae, bleeding on the brain, and a collapsed lung. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for the injuries.

While starting his shift at a municipal waste water treatment plant, an employee fell into the RAS well after foam overflowed through the grates. Efforts to reposition the grating were unsuccessful and the employee either stepped on an unsecured grate or fell through unstable grating, leading to the fatal incident.

An employee was working at a natural gas pipeline. As he opened one of the valves on the pipeline, a fire occurred. The employee sustained multiple burns, which he was hospitalized and received treatment.

The employee at a pulp and paper mill was killed when the railcar she was riding on collided with an awning at the warehouse entrance. She jumped off to avoid being hit by the falling awning, but rolled under the car and was fatally severed. Tragically, the accident resulted in her death.

An employee slipped and fell at a retail store while on break at a restaurant. The employee hit her head on a metal fire gate and suffered internal bleeding injuries. She was hospitalized for treatment.

An employee was working at a thrift store. She had just assisted a customer by bringing in donations and putting them in the storage area. She was shot by a former employee who used to work at the site. She sustained a gunshot wound to the chest and was killed.

During work at a vehicle repair shop, an employee tripped over a metal plate in service bay #12 while a coworker was servicing a vehicle transmission in bay #11. The employee fell onto the concrete floor, resulting in multiple fractures to their right leg.

An employee at a vehicle repair shop fell while descending a ladder with a steel wheel, hitting his head on the shop floor. He was hospitalized and treated for head trauma resulting in brain swelling.
An employee was working at a vineyard. He drowned in a pond on the property. The cause of his death was asphyxiation due to drowning.
An employee was working at a window of a fast food drive through. As the employee was assisting a customer to get change from the store manager, she fainted.

The employee was working alone on 3rd shift at a rafter mill when they suffered a fatal heart attack. A coworker returning from break found the unresponsive employee on the floor near the workstation. The coroner's report confirmed the employee's death was due to natural causes.

While working at an auto repair shop, an employee was conducting an oil change on a Nissan Altima when the vehicle fell forward while being lifted by a Challenger Lift. The employee sustained multiple fractures and a cut under his eye, but was rescued by coworkers who lifted the vehicle off of him. An investigation revealed that the front right lift arm had failed, causing the accident.
An employee was working at his desk and was found unresponsive by a coworker.  Emergency Services were contacted and transported the employee to Kings County Hospital where he died.

An employee was changing a light bulb on a step ladder when he lost his balance and fell, rupturing his patella tendon. He underwent surgery to repair the tendon but died from complications a few weeks later. There were no witnesses to the incident and weather was not a factor.

An employee was working behind a sushi counter. The employee got into an argument with a customer and grabbed a sushi knife and attacked the patron, who sustained serious laceration injuries. The customer grabbed the knife and stabbed the employee. The employee was killed.

The employee of a beer and ale distributor was tragically killed after being pinned against a dumpster by a van in a parking lot. The employee may have been attempting to signal the driver to back up to a loading ramp when the van unexpectedly moved forward, resulting in the fatal accident.

An employee was working for a big box retailer. As she was conducting inventory, she tripped over some clothes that she had put on the floor. She bruised her hip on the floor. Later that evening she went to the hospital and she died.

The employee was operating a batch mixer for a commercial playground contractor when he lost control of the arm while dumping a mixture of rubber compound. The arm struck him in the neck, causing a fracture. He was hospitalized but tragically passed away from his injuries.
An employee was working for a drywall and insulation contractor. He was replacing foam barrels and he was exposed to carbon monoxide gas. The employee was overcome by the gas and he was hospitalized.

An employee working for a drywall and insulation contractor fell from the third floor of a three-story building while trying to retrieve his tools. The employee slipped on debris near a wall opening and fell 19 feet onto a retaining wall. He sustained multiple injuries, including a fractured rib, bruises to his back, side, and arm. He was hospitalized as a result of the incident.
An employee was working for a finish carpentry contractor. He was installing metal decking. He fell and fractured his wrists. and he was hospitalized.

During a woodworking project, an employee using a table saw with a dado blade installed experienced a kickback which caused his left hand to strike the saw blade. This resulted in the amputation of part of his middle finger and required hospitalization.

An employee was working for a finish carpentry contractor. He was using a table saw to cut material. Some of his fingers were amputated as he was operating the table saw. He was hospitalized for his injuries.

An employee was working for a firm engaged in air-conditioning and warm air heating equipment and commercial and industrial refrigeration equipment manufacturing. He was eating lunch, when he sustained a heart attack and he died.

While working at a construction site with a pre-cut mezzanine section, an employee failed to connect his harness to fall protection equipment before removing guardrail components. When he stepped onto the pre-cut section, it collapsed, causing him to fall 3 meters and sustain a fractured hip and elbow. He was hospitalized as a result of the incident.

An employee was working for a firm engaged in commercial and institutional building construction. He was installing a metal deck, when he fell from height. He sustained fractured bones, and he was hospitalized.

An employee working on a construction site fell off a rolling scaffold while plastering a wall and became entangled with overhead wires. As a result, he sustained head trauma and had to be hospitalized for his injuries.

An employee working for a construction firm fell 2.3 meters after a scaffold plank broke while he was preparing to cut steel with a plasma cutter. He sustained a fractured ankle and was hospitalized for two or more days.

A union labor apprentice working on a commercial and residential construction site was injured when he was impaled by a jet lock while stripping plywood from the ceiling of an underground concrete parking garage. The employee sustained fractured ribs and a punctured lung as a result of the incident. The employer reported the incident to DOSH, which conducted an investigation and issued no citations.

While working on a construction project involving the welding of a steel plate, an employee was fatally injured when the plate fell on him. The employee had placed welding leads over the top of the plate, which caused it to become dislodged and fall. The heavy steel plate struck the employee, resulting in severe head trauma and likely broken bones. The incident occurred as the plate was being prepared for welding and was not supported or secured against falling.

While testing the well level using an EKO gun at a crude petroleum and natural gas extraction firm, an employee accidentally caused a ball valve to split open, spraying dangerous gases like hydrogen sulfide and methane onto him. The employee was hospitalized after being overcome by the gases, but fortunately was not suffocated.

The employee was working in an unprotected trench shoveling dirt around a gas main pipe when a partial cave-in occurred, resulting in him being struck by concrete and asphalt. He sustained a fractured left ankle and had to be hospitalized for his injuries.

An employee was working for a firm engaged in landscaping services. The employee was operating a tractor. He fell off the tractor, and he was run over. He was killed from fractures in the area of his pelvis and his right arm, and internal bleeding.

While transporting a bundle of hatch/cargo straps on a forklift truck at Warehouse 5, an employee's fingers on his right hand got caught in the straps as they slipped into the wheel of the forklift. The incident resulted in cuts and lacerations to three fingers, requiring hospitalization but thankfully not leading to amputation.

An employee working for a construction firm was collecting equipment to be loaded onto the company truck after completing a house construction project. While carrying a 32-foot aluminum ladder towards the truck, the ladder accidentally made contact with an overhead power line carrying 7,200 volts, resulting in the employee being electrocuted.

During the construction of a new single-family housing project, an employee was injured while working on the roof of a two-story residential cabin. While installing fascia board along the edge of the roof, the employee lost his balance and fell approximately 5.5 to 6 meters to the ground. He suffered two broken vertebrae in his back and was hospitalized as a result of the fall.
An employee working on a construction site fell from a roof while clearing ice, resulting in two broken ankles and a broken wrist. He was hospitalized for more than two days as a result of the fall.

The employee was working with a chop saw at a plastics manufacturing firm, cutting plastic pipe when a piece got jammed near the blade. Despite the blade still spinning, he reached in to remove the jam and ended up amputating a finger on his right hand. It was not specified in the report whether he was taken to the hospital for treatment.

An employee was working for a firm engaged in postharvest crop activities. The employee was cleaning under a loading dock area with a handheld broom. He sustained a heart attack while working and he died.

The employee, working for a truckload freight trucking firm, was walking towards his switcher truck in a truck yard when he was struck and dragged by a blue 1999 Freightliner tractor unit. The impact crushed the right side of his chest, resulting in his death.

The employee was tragically killed while working in a nursery and tree production firm when the tractor he was operating went into reverse as he was removing a fertilizer spreader. The back tire of the tractor ran over him, pinning him underneath the front tire. The accident resulted in his death.

While preparing an area for an above-ceiling inspection at a non-residential property, an employee working for electrical contractors came into contact with an energized electric conductor at 277 volts. He suffered an electric shock and was ultimately electrocuted. The incident was documented under inspection identity number 1132635, with three inspection identity numbers overall associated with the incident.

An employee working on troubleshooting a sign in a crawl space above a drive-thru lane for a pharmacy was electrocuted when a coworker in an electrical room inside the store was turning unlabeled breakers on and off to determine the cause of the problem with the sign. The employee came into contact with energized equipment, resulting in the fatal incident.

An employee was working for a firm of farm labor contractors and crew leaders. He was picking up raisin trays from the ground and loading them into fruit bins. He was in a vehicle ready to go home after finishing work, when he fainted. He died in a hospital from a sudden cardiac arrest.

An employee was working for a firm of painting and wall covering contractors. He was painting cabinets in a garage and he was found unresponsive on the ground by the homeowner. He was taken to the hospital, where he died. The medical examiner determined that he had been electrocuted.

While working to disconnect an air duct, an employee in the plumbing, heating, and air conditioning contracting firm was electrocuted after coming into contact with a loose wire from another source. Despite being found unresponsive, there were no witnesses to the incident. The employee went into cardiac arrest as a result of the electrocution.

An employee was working for a firm of plumbing, heating, and air-conditioning contractors. He was installing air conditioning ducts and was working in an attic. The employee was crawling, and he came into contact with an exposed energized wire and he was electrocuted.

An employee at a recyclable material merchant wholesalers firm was using a cutting torch outdoors to cut a truck flatbed into sections at a salvage yard. Despite clear and dry weather conditions, the employee experienced a seizure and fell onto the torch cutter, sustaining third-degree burns to the upper torso. Unfortunately, the employee later passed away due to his injuries. He had extensive experience with torch cutting equipment and had been working at the company for five days prior to the incident.

An employee and coworkers were removing wooden mats at a site where a cellular tower had been dismantled. They were using a boom truck near an overhead power line, which was energized at 13.2 kV. The employee holding the hook on the cable from the boom truck inadvertently made contact with a phase conductor and was electrocuted. His coworker standing nearby was not injured.

An employee of a structural steel and precast concrete firm was unloading a truck with coworkers when he suddenly stumbled and fell, hitting his head on a metal bar. Sadly, he was killed in the accident. It was believed that he may have suffered a heart attack leading to his fall.

An employee was working for a firm that dealt in recyclable materials. He had gone into an air conditioned parked trailer. He was found slumped over at the table. The employee died from a heart attack.

A worker at an oil and gas drilling firm was setting up equipment when a tragic incident occurred. While attempting to secure an A-leg in place, the employee failed to ensure that a pin had a keeper to prevent it from dislodging. As a result, the A-leg fell on the worker, causing fatal injuries to his head and neck.
An employee working in sewer line construction fell into an active sewer line after being overcome by fumes near an open manhole. The preliminary cause of death was determined to be asphyxiation.

The employee of a sign and banner company fell off a ladder while working at a junior college, landing on the concrete floor of an auditorium after going through a drop ceiling. He suffered fatal injuries including fractures to his head and neck, broken ribs, and punctured lungs. Tragically, he did not survive the fall.

An employee was working for a firm that managed a residential property. He was completing a work order for replacing a light bulb, when he fell down some stairs. He struck his head on a concrete step and he was killed.

During work at an aircraft parts manufacturing firm, an employee operating a table saw had a piece of wood kick back and amputate the tip of her index finger on her right hand. She was subsequently hospitalized for her injury.

The employee at a brick and concrete block manufacturing firm was fatally injured while straightening concrete blocks in an overhead side feeder. The machine's hydraulic arm caught him as he leaned into the cuber, crushing his upper torso and causing his death.

An employee was working for a firm that manufactured glass containers. He was walking up some stairs, when he lost consciousness and fell over. It is thought that he sustained a heart attack and he died.

During his shift at a welding and soldering equipment manufacturing firm, an employee's ring finger on his right hand was caught between a flat bar and a cutting machine while he was working on a trailer. The finger was broken and he needed surgery, leading to hospitalization.

An employee was working for a firm that operated retail stores where automotive parts and accessories were sold. He was loading a delivery vehicle, when he slipped on some ice. He fell on his right hip and shoulder, fracturing them. He was hospitalized.

The employee was performing maintenance on the Gondola Car Ride #1 when the car suddenly dropped on top of him, pinning him between the car and the deck. This resulted in traumatic asphyxiation and ultimately led to his death. The incident highlights the importance of proper safety measures and training when working on amusement rides.

While working on site preparations with earthmoving equipment, an employee accidentally disturbed a concrete block housing a swarm of bees. The bees attacked the employee, causing him to go into cardiac arrest from the stings and ultimately resulting in his death.

An employee working for a parking lot and garage firm was instructing a coworker to use an industrial truck or golf cart to empty the trash when the coworker slid over from the passenger seat causing the vehicle to lurch forward. The vehicle struck the employee, knocking him to the ground and causing him to hit his head on the pavement. Sadly, he sustained a fractured skull and was killed as a result of the accident.

The incident involved an employee at a firm supporting well drilling operations who was transferring sand from a rail car to a truck using a conveyor system. While stepping across the moving conveyor belt, the employee was caught in the system and suffered fatal injuries.

During his work at a recycling firm, an employee using a cutting torch inadvertently triggered a bomb hidden within the scrap metal he was working on. The bomb partially exploded, causing severe injuries to the employee including burns, puncture wounds from shrapnel, and a concussion. Tragically, the employee ultimately succumbed to his injuries and was killed in the explosion.

An employee at a recycling facility in southern California was injured while torch-cutting a Hydril pulsation dampener, causing it to explode and catch fire. The employee sustained multiple fractures and lacerations, and was transported to the hospital for treatment. The firm promptly reported the incident to the authorities and an inspection was opened to investigate the safety procedures in place at the facility. The employee noted that the employer failed to ensure that the dampener did not contain hazardous flammable substances or build up pressure

An employee was working for a fuel dealer. He was delivering propane gas to a residence. He was filling a tank, when vapors ignited. He sustained burns to his face, hands, and legs. He was hospitalized.

While troubleshooting a motion sensor at a naval air station in Maryland, an employee working for a government contractor providing power systems accidentally made contact with an energized conductor while standing on a portable stepladder. The employee, who was not wearing the required PPE, was electrocuted by the current, believed to have entered his body through his hands.
An employee was working for a heating and air conditioning contractor. He was assisting a coworker. He came into contact with exposed energized wiring and he was electrocuted.

The employee, who had just finished his landscaping job, was preparing to pick up equipment on a public street when a speeding driver drove into the coned area and struck him. The employee suffered fatal injuries, including blunt force trauma, and the driver fled the scene.

While working for a landscaping service, an employee was part of a crew tasked with felling a tree struck by lightning at a residential jobsite. Despite wearing fall protection equipment and being deemed safe to climb by his employer, the employee fell 9.1 to 12.2 meters (30 to 40 feet) after a tree limb unexpectedly split, resulting in fatal injuries.

The employee of a landscaping service was cutting down a large tree branch that was 10.7 meters above the ground. As the branch fell, it caused the branch above it to give way, pushing the employee away from the tree. He fell to the ground below, sustaining severe back and chest injuries that ultimately resulted in his death.

An employee was working for a landscaping service. He was operating a zero-turn riding lawn mower. The mower struck an object and overturned. When it rolled over, it fell into a river. The employee was pinned under the water and he drowned.
An employee was working for a landscaping service. He was trimming or cutting down trees and he was working in a tree. The tree broke, and the employee fell and he was killed.
An employee was working for a logging firm and he was falling trees. He was struck by a snagged top from an alder tree and  he was killed.

During a routine placement of a precast communication vault into an excavation, an employee working from a crane was thrown from his position when the excavation's wall caved in. The employee fell from a height into the excavation and was tragically struck by precast concrete rings, resulting in his death.

While working for a flooring material manufacturer in Cartersville, GA, an employee was replacing a tension roller on an N1A Nip Assembly machine. He climbed on top of the chilled rollers to remove the dirty roller, handing it to his helper before the machine unexpectedly started. Witnesses heard the employee scream and found him caught between the rollers, resulting in his death from crushing injuries and decapitation. No one witnessed the actual incident unfold.
An employee was working for a manufacturer of glass containers. A bottle fell and hit him on the neck and he sustained a fracture and he died from his injury.

An employee was working for a manufacturer of tires for the automotive industry in Danville, Virginia. He was sleeping between pallets and a wall. A forklift pushed the pallets against the wall. The worker sustained fractures to multiple body parts. He was killed.

During work at a metal wall and roof panel manufacturing company, an employee's left hand got caught in a horizontal pull saw while cutting wood boards for packaging. The employee lost his left thumb and index finger, requiring hospitalization and surgery for reattachment. Investigation showed that the saw was missing a safety guard.
An employee was working for a masonry contractor. He was standing on scaffolding and he jumped from the scaffolding to a roof. He fell, breaking two finger on his left hand and he was hospitalized.

The employee, who worked in the maintenance and transportation division of a municipality government, was tragically run over by a truck near the entrance gate to a facility as he was about to begin his work. He sustained fatal injuries to his legs and head, resulting in his death.

While sealing air ducts to prevent leakage, an employee working for a plumbing, heating, and air conditioning contractor sustained a fatal electric shock. His coworker was preparing to reenergize an air conditioning unit when the incident occurred. Despite being resuscitated at the scene, the employee was hospitalized for thirteen days before tragically passing away without ever regaining consciousness.

The employee, working for a plumbing contractor, was on a fiberglass step ladder applying flux to copper pipes when he possibly suffered a seizure and fell onto a concrete floor. He sustained a fractured jaw and was hospitalized, with no one witnessing the incident.

An employee of a plumbing, heating, and air-conditioning contractor fell off a Werner 6.4-meter ladder while accessing the roof of a strip mall to service a new tenant's HVAC system. He sustained multiple fractures and was hospitalized. The incident was reported by a representative of the firm, who noted that the employee was working alone and refused to be interviewed. The issues raised were related to ladder placement and training.

During his shift at a poultry hatchery, an employee was loading a washing machine onto a pickup truck using a liftgate attachment. While operating the controls, his left index finger got caught in the scissor lift mechanism, resulting in a partial amputation up to the first knuckle. He was immediately taken to the hospital for treatment. The incident was caused by the unguarded pinch point on the lifting mechanism.

An employee at a residential mental health or substance abuse facility was stabbed by a consumer while getting them ready for a morning program. The consumer had threatened to stab the employee if forced to go, and despite the employee's efforts to hide all knives, the consumer found one and carried out the threat. The employee sustained a stab wound to their back, which punctured their lung and resulted in hospitalization for multiple days.

An employee was working for a roofing contractor. He was climbing a ladder. The ladder's feet slipped on ice on the floor, and it fell, taking the employee with it. The employee fell onto the ground and sustained broken ribs. He was hospitalized for his injuries.

An employee was working for a scrap metal recycler. He was cutting a sealed cylinder. The cylinder contained oil. The cylinder and/or its contents caught fire when the metal was breached. The worker sustained burns to body.

An employee was working for a sign company. He was connecting electrical wiring. He came into contact with an energized electrical circuit. The current took a path through his chest and he  was electrocuted.

An employee was working for a site preparation contractor. He was cutting a pipe with a cutting/chop saw. When the cut had been made all the way onto the pipe, the saw blade kicked back. The employee sustained a deep laceration on his right cheek and he was hospitalized for his  injury.
An employee was working for a solid waste collection firm. He was signaling the driver of a vehicle and was struck by that or another vehicle. The employee was crushed. and killed.

An employee working for a structural steel and precast concrete contractor fell approximately 4.3 meters onto a concrete floor while doing ironwork. He sustained a broken shoulder and tailbone and was hospitalized as a result of the fall.

The employee, while operating a Enburo 30 Nissan Model C1 3F 475 forklift at a textile manufacturer, struck a wall while turning the vehicle. The impact caused him to be ejected from the forklift and subsequently pinned between the forklift and the wall. He sustained a broken neck and tragically passed away as a result of the incident.

The employee, working for a towing firm, was removing a split rim wheel from the hub of a towing crane when the tire blew off the rim while still inflated. The tire struck the employee, throwing him into the back of his truck where a tire and tool box were located. The employee sustained blunt force trauma and unfortunately, was killed as a result of the incident.

The employee, a truck driver for a trucking firm serving energy companies in the shale formation, was involved in a fatal rollover accident at the intersection of North Dakota Highway 23 and US Route 85. The tanker truck he was driving rolled over at the ramp and he suffered blunt force trauma to his head and face, resulting in his death. The incident occurred after he had filled the tanker with oil at a well site.
An employee was working for a water supply firm. Soon after arriving at work, the employee committed suicide.

An employee was working for a wired telecommunications carrier. He was installing telephone cable and working from an aerial lift. The employee made contact with an energized overhead power line and he was electrocuted.

While inspecting a vending machine at an amusement arcade, an employee unknowingly came into contact with energized parts due to incorrect wiring. He was electrocuted and killed after being in contact with the parts for approximately 15 minutes. The fire department intervened and unplugged the machine, but it was too late to save the employee.

An employee was working for an auctioneer. He was closing an industrial overhead garage door. The door had no safety recoil devices to prevent crushing injuries.The employee was crushed and killed when the door closed on him. he door closed on him.

An employee of an electric power utility was killed while attempting to free a wooden utility pole that became lodged in the dirt and brush. He was using a peavey tool to rock the pole free while it was still being pulled on by a line truck. The 360-millimeter (14-inch) Lindsey 501-2 pulley being used in the operation launched towards the employee, striking him in the head and causing his death.

An employee working for an oil or gas pipeline construction firm was caught in severe weather conditions. He walked nearly half a mile to reach shelter but upon arrival at a tent, he suffered a heart attack or seizure and died. The exact cause of the incident was not specified in the narrative.

An employee was working for the U.S. Postal Service. She was attempting to scan a bar code inside a trailer. When she stepped on the surface of a loading dock bumper guard, she fell from the dock to the concrete floor. She struck her head and was killed.

During a task involving communication cables above a false ceiling, an employee was working from a step ladder alongside a coworker. The ladder collapsed when the employee turned to the left, causing him to fall to the concrete floor. Despite being treated for injuries including a fractured left tibia and T11 vertebral, as well as a concussion, the employee tragically succumbed to the fall.

An employee working from a 10 foot tall A-frame ladder fell to the concrete while trying to hand a sign to a coworker. The ladder tipped sideways, causing the employee to sustain a fractured left tibia.

During the incident, an employee fell from a 12 foot Werner stepladder while working to fill holes near the top of a rolling door. The employee landed on his right side, sustaining injuries to his neck, shoulder, hip, and lower back. The accident occurred as birds were gaining access to the shop area through the holes.

An employee fell off a 4 foot tall ladder while resetting a door, hitting his head and suffering from strained back and a lacerated elbow. Initially released back to work on light duty, he was later admitted to the hospital over the weekend due to a subdural hematoma and was placed in the intensive care unit.

An employee was electrocuted while changing a recessed light ballast on a 6 foot A frame ladder, causing them to fall to the floor. The employee sustained fatal injuries including a subdural hematoma, right clavicle fracture, and rib fractures.
An employee fell from a 6 foot fiberglass step ladder while installing hurricane clips on a building, sustaining a fractured ankle. He was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.
An employee fell from a 6 foot high step ladder while stocking shelves, resulting in a fracture to his left lower leg. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injury.

An employee was working from a basket 20 feet above the ground to install a screen over a vent pipe. The basket slipped from the forks of the JCB Material Handler, causing the employee to fall and suffer multiple injuries. The basket was not secured to the material handler, leading to the accident.

An employee was working from a creeper under a tractor trailer truck loosening brake shoe adjustments. He was preparing to change brake drums when the tractor trailer truck fell off the jacks, crushing the employee's abdomen.

An employee fell 22 feet while working on a decommissioned large conveyor line with a torch cutter, removing smaller metal conveyors. Witnesses heard a thud and found the employee lying on the concrete floor. Despite being part of regular work duties, the employee ultimately succumbed to the injuries sustained from the fall.

During a tower maintenance project, an employee was working from a forklift man basket to replace worn siding when the basket tipped over, causing the employee to fall 30 feet. The employee suffered multiple fractures to his leg, ankle, and left arm and was hospitalized for treatment.

An employee was injured while working on a ladder to replace a light bulb in the training room. He fell when the wire he was removing from the rigging pulled him off the ladder, resulting in a fractured left ankle. He was hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.
An employee was working from a ladder to inspect a truck when he fell and sustained a fracture. He was hospitalized and treated for his injury.

An employee was working from a ladder to install a light fixture when he received an electric shock and fell. He sustained multiple injuries that included a burned hand, and lower back and right heel fractures, which he was hospitalized for treatment.

During the installation of an elevated walkway, an employee fell from a ladder and suffered a broken wrist, fractured ribs, and a bruised lung. It was discovered during the investigation that the employee's harness was not properly connected to its anchor at the time of the incident. The employee was hospitalized for treatment of his injuries.
An employee was working from a ladder when he fell 3.5 feet. The employee sustained a concussion.

An employee was working from a ladder when he fell. He received multiple fractures to his ribs, head, and vertebrae. The incident investigation determined that the employee had missed a step on the ladder, resulting in the fall.

An employee working from an uninsulated bucket of a truck-mounted aerial lift was electrocuted after something made contact with an overhead power line while pulling telecommunications strand to connect it to a utility pole. The strand was being installed 55 inches below the neutral conductor on the poles and the employee was using a chainsaw to trim trees while installing it. The truck driver stopped the truck when instructed by the employee, but then heard two loud bangs and saw a flash of light as the employee caught fire.
