During a television production set, an employee fell 6 feet into a pit underneath a drawbridge platform while adjusting a lighting fixture. The employee suffered a laceration to the elbow and head injury, requiring hospitalization and treatment.

An employee was working from a scaffold deck to lay bricks. During work, he slid off the outrigger support and fell 41.3 feet. The employee struck the concrete floor below and hit his head on a steel beam and was killed.

The employee was working on a scissor lift when he became pinned between the guardrail and a steel beam, sustaining multiple fractures and a punctured lung. He was discovered by a coworker and hospitalized for treatment.

An employee was working from a ladder with a chainsaw, attempting to cut a hole in the ceiling of a new residential home for a HVAC installation. The employee accidentally cut his jugular vein while working, and despite receiving first aid from coworkers, he was pronounced dead at the hospital after being transported by Emergency Services.

An employee was working from a train cart loaded with rebar. As the employee was unhooking the cart, a bundle of rebar rolled off the cart. He lost his balance and fell, striking his head on a protruding horizontal piece of rebar before falling to the ground.

During routine gutter maintenance on a residential structure, an employee fell from an 8-foot A-frame ladder while descending, hitting his head and back on the ground and losing consciousness. The employee required hospitalization and treatment for his injuries.

An employee was working from an A-fame ladder installing a metal soffit, when the employee lost his balance and fell approximately 8 feet to the ground. The employee was killed from lower back and head injuries.

An experienced school maintenance worker of over 30 years was operating an aerial lift inside the school gym to troubleshoot a malfunctioning curtain motor. The lift, raised to approximately 20 feet high, tipped over causing the employee to fall to the gym floor below, resulting in fatal blunt force trauma to the head.

While pressure washing a residence from an aerial lift, an employee accidentally struck a height level warning sign with the lift's basket as they maneuvered towards the garage, resulting in broken ribs and abrasions to the employee's back. A coworker witnessed the incident, contacted emergency services, and helped release the employee from being pinned between the basket and the sign. The injured employee was then taken to a nearby hospital for treatment.

An employee was removing satellite dishes from a two-story residential building using an aluminum extension ladder. The ladder was resting on the energized electrical power service to the building. The employee was shocked, fell from the ladder, and died after hitting his head on the asphalt driveway below.

An employee was working from an elevated basket that was lifted by the tines of a forklift. As the employee was removing bolts to a door, the basket he was working from fell to the ground. The employee sustained a fractured wrist and multiple lacerations to the side of his body.
An employee was working from an elevated bucket truck. The employee made contact with a 7,200 volts energized power line and was electrocuted and killed.

While working from an elevated location, an employee fell to a concrete slab after a joist he was sitting on gave way. The employee sustained a fractured pelvis and right arm, resulting in hospitalization and treatment.

While working from an elevated platform to fill a nurse tank, an employee accidentally stepped backwards and got his right leg caught in the opening of the running gear step. This caused contusions on his lower leg, ankle, and knee, requiring hospitalization and treatment.

While cleaning the inside of a mixer at a mushroom manufacturing facility, an employee fell from an elevated wood platform that was 39.75 inches above the floor. He struck a step ladder before landing on the floor, resulting in three broken ribs and multiple contusions. The employee was hospitalized for two days for treatment.

An employee was working from an elevated work platform to remove a hydraulic check valve. During removal, the employee fell to a lower level and fractured his right leg, which he was hospitalized and received treatment.

The employee fell from an extension ladder while placing hazard warning labels on a semi-trailer box container. The truck driver discovered the injured employee and called emergency services. Emergency personnel from Bedford Park responded and the employee was transported to Christ Hospital for treatment of a broken left wrist.

The incident occurred when an employee was working on disassembling metal racking from an order picker at a height of six feet, with inadequate fall protection. A beam fell and struck the employee, causing them to fall to the concrete floor, resulting in broken bones.

The employee was working in a 2.0-meter-deep unguarded vat containing boiling water and oil. While replacing a rope on an oil skimmer, he was overcome by the heat and vapors and was found dead by the emergency response team. He suffered severe thermal burns and drowned due to asphyxiation.

On October 8, 2016, an employee was working in a trench when the sidewall caved in, burying him completely. He suffered from crushing injuries to his chest and head. Despite being extracted and transported to the hospital, the employee tragically passed away at 11:00 a.m.
An employee was working in a crawl space underneath a mobile home. The employee contacted a live electrical wire left unguarded underneath the mobile home. The employee was electrocuted.

An employee working in a data command center responded to an alarm, but later coworkers found them unresponsive in a rest room. The Medical Examiner determined that the employee had suffered a heart attack.

An employee was working in a filed picking eggplants.  The employee was found unresponsive on the ground.  Cause of death was possible heat stoke (pending toxicology report). The employee's core temperature was unknown.
An employee was working in a machine room.  A pipe on the pilot receiver broke and released large amount of anhydrous ammonia.

An employee was working in a motor control cabinet on a down turn.  The employee was assigned to change out the fuse holder.  The employee was found unresponsive with electrical burns on the side of his face near his ear.  The employee was killed.

An employee was working in a pond constructing a pier. While using a Jon boat equipped with an irrigation pump to sink pier pilings, the employer provided an additional "lifesaving skiff" which drifted out into the pond. The employee swam out to retrieve the "lifesaving skiff" and drowned.
An employee was working in a security guard shack. He suffered a heart attack and died.
An employee was working in a small family-owned gift shop and suffered a stroke.  The County Coroner issued a finding that the employee died from a pre-existing medical condition.

A bricklayer employee was working in a trench that was 20 feet wide and 10 feet deep, connecting pipes and using mortar. Despite the presence of a protective steel trench box, the employee stepped outside of its confines for an unknown reason, causing a piece of clay to dislodge and strike him in the head. The employee suffered serious cranial trauma as a result and passed away from complications following hospitalization and treatment.

An employee was working in a warehouse unloading an intermodal container. The employee fell backwards in the dock area near the opening of the intermodal container. He was killed by possible heat stress.

An employee was working in a warehouse. As he walked down an aisle in the warehouse, he was struck by a forklift that was travelling in reverse. The worker was taken by emergency services to a nearby hospital, where he died two hours later as a result of his injuries.

An employee was working in an aerial lift basket.  The employee moved the basked toward the roof and was pinned between the roof and the control in the basket.  The employee was crushed and killed onsite.

An employee was working in an excavation installing a drainage system for a parking lot.  A coworker emptied a load of material from a backhoe and it rolled into the trench, striking and crushing him.

While assisting in unloading a curtain side trailer at a sawmill facility, an employee sustained injuries after a vertical column collapsed and struck him on the face, knocking him to the ground and fracturing his right hip. He was taken to an urgent care facility for surgery.

The employee was placing a plywood panel on the second floor of the office to create a platform when he fell nine feet and six inches to the bottom floor after misjudging the edge. He suffered from a broken hip and tragically lost his life as a result of the incident.
An employee was working in housekeeping. While sweeping a FYPA the employee was run over by a truck and crushed.
An employee was working in the bindery and reached behind the stitcher pocket to remove a misfed piece of paper. The employee caught one of their fingers in the drum unit.

An employee was working in the compost yard and was struck by a garbage truck that was backing up.  The employee passed away 10 days later.  Case file number is Snohomish County Medical Examiner case # 16-SN1165.

An employee collapsed and passed away after exiting a confined space in Tower B, where he was working to unclog food sink drains. The employee was wearing protective gear, but medical staff discovered 8.5 ppm of Hydrogen Cyanide in the room near the entrance of the confined space. The company did not have proper safety programs in place, and the autopsy revealed a pre-existing health condition that may have been worsened by respirator use.

During operation of a Wysong press brake, an employee's small metal piece fell back into the machine. The employee disconnected his restraints to retrieve the piece, resulting in the press brake coming down on his fingers. The employee suffered an amputation to the middle three fingers on his left hand and was subsequently hospitalized.

An employee was working in the freezer at temperature as low as minus 10 degrees.  The employee was handling cold products and hands and finger were frost burn. The employee was hospitalized with the frost burns to his finger.
An employee was working in the store when two men walked in and shot the employee. The employee was killed.
An employee was working inside a golf pro-shop.  The employee told customers he wasn't feeling good and called 911. The employee died from a stroke/brain aneurysm.

The employee was found unresponsive inside a new residence under construction while working with spackle and a putty knife. Despite coworkers finding him holding his chest, he was pronounced dead, with the coroner determining cardiovascular disease as the cause of death.

During the excavation process at a residential property, a 4 feet tall brick retaining wall collapsed while an employee was working inside the trench. The wall struck the employee's leg, causing fractures to his ankle and leg. The incident occurred as the employee was leveling the bottom of the 2.5 feet deep and 16 feet long trench.
An employee was working inside a trench when the left side collapsed. No cave-in-protection was in place. The employee was buried and died.

An employee was working inside an Eaton Dry Distribution Transformer, Serial # J14G00891, with a socket and ratchet.  The employee had removed the cover from the transformer and received an electrical shock on their hands.  The employee had not completed lockout, tagout procedures.

An employee was working inside a building scheduled for demolition, which was being performed by a contractor. The contractor made cuts to structural steel columns on multiple floors with the plan to pull them down using wire ropes attached to an excavator. However, during the process, two wire ropes broke while trying to pull down a column. The superintendent resorted to hitting one of the columns with a sledgehammer, causing it to break and fatally injure him in the abdomen. He was transported to the hospital but

During repair work inside an empty jet fuel tank, an employee fell from an extension ladder while taking X-ray shots of welds on the tank wall. Despite being attached to a rope tied to a scaffold, the employee sustained fractures to his femur and neck after hitting the tank floor. He was hospitalized for treatment following the incident.

An employee working in a greenhouse was fatally injured when he tripped over a pallet while carrying a flat of dead plants to a dumpster. The fall resulted in blunt force trauma to his head and neck, causing his death.

The incident involved an employee being pulled into an unguarded Hobart dough mixer while working near it. The employee, wearing a work uniform with a thin white apron and possibly a long sleeve shirt, sustained fatal injuries from blunt and sharp force trauma to the head, neck, and arm. The mixer involved was a Hobart V-1401, serial number 11-1005-003, with a 5 hp motor rated at 1725 rpm, and there were no guards in place

A coworker was using a forklift truck to move a heavy industrial oil filter crushing machine near an employee. The coworker did not fully lowered the load and the unstable machine fell off the lift, hitting and killing the employee. The employee sustained fatal blunt force injuries to the trunk.

The employee was tragically struck and killed by a track-type loader at work, resulting in a crushed head and amputated right arm. Due to lack of witnesses, the exact circumstances of the incident remain unknown, but the employee was last seen in the southeast corner of the property before the accident occurred.

An employee was working near the edge of a slope. There was a safety cable that ended and he reached beyond the safety cable to grab a tree branch, lost his balance and fell approximately six feet. The employee was hospitalized and treated for a fractured back and four broken left ribs.
An employee was working of a ladder. The employee fell to the concrete floor and was killed from head injuries.
An employee was working on a barge that was located in a bay when he died from a prescription drug overdose.
An employee was working on a chimney from a boom basket.  The employee was killed when thrown from the basket when the aerial lift overturned.
An employee was working on a communication tower when he fell backward from it.  The employee fell to the ground and was killed from blunt force trauma.

While working on a construction site for building renovations, an employee transporting ceramic tiles on a steel drywall cart at a business plaza encountered an accident. The cart's caster got stuck in the loading dock leveler, causing the tiles to fall and injure the employee's leg. As a result, the employee suffered a fracture and had to be hospitalized. The incident occurred because the tiles were not properly secured during transportation.

An employee working on a farm hand picking tomatoes suddenly collapsed and died from a sudden cardiac arrest with pre-existing medical conditions. Despite efforts to perform CPR, he was pronounced dead on the scene. He had not been feeling well and did not eat lunch before abruptly ceasing work and collapsing in the parking lot.
An employee was working on a flat roof, when he fell. The employee struck the ground below, sustaining a back injury, which he was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.
An employee was working on a General Electric exhaust fan located on a roof.  The employee fell through a skylight, dropped approximately 19 feet, and struck the concrete floor, killing him.

An employee was working on a ladder jack scaffold platform located greater than 7 1/2 feet above ground.  The employee fell and struck his head on the ground and was killed due to traumatic head injuries.
An employee was working on a ladder. He fell off the ladder and 	broke his leg. The employee was hospitalized and treated for his injuries.
An employee was working on a lathe machine. The employee's sweater from his left arm became entangled and the employee was pulled into the machine and killed.

An employee working on a Line PC-3200 and bagger #9 had his right middle finger amputated when it became caught in the belt and sprocket while making a minor adjustment. The employee received treatment at a nearby hospital. The incident investigation revealed that proper lockout/tagout procedures were not followed to control hazardous energy before the adjustment was made.

An employee working on a light rail extension project on a public street was hit by a water crossing that was dragged by a passing double decker bus. The employee, who was implementing traffic control measures at the time, suffered a fractured leg and ankle as a result of the accident and had to be hospitalized.

An employee was working on a roof within 6 feet of a skylight. The employee fell through the skylight approximately 35 feet to the concrete surface below.  The employee was killed due to blunt force injuries of the head and chest.

An employee was working on a roof. As he transitioned from a flat portion of the roof, to one with pitch to install an anchor point and retractable lanyard, he lost traction and fell 12 feet to the ground below. He fractured both his legs and a heel of one of his feet.

While working on a RV vehicle, an employee accidentally cut an airline that supplied air to the air bags, causing the RV to collapse on him. The employee was pinned between the fender and the wheel of the vehicle, resulting in injuries to his shoulder and neck. He was subsequently hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was working on a scaffold building a masonry wall.  The scaffold collapsed and the employee fell to the ground and was killed.

An employee was working on a six foot ladder outside the employers warehouse. The employee fell off the ladder while removing an electrical cable and struck the pavement and retaining wall. The employee was killed from the injury.

The employee was working on a steep slope roof assisting with the installation of step flashing when he was struck by a piece of plywood caught by the wind. The impact caused him to lose his balance and fall from the north side eave, which was nearly 10 feet in elevation. Tragically, the fall resulted in the employee's death.

An employee was working on a vehicle in an auto parts store when it went off balance and fell on top of the employee.  He suffered blunt force trauma to their torso and suffocated.  The employee was killed.

An employee was working on a Warehouse Dock Plate. It appears that the rod that held the dock plate up failed or that objects forced the dock plate down, bending the support rod. The dock plate smashed the employee to death.

An employee was working on an 8-foot ladder to replace a part from the top of a vapor canister,  which was approximately 14 feet high from a rock-embedded slab.  The employee fell off the ladder, hit his head on the floor, and was killed.

An employee was working on an AP test machine. The employee reached for the part by placing her fingers on a dual digit sensor. It came down and amputated her fingertip. The employee was hospitalized and treated for her injuries.
An employee was working on an elevated surface.  The employee fell from an unprotected edge and struck the concrete floor.  The employee was killed as a result of a traumatic brain injury.

An employee was working on an elevator shaft landing. He picked up a 6 by 6 post and dropped it. The post broke and fell through the landing. The employee fell 9 feet through the first landing then 10 feet through the next landing. The employee was hospitalized and treated for two fractured ribs.

An employee was working on an excavation.  The employee looked into the excavation when it collapsed and engulfed him when a 10 inch water main broke and he was covered with a water and mud mixture.  The employee drowned as a result.

An employee was working on an unpressurized vessel and was to replace lining of a dump nozzle.  The employee felt chest pains and climbed down from his work station prior to performing work.  The employee was taken to a hospital by staff onsite, where he died.

An employee was working on carpentry fascia work with a nail gun.  The employee became entangled in a lifeline and unhooked his harness to remove himself from the tangle.  The employee fell approximately 24 feet to ground, struck ground and suffered injuries from impact. The employee was killed.

During the demolition of a support and grain elevator leg casing, an employee was using a special purpose personnel elevator. Unfortunately, the employee was crushed between the elevator car and the top of the elevator structure when electrical wiring was damaged by a crane pulling out demolition work.

The employee was abrasive blasting the top deck of a tugboat when they slipped on the blasting material, causing them to accidentally blast their left forearm. The employee sustained a laceration and had abrasive grit embedded under their skin.

An employee fell 33 feet to the ground while working on an unfinished roof without wearing fall protection. He suffered a fatal skull fracture as a result. The incident investigation found that there was no dedicated monitor or supervisor to ensure workers stayed within the designated safety boundaries.

An employee was crushed between a flywheel and the forks of a forklift while working on a Wegner Perforating Press. The employee had climbed onto the forks of a Toyota forklift, raised approximately 8 feet, 5 inches in the air by the operator, to access the flywheel and remove spacers from the bearings. When the employee removed the locking nut from the shaft of the flywheel, the weight of the flywheel caused it to fall forward, resulting in the
An employee was working on the ground under a bucket truck. The limb being trimmed by bucket truck operator fell and struck the employee in back of neck. The employee was killed.

An employee was working on the return copper tube of an HVAC condenser machine.  The employee was found unresponsive in a fetal position by the home owner.  Cause of death was not apparent at the time of the incident report.

An employee working on the roof of a two-story apartment complex fell 19 feet to the ground after losing his footing near the unprotected side of the roof. He suffered multiple contusions and rib fractures, requiring hospitalization and treatment. Investigation revealed that the employee was not wearing fall protection at the time of the incident.

While working on the roof of the new student center building, an employee unknowingly walked into an opening covered by a sheet of plywood that was not properly secured. The employee fell 25 feet to the concrete floor below, sustaining serious injuries that led to their death at the hospital.

An employee working on a residential roof fell 11 feet to the concrete below, striking his head. Despite coworkers administering first aid and contacting EMS, the employee passed away from a subdural hematoma. Tragically, the incident occurred while the employee was stapling down roof material.
An employee was working on the roof when he fell through the skylight.  The employee landed on the concrete floor, cut his head, and fractured an unspecified bone.

An employee was working on the roof, carrying roofing panels. The employee unhooked his lanyard and was blown off the roof by a gust of wind and fell to the ground on a concrete surface.  The employee suffered from fractured skull, concussion and other broken bones and was hospitalized.
An employee was working on the roof. The employee had trouble breathing and collapsed.The employee died of cardiac arrest.

During a work task using the Scotchman Industries Model 6509 ironworker, an employee accidentally amputated their right thumb above the first knuckle while fashioning a switch housing. The incident occurred when the employee pinched their thumb between the part and the top die while using the press function of the machine.
An employee was working on the second floor of an evaporator.  The sight glass was broken and the employee had their left arm sucked into the evaporator by the vacuum.  The employee was killed.

An employee at a full service printed circuit board manufacturer was injured while fixing a jammed hoist on top of a plating tank in the production area. The employee slipped while climbing down from the tank, causing their left foot to fall into the tank containing hot chemical mixtures. They were transported to a hospital in San Jose for treatment of chemical burns.

An employee working alone in the shop on overtime became trapped in the Willis Fanuc CNC lathe while working on an auger. A coworker discovered the deceased employee lying on top of the lathe after returning to check on him. The interlocked doors of the lathe were found to be disabled. Video footage captured only a portion of the incident.

During construction operations, an employee fell approximately 11 feet to the ground after a material lifting platform tipped over on top of him. The employee was working on attaching metal roofing materials on top of a framed building when the accident occurred. The 20 ft. cage used to lift materials weighed approximately 1,100 lbs and ultimately crushed and killed the employee.

An employee was working the counter at a convenience store.  Two armed individuals entered the store and demanded money. The employee emptied both cash registers and his own pockets. Perpetrators shot the employee on their way out of the store. The employee died at the hospital.

While working in the injection molding department, an employee was moving a cart with a 975 lb mold on top. The cart, rated for 4,000 lbs, tipped over as the employee released the brakes, causing the mold to fall on her left side and hands. This resulted in fractured ribs and bruising to her abdomen, hip, femur, and hands, leading to a two-day hospitalization.

While attempting to attach an overhead chain hoist to an engine block on an elevated shelf, an employee accidentally stepped on a shelf holding a car engine. As he was stepping down, he bumped a piece of 18-inch rebar with a pointed end, causing it to fall and puncture his shin as he landed on the concrete floor. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for his injury.

An employee was working to clear a jam from a conveyor system, when he was pilled into the equipment. He sustained crushing injuries to his right wrist and forearm, which he was hospitalized and received treatment.

An employee was working to disengage a trash dumpster from a chain. However, the empty trash dumpster got caught by a hook on the chain. As he removed the hook the dumpster dropped onto his left foot causing four broken toes.

While trying to free a stuck extractor in an injection mold, an employee used a hammer to strike the return pins. When the mold began to move on the bench, the employee placed his left hand on top to hold it in place. The extractor was released, but the employee's left index finger was amputated in the process.

While adjusting bracing on the interior of a structure, an employee accidentally stepped into an uncovered opening on the first floor, falling 11.5 feet to the ground below. The opening, meant to be a stairwell, measured 11.9 feet by 3.6 feet. Tragically, the employee did not survive the fall.

While trying to remove a roller board from a metal hook, an employee lost her balance and fell backwards, hitting her left hip on the linoleum floor. She suffered a hip fracture and had to be hospitalized for treatment.

During maintenance work, an employee's foot was amputated after a 40,000 pound furnace scrapper fell while he was removing bolts. The incident occurred as he was arc welding the final bolt for removal. Medics treated the injured employee at the hospital following the accident.

An employee was working to un-jam a piece of equipment. During troubleshooting, the air actuated the cutting head of the equipment. This crushed the employee's fingers and the two tips of his fingers were amputated. He was hospitalized and received treatment.

An employee was working to unclog a tube of a roller machine. As the employee removed the machine's guard and placed his hand near the rollers of the machine, his fingers became entangled in the moving parts. The tip of one of his fingers was amputated.

An employee was working to unjam a pallet that had become caught in an auto feed machine. As the employee entered the machine to pull the pallet out, one of his hands became caught in between the pallet and the frame of the machine. The employee crushes hand and is hospitalized.

The employee was injured while trying to unjam packaging film from a vertical fill of a packaging machine. Her hand was crushed and fingers lacerated when the machine actuated while her hand was inside its cutting and seaming platens. The employee was hospitalized and underwent surgery as a result of the accident.
An employee was working under a Low-boy trailer.  The trailer was not blocked or cribbed, and it fell onto the employee, killing him.
An employee was working underneath a minivan that was raised on a jack. The minivan fell on the employee. The employee sustained compressional asphyxia and was killed.

An employee was working underneath a vehicle that was supported by an automotive lift.  The employee was crushed when one of the four supporting arms shifted and the vehicle fell on top of the employee.

An employee working underneath the cab of a semi wrecker for mechanical repairs on the Jake brake was fatally injured when the cab unexpectedly released and trapped his body between the cab and the engine exhaust pipe. He suffered fatal blunt force trauma and asphyxiation from the weight of the cab.

While working with a coworker, an employee was attempting to move a heavy safety barrier for a pressure test on a Dragon capsule propulsion system. They tried to maneuver the barrier through a set of double doors and when it started to fall over, the employee's left hand got crushed, resulting in the amputation of the tips of his middle and ring fingers.

An employee working in an aerial lift with a coworker to install a ceiling panel in a bell tower was tragically caught between the panel and the tower's structural frame when the lift moved unintentionally. The lift's movement was caused by the platform leveling pedal being activated, despite a safety device being removed or bypassed. The employee's cause of death was confirmed as compression asphyxiation due to mechanical compression of the neck, with additional injuries including head trauma and crushing injuries.

While working with a coworker to clear a hardened chemical product from the feed throat of the Color Development Line Extruder, an employee left the machine turned on during lunch. Upon returning, they attempted to clear the blockage using a shop-vac, but a buildup of back pressure caused heated PET to blow out and result in second degree burns to the employee's face, arms, and hands. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for the burns.

An employee was working with a coworker loading a 55 gallon barrel of used oil onto a truck lift gate.  The employee fell from the lift gate while guiding the barrel from the lift gate to the truck body.  The employees chest and abdomen were crushed when the barrel fell on top of them.

While working with a coworker to haul off propane tanks using cranes mounted on truck tractors, an employee was electrocuted when the crane's boom made contact with an exposed powerline. The incident occurred as they were moving the tanks from the East perimeter of the site to the West side of the powerlines.

During the installation of anchor bolts in a Power Distribution Unit, one employee was exposed to 480 volts and was killed, while another employee received an electrical burn on his shoulder. The incident occurred while the employees were working inside the cabinet, with one coming into contact with the line-feed side of the breaker. Employee #2 was leaning on a transformer at the time of the incident. Employee #1 was fatally injured, while Employee #2 was not hospitalized for his injuries.

While working on replacing the hopper floor of a garbage truck, an employee's right thumb got caught between the hydraulic floor jack extension shaft and a shim when the shaft began losing contact with the bucket frame. As a result, the tip of his thumb was amputated, leading to hospitalization and treatment.

The incident involved an employee operating a Deere 50D mini excavator to push a trunk from a tall pine tree. While working on another trunk, the employee was unaware of the original tree leaning towards him. Despite warnings from coworkers, the employee was struck and killed by the falling tree trunk.
An employee was working with a press brake and amputated a finger.  No additional details were provided in the original accident report.

During a sheet metal manipulation process using a press brake, an employee's left hand got crushed between the clamp and the sheet metal. This resulted in fractures in three of the digits on his hand. The incident occurred when he stepped on the foot pedal control while using his left hand to hold the sheet metal in place.

An employee working with a trailer carrying empty porta-potty stalls was crushed under the trailer hitch by his neck and chest after it was not properly secured. He was taken to the hospital but sadly passed away three days later.

While setting up a work zone, an employee fell from the back of a moving truck as an unsecured tamper machine slid off the tailgate. Despite initially landing on his feet, the employee ultimately stumbled and fell backwards, hitting his head on the pavement. Tragically, he sustained fatal head trauma and passed away a few hours later.

During hydro-testing of tubing in a well, an employee's left thumb was partially amputated when a coworker accidentally pinched it between the API ring and elevator while adjusting equipment. The incident occurred after the crew realized they had installed a circulating head that was too large and replaced it with a smaller one.

The incident involved an employee helping to move a 120 gallon upright air compressor with two coworkers. During the process, the shipping pallet holding the air compressor fell over, crushing the employee between the compressor and the ground. The employee sustained a fractured arm and leg as a result of the accident.

During a roofing job at a two-story residential home, an employee lost his balance and fell approximately 25 feet to the ground in an alleyway while tearing off shingles. The employee suffered fatal internal and head injuries as a result of the fall.

An employee was working with two other workers and they were mating a 480 VAC Limitorque actuator to a 30-inch valve using a Jib crane.  The employee's hand contacted the valve casing that was shorted internally and was electrocuted.

An employee was writing the container location on the frame of the container chassis. A coworker was driving a truck which then pulled forward when the employee was in the zone of danger. The employee was run over by the 4th and 5th axle of the truck.

An employee wearing a positioning saddle fall arrest system was ascending a rope in a tree when the harness broke, causing the employee to fall approximately 40 feet to a wood deck below. The employee suffered head trauma and was killed in the incident.
An employee weighed and carried potassium cyanide salts to a laboratory hood. The employee was wearing an N95 respirator. The employee sustained acute potassium cyanide poisoning.

An employee lost their life after being found unresponsive in a tank containing alkyl ketone while cleaning it. The coworker became concerned after not hearing any activity and found the employee face-up inside the tank. Despite efforts by emergency services, the employee did not survive. The tank originally contained an environmental hazardous substance.

An employee went to service a machine that had a mechanical part that stopped.  The employee reached into the machine where a metal part engaged and it pinned him against the machine support bar, crushing his skull.
An employee while sitting on a wooden bench informing residents to leave the beach area, was struck and killed by lightning.

The employee slipped on ice while exiting a truck at the worksite and struck his head on the asphalt parking lot. Despite expressing that he did not feel well to co-workers, he was admitted to the hospital where he developed a coma and eventually died on March 15, 2016, due to blunt force trauma to the head.

An employee who was a CNC machine operator, was milling a 1-1/4 inch diameter metal bar when he was struck by the 27 inches of rod that was outside of the machine. He suffered a severe upper arm injury and he later died at the hospital.

A custodian employee was cleaning up after a weekend event when she fell while throwing trash from an elevated dock into a dumpster due to rags blocking an overhead door. She fractured her ankle and later passed away after complications with her recovery.

While using a hand held oxygen/acetylene torch to wash old welds from bulkhead ribs inside a vessel, a fitter/boilermaker was tragically engulfed in flames at floor level. Despite the efforts of the fire watch and crew members, the employee suffered fatal thermal burns.

The employee, a foreman for a power line clearance crew, was operating a chainsaw while elevated in a bay laurel tree at a height of 54 feet. He accidentally cut through his work lanyard with the chainsaw, causing him to fall to the ground. Tragically, the employee was killed as a result of blunt force trauma to the head and chest from the fall.
An employee who was a landscaper was walking towards the company truck. The employee collapsed on his way to the company truck and died of an apparent heart attack.
An employee who was a lineman was hanging fuses and barrels onto an electrical cutout. The employee contacted a live electrical line and sustained an electrical shock that killed him.
An employee who was a nurse manager was assisting a patient in a hospital to move onto a bedpan when she injured her back. The employee sustained a severe back sprain requiring hospitalization.

A roofer was working on a roof ridge 30 feet above the ground when he slipped on the 45 degree slope. As he caught himself, a roll of Grip Rite waterproofing material rolled off the ridge and struck him on the head, causing a fatal injury. The incident occurred while the employee was carrying two PVC pipes from the garage to the crawl space on the North West side of the house.

An employee who was a Widland Firefighter, was cutting a tree down and the tree fell on top of him when it changed direction.  The employee's head and chest was crushed when struck by the tree and died from those injuries.

An electrician was working with two colleagues to remove anchoring bolts from a new electrical panel unit when he suddenly collapsed in an awkward position between the unit and a wall. Despite attempts at first aid by his coworkers and emergency responders, the electrician unfortunately passed away from a heart attack.

An employee who was doing tuck pointing fell as he was attempting to step off of a shed dormer onto a ladder placed against a chimney.  The ladder moved and the employee fell 26 feet. He was killed as a result of a broken neck and concussion/brain injury.
An employee who was installing an aluminum frame was found dead in a company vehicle. The employee died from a wasp sting.

An employee who was leaving work for the day lost her balance fell and fractured her femur.  She was brought to surgery the next day 8/29/16. Prior to her surgical procedure, Ms. Cumberbatch went into cardiac arrest and died.
An employee who was picking berries was found laying unconscious in a restroom.  The employee died from a heart attack. attack.
An employee who was removing a dip-stick housing from a bus, fell 33 inches from a ladder onto a concrete floor, sustained head trauma, and died.
An employee who was working at a roofs edge fell 22 feet to the concrete and was killed.

During a multi-agency technical rescue training class, a fire department employee was participating in an exercise involving rescue from a burning tower stack. After completing the simulated rescue, the employee was descending a ladder with a full body harness and a Tower Rig tie-off system. Unfortunately, one of the carabineers became tangled in his portable radio, causing it to break free and hit him in the nose. This led to the employee slipping off the ladder and falling approximately 1 foot, resulting in the displacement
An employee who worked for a towing company lost his balance and fell over an overpass, striking his head upon the ground. The employee was killed from head injuries.

An employee on a hog farm entered a building divided into an entrance and an office to shower and change clothes before entering the hog barn. While taking a break, her coworker found her unconscious in the shower area. Testing revealed high levels of carboxyhemoglobin in her blood, indicating exposure to dangerous levels of a chemical. The employee tragically died from asphyxiation due to the exposure.

An employee on a hog farm lost their life after being exposed to deadly levels of carboxyhemoglobin in a small building where they were required to shower and change clothes before entering the hog barn. The coworker found the employee unconscious in the shower area after using a power washer nearby. The employee's blood test showed a carboxyhemoglobin level of 47.8 percent, leading to their tragic death from asphyxiation.

A temporary worker was moving a trough filled with 1,000 lbs. of hot water when it splashed onto his right arm and foot, causing severe burns. The incident occurred while the employee was rocking the trough, causing the water to wave towards him. The employee suffered second degree burns on his right foot and a severe burn on his right arm.

An armed man drove through a parking lot at high speed, entered a store and began shooting at employees. One employee, with one year of tenure and 50 years of age, was tragically killed in the encounter. The assailant quickly fled the scene, leaving chaos and grief in his wake. The coworker of the deceased employee believes that he died immediately and was pronounced dead shortly after the incident.

An employee with temporary status was operating a chop saw machine. The employee was adjusting the position of the wood and placed his hand in the point of operation of the machine.  As a result, his right thumb was partially amputated.

During troubleshooting and installation of new parts for a Laempe LFB50-H Sand Core Machine, an employee was caught inside the machine as the outer ram section began slipping downward. Despite attempts to rescue him, the worker could not be removed due to the crushing action of the machine. After securing and lifting the ram off the worker, first aid was administered but unfortunately, the employee did not survive his injuries. He was pronounced dead at a local hospital.

An employee working adjacent to a tackle block and sheave assembly got his gloved hand caught in a pinch point where the winch cable and block parts met. The employee sustained partial amputation of his finger tips.

While troubleshooting the air flow of an exhaust hood above an oven in a kitchen, an employee fell from a ladder in a riser room to the concrete floor, sustaining fatal injuries. The employee had been carrying new V-Belts for the exhaust hood at the time of the incident. A 6-foot ladder was found placed against a 15-foot fixed ladder in the riser room where the employee fell.

The incident involved a baler operator who was fatally injured after becoming caught inside a Machinex single-ram open ended baler. The employee was fixing broken wires inside the machine chamber when the baler cycled, crushing the employee. The employee sustained multiple crushing injuries and tragically lost their life as a result of the incident.
An employee working as a deckhand securing a barge to a barge dock was caught between the barge dock rake and the coaming of the barge.  The employee was crushed and killed.
An employee working as a security guard at a restaurant/lounge was struck and killed when breaking up fight.

An employee part of a railroad repair team was checking the level of newly laid rails when a nearby flat storage building collapsed, burying him in tons of flowing grain. Despite his co-workers managing to escape, the employee was tragically killed and crushed by the weight of the wheat.

An employee at a cranberry processing facility was performing sanitation operations from the top of a large cranberry dryer using a pressure washer. The employee lost his balance while standing up after closing a panel and fell backwards, sustaining a head laceration and two fractures to the left shoulder. It was discovered that no fall protection was used and the employee was not trained on fall protection or safe cleaning procedures for working at heights.

A worker at a vehicle recycling yard was fatally injured while using a Titan HD2P -9000AF 9000 lb capacity two post lift to raise a vehicle. The lift was missing rubber pads on the lifting arms and the control button had been replaced with a male plug. As the vehicle was being raised, the employee got caught between the hydraulic lift post and the vehicle, causing the vehicle to slide off and crush him.

A worker at a wooden window and door manufacturing firm suffered a partial amputation of his left thumb while removing parts from an adhesive spreader machine. The incident occurred when his thumb got caught in a pinch point created by the upper rollers of the machine as he reached for a piece of scrap cardboard. Fortunately, he did not require hospitalization for his injury.

An employee working from a truck bucket hoist installing an electrical wire spreader arm on an electrical pole at a height of approximately 40 feet made contact with a 12,000 volt live wire. The employee received an electrical shock and was killed.

The employee, who was working from an elevated position of 10 to 12 feet, fell and struck the right side of his head, resulting in a severe head injury. He was transported to a hospital where he underwent surgery, but unfortunately passed away on March 7, 2016 due to complications from the head injury and a pre-existing heart condition.
An employee working in a construction zone was struck and killed by a motor vehicle. The driver didn't yield to workers in a construction zone.

While cleaning a pneumatic butterfly valve to remove leftover meat product in a nutritional supplements manufacturing plant, an employee's right index finger tip was amputated when the valve closed unexpectedly after a miscommunication with a coworker resulted in the air source being disconnected. EMS took the employee to the hospital for treatment. The accident highlighted the importance of proper energy restraint (lockout) procedures in the workplace.
An employee working in alkylation "alky" unit.  A isobutane fire occurred and  the employee received serious burns.

An employee working in an extended aerial lift basket was removing metal trim from an outdoor sign when the trim touched a power transmission line, shocking the employee. The employee fell through the rails of the basket due to lack of fall protection and was killed as a result.
An employee working on a "Moffett" forklift was struck by a semi-tractor trailer and killed.

An employee working on a roof taking materials to other employees became ill. The supervisor had the employee go to the ground to cool off. The employee walked around and collapsed from possible heat stress and dehydration. The employee died from organ failure and hemorrhage during intubation.
An employee working on an electrical circuit made contact with a live wire energized to 277 Volts. The employee was killed from an electrical shock.
An employee working on computer passed out and struck head on furniture. The employee was killed from acute cardiopulmonary insufficiency.

During the installation of a beam on the second floor of a house, an employee standing on a wet baker's scaffold with a metal decking work surface slipped while trying to catch a shifted beam. The employee fell through a doorway from the second floor to the ground below, hitting his head and breaking his neck, resulting in his death.
An employee working on top of a building died from a heart attack.
An employee working outside and waiting near a tree for a hole to be filled, was struck by heavy equipment. The employee received two injuries to the head, and died.

An employee was injured while trying to un-jam a stack of milk crates from a conveyor system in a cooler room. The track popped up and caught the employee's left ankle, resulting in a severe injury that ultimately required surgery to amputate his foot. The employee was hospitalized for treatment following the incident.

A 54-year-old superintendent went to a job site to drop off tools and materials. While on the 3rd floor, he climbed into an unstable load box that fell 27 feet to the ground, resulting in his death. The box was not properly secured to the industrial vehicle and was constructed with inadequate materials.

A 30-year-old male laborer was found hunched over a bathtub by the home leaseholder while refinishing a bathtub for the housing authority. The employee had poured a chemical containing methylene chloride into the bathtub, brushed it onto the sides, and scraped the bathtub as part of the deglazing process. The employee was working alone at the worksite, with the door closed to prevent vapors from spreading, and a window in the bathroom propped open with a can of shaving cream.

An employee, a 38 year old, male painter, was painting the ceiling of an existing commercial building, and then fell 11.5 foot high mobile frame scaffold to the ground.  As a result, the employee sustained multiple injuries and then died, on February 13, 2017.

On December 27, 2016, a 45-year-old male employee fell approximately 15 feet from a ladder while assisting with the installation of a fascia board on a 2-story roof. Despite being rushed to the hospital, the employee tragically passed away from head injuries sustained in the fall. The incident serves as a grim reminder of the importance of workplace safety measures and precautions.

A 60 year old male employee fell approximately 13 feet from the top of a dry tank trailer while trying to secure a dryer hose with a Bungee strap. The employee sustained head and neck injuries and died later that same day as a result of the fall.

The employee, a carpenter framing roofing trusses at a commercial gas station, fell 13.6 feet to the concrete ground. Despite wearing a body harness, it was not properly adjusted to limit falls to 6 feet or less. The employee was taken to the hospital where he passed away 10 days later from injuries sustained in the fall.

A carpenter fell approximately nine feet from scaffold plank while taking measurements to install j-channel and flashing around windows. The fall resulted in fractures to the pelvis, tailbone, ribs, separated shoulder, and lacerations to the thumb. The employee was then admitted to Carle Foundation Hospital in Urbana for treatment.

An employee, a construction worker, was doing some light demolition and clean-out of debris from a hospital worksite.  The employee collapsed at the end of a 7-hour work shift and was killed from heat-induced seizures. The ambient temperature on that day reached 91 degrees Fahrenheit.

While working in the Chabot Dam, a diver was using a pressure washer to cut through sediments around a pipeline. His coworker informed him to secure the pressure washer and eductor as his dive was ending. Despite efforts to make the units cold, the employee accidentally injured his right foot with the pressure washer due to possible kickback and not holding it with two hands. He was hospitalized for an injection injury.
An employee, a doorman, was found unresponsive and had died from cardiac arrest.

During the night shift, a dozer operator was standing on a wood chip pile next to a drag chain conveyor when the ground gave way, pulling him under the chips. His body was eventually found on a conveyor leading to a screening operation, where it was ejected through a chute to a scrap pile. The employee suffered body trauma and suffocated during the incident.

The employee, a drywall finisher, fell while applying tape and joint compound to an interior gypsum wall from a Skyjack scissor lift on a construction site. He suffered a head laceration, spinal cord injury, and nerve damage, with no witnesses to the fall. Emergency response was called and he was taken to the University of Vermont Medical Center before being transferred to Spaulding Rehabilitation Hospital. The details of the incident were unclear, with witnesses reporting the scissor lift was down when the

An employee, a gardener was performing gardening services for a private residence. He was working near the homeowner's pool.  The employee was found unresponsive at the bottom of the pool with his leave blower. He was declared dead on-site. The coroner listed the cause of death as "drowning."

On May 4, 2016, a school crossing guard was assisting children crossing the intersection when they were struck by a motor vehicle traveling eastbound. Despite efforts to save them, the employee later succumbed to their injuries. Our thoughts are with the employee's loved ones during this difficult time.

During a concrete coring operation, the machine being operated by a superintendent was not securely anchored to the floor. As a result, the machine spun out of control and the handle struck the employee in the right upper arm, causing a two inch laceration. The employee required approximately 20 stitches but did not need to be hospitalized.

The employee, a truck driver, was trying to raise and retract the landing gear on a flatbed trailer after connecting the electrical and air lines. When he realized the landing gear was still down, he left the tractor without setting the parking brake and went to manually crank up the landing gear. Unfortunately, as he was cranking, his head got caught between two flatbed trailers when the tractor and trailer rolled backwards. This resulted in his death from severe head trauma.

The employee, a truck driver, was parked and had dropped a trailer. While attempting to locate the trailer he was scheduled to pick up, the employee was struck and killed by a company trailer switcher who was relocating a full trailer from the dock. The employee suffered multiple injuries to the upper body, resulting in his death.

An employee was tragically killed when he was run over by a skip loader at a truck wash facility after starting the engine. The skip loader moved forward, striking a utility truck and pushing it into stacked tires. The employee suffered blunt force trauma to the chest and was found on the ground. The skip loader had been left in first gear with the throttle control set to low, but the parking brake was engaged.

An employee, after unloading steel all morning, ate lunch and returned to work at 1:00 p.m.  At 200 p.m. the employee was cramping and instructed to rest in the shade and hydrate.  At 5 p.m. the employee collapsed. The employee died from suspected heat related illness.

While on the fourth floor observing a coworker take measurements for an electrical raceway, an electrician tragically fell into an unguarded ventilation shaft. Despite efforts to help, the employee succumbed to head and body injuries sustained from the fall.

An employee, who was also the owner, was felling a 35-foot tree when he fell to the ground after cutting the top. He was wearing a safety belt, but it did not appear that a lanyard was connected to it. The employee was pronounced dead at the hospital.
An employee, an owner, was installing tar paper on a roof. The employee fell 45 feet to the ground level. The employee suffered from multiple fractures and and was killed.

The employee, who had a Level III Blasting Certification, was performing blasting operations with a coworker. After the first blast attempt failed to detonate all blast-holes, the employee and coworker made repairs and proceeded with a second blast. Unfortunately, during the second blast, the employee was fatally injured when debris flew towards him. Despite immediate medical attention, the employee later died at the hospital.

During the process of hanging a tarp on the wall to cover an opening, an employee and coworker were standing on a pallet lifted by a forklift truck. Unfortunately, the pallet cracked under the weight and the employee fell to the ground below, breaking his right lower leg.

An employee, direct support professional, was found unresponsive at residence where she worked as an assisted living staff member for people with mental disabilities by a coworker. It is believed the employee was fatally stabbed to death by one of three residents under her care.

During electrical installation work at a commercial freezer, an employee fell approximately twenty five feet to the concrete floor below from the top of the freezer after exiting a scissor lift. Tragically, the employee was killed despite wearing a full body harness at the time of the accident. Multiple workers were on the scissor lift and along the perimeter of the freezer during the incident.

While troubleshooting a rolling ball machine, a maintenance mechanic attempted to dry a drive belt with a paper towel. The mechanic's left index finger got caught between the drive pulley and belt, resulting in a partial amputation. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment for the injury.

The employee, a maintenance worker at a mobile home park, was operating a Craftsman gas powered pressure washer to clean a laundry room floor. Sadly, the employee was killed by asphyxiation, likely due to exposure to carbon monoxide from the pressure washer. The incident serves as a tragic reminder of the importance of proper ventilation and safety protocols when using gas powered equipment indoors.

While attempting to move the boom lift closer to the work location, the operator drove the lift onto unstable ground, causing it to tilt and fall over. This resulted in Employee #1 and Employee #2 being ejected 60 feet from the lift. Employee #1 tragically passed away from his injuries, while Employee #2 suffered multiple broken bones and was taken to the hospital for treatment.

The pest control technician was setting traps in the crawl space of an attic in an occupied professional office building when he was found unresponsive. He was later pronounced dead from a fracture of the neck due to blunt force injury to the head from a fall. The autopsy report confirmed the cause of death.

The Rolling Operator/Machinist II was operating the Grief Buffer machine in the Ball Screw Rolling Department when the incident occurred involving a large screw 2502 ball screw. The employee's hand was caught between the buffing wheel and screw stock, resulting in the loss of the pinky finger and serious injury to the ring finger. The employee was taken to the hospital via ambulance for treatment and was hospitalized for his injuries.
An employee, sitting in a car sustained a ruptured aneurysm and died.
An employee, while diagnosing a customer's engine on a boat in a body of water, apparently fell overboard. The employee suffered a possible heart attack and died.
An employee, while operating a zero-turn ridding lawnmower on an incline, went over an embankment falling approximately 10 feet into a creek, and was killed.
An employee, while picking olives, felt ill and fell to ground which was the same level and was a dirt surface. The employee died from congestive heart failure.

An employee, while preparing to perform routine maintenance on an elevator, was struck by a falling elevator car and pinned against a ladder and a beam. The employee sustained crushing injuries to the head and was killed.
An employee, while talking on the telephone, dropped the suspended two point scaffold. The employee was strangled by lifeline and was killed.
An employee, while trouble shooting electrical outlets touched exposed wires, got shocked, and was killed.
An employee, while troubleshooting a home owner's satellite dish, fell 20 feet from ladder.  The employee was killed.

An employee, while trying to adjust packaging film, reached between the jaws of a packaging machine and the machine unexpectedly cycled. The employee sustained a severed left index finger which resulted in amputation beyond the first joint.

An employee inspecting parts behind Press Number 23 was struck by a high-low fork truck while walking towards the shipping department. The employee suffered a crushing injury to the right foot and required reconstructive surgery on the right elbow, resulting in a four-night hospital stay.

A 59-year-old crane operator was moving a 3,000 lb steel assembly when the load tipped, striking him in the lower leg. He sustained broken tibia and fibula and was hospitalized, undergoing surgery. Sadly, he passed away three weeks later from a pulmonary embolism.

A teacher working at a high school for disabled students tried to escort a misbehaving student back to class, but the student refused to comply. While attempting to hold the student with a coworker, the teacher fell to the ground and fractured their hip. The teacher was taken to the hospital for treatment.
An employee, who was previously on medical leave, returned to work to inquire about when he could return to work. While onsite, the employee suffered a heart attack and died.

The owner of the company was using a scissor lift to work on plumbing lines 26 feet above ground in a commercial building. The lift's wheel rolled into a ditch, causing it to fall over and eject the employee onto the concrete floor. Despite immediate help from a subcontractor and outside workers, the employee tragically lost his life in the accident.

An employee working as a plumbing apprentice developed an infection in his knee after kneeling in a broken sewage pipe area with a small cut on March 8, 2017. The infection symptoms started on the same night and he was hospitalized and treated for the infection.

A Test Engineer at an engineering test station fell off his chair while attempting to enter a password on a computer. He bumped into a cart during the fall, causing him to land on his back and hit his head on the floor. He was found by a coworker with blood coming from his ear and mouth, and emergency medical services were called. Despite their arrival, the employee passed away at the hospital on January 15, 2017.

An employee, working from the fifth rung of an 8-foot step ladder, was wiring a live electrical junction box with bare hands. The employee fell from the ladder to the floor.  The employee sustained electrical burns and head trauma and was killed.
An employee's finger was pinched between a dolly and trailer. The employee's right middle finger tip was amputated.
An employee's hand was caught between the blow-out preventer and elevator. The employee sustained lacerations and fractured his hand. The employee was hospitalized.

As an employee was warning coworkers about a piece of equipment out of service by a grinding room entrance, she was accidentally hit by an electric pallet jack operated by a coworker. The coworker had stopped to speak with the employee but forgot to set the brakes on the pallet jack. The pallet jack rolled forward, pinning the employee's right leg against a concrete wall, causing a contusion and crushing injury to her right ankle, resulting in hospitalization.

The employee did not return home after his shift ended at 4:30 p.m. His wife called the company, leading personnel to find him unresponsive at a poultry house at 8:16 p.m. He was taken to the hospital and admitted in critical condition, eventually passing away from head trauma on April 3, 2017.
An employee/owner jumped from the fourth floor to escape a fire and he was killed.

A worker accessed an unguarded area of a steel coil recoiling machine, where he attempted to insert paper between coils of steel. His hands and arms became caught in the recoiler, pulling him into the machine up to his waist before it was stopped by a coworker. Tragically, the employee was killed in the incident.
An employees was removing a stair tower and when the rigging was released, the stair tower fell over striking and killing the employee.
An employees was using the porta potty.  The porta potty exploded and caught fire while employee was inside. The employee was killed from burns to the body.

Employee #1 was working on laying a new roof at a residence along with the employer. The roof had a pitch of 10:12 and was 20 feet above the ground. While connecting to one of the anchors to lay roofing felt paper, Employee #1 tripped over a piece of lumber and fell from the roof, striking a concrete pad below and unfortunately, succumbed to his injuries.

While upgrading natural gas lines for Peoples Gas as a subcontractor, an employer was using a Vacmasters System 4000 vacuum truck to remove soil from excavations. The truck's spoil tank detached from the frame, pinning an employee beneath it. Despite efforts to free the employee using excavating equipment, they were pronounced dead at a local hospital. Coworkers witnessed and assisted in the tragic incident.
An employer was working from a ladder to cut palm fronds, when he feel 18 feet, striking his head on the pool deck below. The worker died as a result of his injury.

During the installation of a tress for a second story addition on a residential building, an employer fell to the ground and died after losing his footing while removing a nail from a hip rafter to reset its height. The addition was being constructed above the garage of the house at the time of the incident.
An employing was playing basketball with a metnally disabled client.  The employee collapsed to the ground and died.
An emplyee was operating a clam shell machine. The employee became caught in the machine and his head and chest were crushed. The employee was killed from his injuries.

Two employees from a temporary staffing agency were assigned to work at a construction site. Employee #1 expressed concern about Employee #2's previous poor work performance at the site, leading to a confrontation and physical altercation. Employee #1 ended up stabbing Employee #2, resulting in Employee #2's death due to a stab wound to the heart.

During the installation of a new sewer line, an excavating employee was working in an improperly shored excavation that was 10 feet deep. While positioned in between two pieces of shoring spaced 15 feet apart, the wall collapsed, burying the employee under 6 feet of dirt and resulting in a fatal accident.
An explosion occurred at a work-site causing significant structural damage to building and an employee hospitalization.

An explosion caused by a natural gas leak occurred in a building, resulting in emergency services being called to respond. Three firemen, two policemen, and two civilians arrived at the scene. Six of those who responded sustained minor injuries, while one fireman suffered two broken legs and was hospitalized for treatment.

A foreman employee was preparing a large fan for removal on the Cooling Tower Fan Deck when he was crushed by the fan and killed. He had been using a wrench to remove bolts from the fan's vertical shaft when the incident occurred. Materials to block and sling the fan were supposed to be brought up from the ground.

A fatal incident occurred at a fabrication yard when a steel staircase being offloaded from a forklift shifted unexpectedly, causing an employee to be struck and pinned between the staircase and a fork on the lift. Despite the prompt arrival of emergency responders, the employee was pronounced dead at the scene.

An independent contractor sound engineer was recording sound for a video production.  The contractor was found unresponsive in the restroom.  The cause of the medical episode was a pre-existing health condition.

An industrial truck was being refueled with propane when the hose leaked and a fire started.  Employee #1 attempted to move the forklift when it exploded into flames.  Employee #1 was hospitalized with burns to his arms, legs and face.

The interior finishing carpenter was installing ceiling beams from a mobile scaffold when he fell through the side due to missing cross braces and guardrails. He landed on the main floor of the living room and was taken to the hospital where he later passed away 18 days later from his injuries.

An ironworker was installing steel decking on a newly constructed commercial building. During the decking operations the employee fell approximately 40 feet to the ground. The employee died as a result of his injuries.
An office worker was killed in a fire. Workers in the building were alerted of a fire on the third floor of the building and were evacuated. However, one worker died of smoke inhalation.
An officer (employee) reported he was chasing three suspects. The employee was shot during pursuit, and it was later determined it was a suicide. No other details were given on the shooting.

During a race under caution, a safety crew member was directing traffic near turn 2 on the racetrack when a car unexpectedly left the single-file line and struck the employee. Tragically, the employee suffered fatal injuries to the head and body system as a result of the impact.

An employee was killed during a pump maintenance operation after a pressure blast blew out the right side of the pump, causing the employee to be struck and smashed into an adjacent concrete block wall. The incident occurred after the maintenance mechanics had completed the first line break, resulting in hot PET monomer spilling onto the floor and solidifying. The employee had already locked out the necessary valves and a Safe Work Permit was issued prior to the incident.

An operator of an excavator was clearing trees and brush from a drainage ditch to level and install a drain pipe. A tree fell on the cab of the excavator he was driving. The operator sustained head injuries and was killed.

While changing the wheel studs on a trailer, the owner and an employee used a cutting torch to remove stubborn studs, which ignited oil and oil absorbent on the floor. Despite attempts to extinguish the small fire with a fire extinguisher, it continued to spread. In a unfortunate turn of events, the employee became trapped under the truck and was tragically killed by the rear brake booster as the truck passed over him.
An supervising employee was feeling bad and died from suspected cardiovascular problem.

An was employee operating a tractor to clear trees and tree limbs from a path/road. The employee was pushing limbs with the tractor, when another tree limb fell and struck the employee in the head. The employee was killed from blunt force trauma to the head.
And appeared to be trembling with his arms and legs shaking when he saw him after work. The employee died from an unknown cause and not other details were specified.

The employee was working on repairing a roof leak with two coworkers when he realized he needed a caulking gun from the first repair. Upon returning to the first repair site, the employee accidentally stepped through a fiberglass panel skylight and fell 14 feet to the concrete floor below, resulting in his death.
And employee had set chokers on a log. As the turn broke out the log, the turn struck and killed the employee.

The employee tragically jumped head first off a 5 story roof after climbing out of a window and climbing a safety ladder from a nearby building. The employee sustained severe head and chest trauma, resulting in his death.

The employee of a landscape trucking company was operating a John Deere Tractor with a Howard Rotavator attachment to aerate a large dirt mound. The tractor rolled over the sloped edge of the mound, resulting in the employee's tragic death.

24 individuals were on their way to Ameriqual Foods for their second shift in a 1994 Dodge van designed for 16 passengers. Unfortunately, one of the tires blew out near the Fort Branch exit on I-69, causing the van to roll over multiple times. The van, not owned by the company, had three worn-out tires with signs of dry rot and a piece of wood serving as a rear bumper. Employee #1 was pronounced dead at the scene, while Employee #2 passed
As a result of sepsis. sepsis.
As an employee was applying stucco on a residential construction site. He slipped and fell from a 6-1/2 foot high scaffold and sustained a dislocated shoulder.
At 12:00 a.m., an employee was pumping produced water from a tank battery into the tank on his truck. The employee was found dead near his vehicle. He died of a heart attack.

At 2:00 p.m., an Employee was working from a swing stage scaffold when painting the exterior wall of a building when the scaffold fell to the ground. The employee fell along with the scaffold and was killed. and was killed.
At 3:00 p.m. an employee was trimming a tree when he was struck and killed by a tree limb.

At 3:00 p.m., an employee fell into a hole/depression while working alone. He called for help and coworkers responded, finding him complaining of back pain. Emergency services arrived and attempted CPR, but the employee died due to an internal hemorrhage shortly after.
At 3:30 p.m., an employee was found kneeling and unconscious by an orange tree.  The employee was working in an orange grove undergoing harvesting and died of unknown causes.

Employee #1, an experienced framer, was working with a co-worker to install wooden floor trusses on the 4th floor of an apartment complex. Despite being issued a 3 foot lanyard and lifeline rope, Employee #1 fell approximately 36 feet to the ground while attempting to reconnect himself to another anchor point. He suffered severe blunt force trauma to the chest and ultimately succumbed to his injuries.

At around 10:45 a.m., a 45-year-old employee and his co-worker were cutting a concrete wall to create a double door opening. After finishing the cut and handing the saw to his co-worker, the wall collapsed on the employee, causing fatal head and body injuries. He was taken to a nearby hospital where he was pronounced dead.

Employee #1 tragically fell through a floor opening on a mezzanine while counting ductwork, resulting in his death due to severe head injuries. The floor opening was 40 inches wide by 10 feet long and was marked with red caution tape around steel beams, but unfortunately Employee #1 fell through.

Around 5:00 PM, an employee at a steel mill facility was replacing a hydraulic cylinder for an electrode arm on the Ladle Metallurgy System. The 16-foot electrode arm weighed around 800 pounds when filled with hydraulic fluid. While cutting a metal piece from the arm, it detached and fell, striking the employee on the head. Tragically, the employee sustained a lacerated brain injury and fractured skull, resulting in their death.

Employee #1 tripped on a plastic pallet placed near the entrance to the transportation/security office while walking to the kitchen. The pallet, measuring 24" x 48" x 3", had boxes of documents on top of it and was not visible to employees entering the office. Employee #1 sustained a broken bone in the left foot, pain in the left side of the back, and bruises on the left side of the body as a result of the fall. The pallet had been placed there

Two employees were hit by a car while preparing to install a fire hydrant on the side of the road. Employee #1 was struck, landed on the hood of the car, and was ultimately killed when the car hit a utility pole. Employee #2 was also hit and sustained injuries to the head and leg, requiring hospitalization. The third employee narrowly avoided being hit by the car.
Electricians were trouble shooting switch gear. An arc blast/flash occurred. One employee sustained an electrical shock and burns to the face.
Employed #1 was backing his truck down a ramp to position it underneath a hopper to collect limestone from a barge.  He lost control of the truck and backed into the river and Employee #1 drowned.

Employee #1 and coworkers were working on a two lane highway, with two coworkers installing epoxy and reflectors in the center while Employee #1 was flagging traffic in a mobile work zone. Employee #1 was struck by a vehicle in the southbound lane, thrown into the northbound lane, and then struck by a second vehicle. Tragically, Employee #1 sustained fatal injuries from the incident.

While setting up a work zone to clean a bridge, a utility trailer became unhitched and struck a KYTC vehicle, pinning Employee #2 between the truck and the bridge barrier wall. Employee #1 was knocked over the barrier and fell into the creek below, resulting in his death. Employee #2 was eventually extracted and taken to the hospital where he recovered from his injuries.

Employee #1 and two co-workers were unloading 24 palm trees from a trailer using a Caterpillar skid steer at an ocean-side resort. Each tree weighed 2,000 pounds and measured 19 feet long. Employee #1 was wrapping a strap around the trees when one of them came free, catching his foot and causing him to fall four feet to the ground, where he was crushed by the tree and suffered a fatal head injury.

Employee #1, a construction laborer, was struck in the head by an excavator bucket while working on a drainage pipe installation at a residential construction site. The excavator operator did not have a clear view of Employee #1 as he swung the boom to pick up another bucket of soil, resulting in the fatal accident. Employee #1 was pronounced dead at the scene by emergency personnel.

Employee #1 and Employee #2 were part of a tree-trimming crew at a residential home, with Employee #1 feeding limbs into a wood chipper and Employee #2 trimming limbs. When Employee #2 heard a strange noise and saw smoke coming from the chipper, he discovered Employee #1 was caught in it. Employee #2 managed to retrieve Employee #1's body from the chipper but suffered a heart attack in the process. Employee #1 was pronounced dead at the scene, and

Employee #1 and coworkers were working in a multi-level building installing precast concrete planks when a plank being delivered struck the one Employee #1 was standing on. He was ejected from the first floor, and the plank landed on top of him, resulting in multiple injuries. He was taken to the hospital where he later passed away.

Employee #1 was performing maintenance on a conveyor belt with a coworker. After completing the gearbox replacement and starting the belt for testing, Employee #1 went to the control box 250 feet away. When the coworker did not receive a response from him over the radio, they shut off the belt and found Employee #1 crushed and killed underneath the conveyor system.

During training, Employee #2 accidentally backed the semi-trailer truck into Employee #1, causing fatal injuries. Employee #2 called for emergency assistance, but Employee #1 passed away at the hospital from severe injuries sustained in the incident.
