Employee #1 and #2 were working in a trench at a depth of 11 feet and 11 inches when the walls suddenly collapsed and a fire hydrant became dislodged, burying them in soil. Both employees tragically lost their lives as a result of the engulfment.

Employee #1 and #2 were removing a carrier wheel from an amusement park ride using a maintenance cart. The cart began to fall when Employee #2 moved, causing a shift in the load. Both employees were arrested by their personal fall protection equipment, but the cart's suspend pole failed, leading to Employee #1 being struck in the head and killed. Employee #2 sustained abrasions and contusions.

Employee #1 and #2 were working from a carpenter's bracket scaffolding, when it suddenly pulled off causing both employees to fall 16 feet to the ground. Both employees suffered unspecified broken bones and were hospitalized for treatment.

Employee #1 and 43 coworkers were participating in physical training with a local police academy. The training, held in a hot and humid outdoor area, included an obstacle course. Despite dangerous conditions, no water breaks were provided and an AED was not onsite. Employee #1 collapsed and died from apparent heat-related complications.

Employee #1 and a co-worker were installing grated steel decking on a maintenance platform at a feed mill facility. Employee #1 fell 24 feet to a steel scale platform below, breaking three ribs and puncturing his lung. Both employees were wearing body harnesses with six-foot lanyards but had not tied off.

While operating a lamination machine, Employee #1 stepped over the emergency stop cord and raised his hands above his head, causing them to come into contact with the machine's moving roller. He was pulled into the roller but was freed by a co-worker who stopped the machine. Emergency services were contacted, and Employee #1 was taken to the hospital where he passed away six hours later due to internal bleeding.

Employee #1 and a co-worker were performing flag duties at a road construction site when a commercial garbage truck failed to stop, causing a chain reaction crash. The garbage truck swerved out of control, striking and killing Employee #1 who was signaling east bound traffic.

Employee #1 and a co-worker were riding in an MTV after spraying weeds. Employee #1 lost control of the vehicle on a steep hill, causing it to crash into two trees. The co-worker managed to jump out before the crash, but Employee #1 suffered fatal head and neck injuries.

Employee #1 and a co-worker were working inside an excavation spreading out gravel, when the excavator operator mistakenly lowered the digger/bucket into the excavation, striking Employee #1 on the head and crushing him to death. The depth of the excavation was over 15 feet, leading to the tragic incident.

Employee #1 and a co-worker were attempting to access the battery of a Holland Skid Steer that had failed by releasing the locking mechanism on the lift arms. While the co-worker used a Hyundai forklift with a 400 pound jib attached to elevate the lift arms, Employee #1 maneuvered the skid steer. Unfortunately, the skid steer began to rotate backwards, causing the front plate on the lift arms to slide off the jib and crush Employee #1, resulting in

Employee #1 and a coworker finished replacing a generator at a communications tower. As Employee #1 exited his vehicle, he had a coughing spasm and walked behind a Dodge 3500 pickup. The driver did not see him and accidentally backed up, resulting in the tragic death of Employee #1.
Employee #1 fell from a ladder while trying to reach a spot on a drywall sheet during an office renovation project, resulting in fractured ribs and hospitalization.

Employee #1 and a coworker were changing out an electric motor on a fruit bin dumper.  Employee #1 released the drive chain and the carriage fell and his leg was caught between the frame and the carriage.  Employee #1's leg was fractured and he was hospitalized.

Employee #1 was cleaning a rotating table on a cup filler machine when her coworker inadvertently activated the machine, causing the heat sealant to amputate her right index finger. She was rushed to a medical center for treatment and was subsequently hospitalized.

Employee #1 and a coworker were operating a wood chipper to clean up limbs near power lines when Employee #1's left hand was caught in the feed wheels of the machine. The employee suffered a traumatic amputation of his hand at the wrist, as well as lacerations to his face and ear.

Employee #1 and a coworker were boarding up windows at a fire-damaged residential home. While working on a sloped area, Employee #1 fell from an eight foot ladder, sustaining a head laceration and four fractured places in his left shoulder. Employee #1 was injured while trying to get a well head back on line by operating a valve that had cross-threaded threads, causing it to break and strike him in the hip. He was hospitalized with a fractured hip and laceration above his ear.

Employee #1 was trying to remove aluminum dust/debris from the die of a 35-ton trim press. The four post hydraulic trim press malfunctioned and cycled. The employee sustained a crushing injury to his left thumb and an amputation of his left middle finger.
Employee #1 was trying to remove an unlawful driver from inside a cab of an ambulance.  Employee #1 was thrown to the ground and run over.  Employee #1 was killed.

Employee #1 was troubleshooting a system error in a storage freezer when he fell approximately 24 feet from a catwalk to the floor below. Despite keyed interlock gates preventing access to the open edge, the employee somehow fell. His injuries included a broken hip and internal bleeding, and he did not survive.

Employee #1 was trying to unjam a rotational molding machine when his fingers were caught in the pulley on the end of the track.  He suffered a laceration and partial amputation to his last two fingers on his right hand and was hospitalized.

Employee #1 was trying to unjam capsules in a standalone rectifier as she had seen the lead teach her. The machine was still energized and the reciprocating part came down and crushed her fingers.  Employee #1 suffered fractured middle fingers and perforated index fingers but was not hospitalized.
Employee #1 was trying to unplug a chute used to load screened corn into a grain trailer.  He fell or was pulled into the loading chute and died of suffocation.

Employee #1 was under a mobile home helping to set up the home on stacked concrete blocks. A pier of blocks near Employee #1 began to shift to the side.  He attempted to crawl out from under the mobile home but only got out partially before the mobile home fell on him. Employee #1 died.
Employee #1 was underneath a sanitation truck adjusting the brakes. The truck rolled over Employee #1, killing him.

Employee #1 was killed when he was pinned under the wheels of a truck while unhitching an empty cargo trailer. The employee had not applied the parking brake, causing the truck to roll forward as he was disconnecting the trailer. The accident occurred when Employee #1 pulled the retaining pin to release the trailer from the truck.

Employee #1 was unhooking a lowboy trailer. The employee removed the 2 axle extensions and put the locking pin back in place. The locking pin, however, was not fully engaged and the equipment dropped on Employee #1's head, killing him.

Employee #1 was using a forklift to unload a large container from a pickup truck at a loading dock. He positioned himself between the container and the forklift, which was on a slight incline with the engine running and the parking brake off. The forklift unexpectedly moved onto the pickup truck bed, crushing Employee #1's chest and head between the forklift mast and the container, resulting in his death.

Employee #1 was unloading boxes from a semi-trailer when an unknown number of boxes fell on him, causing blunt force trauma to his chest. Although he initially reported being okay, he later informed his supervisor that he wasn't feeling well and went to the hospital. It was discovered that he had pneumonia, a heart condition, and had been struck by boxes. Employee #1 underwent heart surgery but unfortunately passed away approximately 2 weeks later.
Employee #1 was unloading Christmas trees from a stake bed trailer. He was pulling the twine loose when he lost his balance and fell.  Employee #1 fractured his neck and is killed.
Employee #1 was unloading concrete lined pipe off of a truck.  A pipe fell and struck Employee #1 who was hospitalized and died the next day.. .

Employee #1 was unloading material from a steel conex container. As he worked, material fell on him pinning him against the steel conex wall. The employee was killed when the material crushed his upper body, including his chest and abdomen.

Employee #1 was unloading plywood sheets off of a conveyor. The employee's left hand got caught between the conveyor belt and the fixture holding the spring-loaded conveyor wheel, amputating his left ring finger.

Employee #1 was unloading the dishwasher when it unexpectedly turned back on. The employee jumped away from the dishwasher, hitting his back against the counter behind him. Employee #1 experienced extreme back pain and later died.

Employee #1 was up in a tree, trying to secure himself and the saddle, so that he could begin to trim the branches. The loop on his saddle failed. The employee fell to the ground and broke his ankle and injured his ribs.

Employee #1 was injured while using a 3-roll bending machine to bend metal into a circle. His left hand was pulled into the rollers up to the middle of his forearm, causing crushing injuries that required surgery and hospitalization. A coworker heard his screams and helped to stop the machine, allowing him to remove his arm.
Employee #1 was using a band saw to cut a bone-in ham. While cutting the ham, the meat rolled and the employee cut off the tip of his right thumb.

Employee #1 was using a band saw to remove the heads from catfish. The employee was not wearing the required PPE (chain gloves). Employee #1 was either not paying attention or working too fast, and struck the band saw blade, severing his left thumb to the first knuckle.

Employee #1, who was not properly trained, had his right index finger amputated while using a bending machine to bend rebar. The machine lacked adequate guarding and could only be stopped by completing the cycle or using the emergency stop switch. Thankfully, Employee #1 did not require hospitalization.

Employee #1 was using a bucket truck aerial device to lift a section of a spruce tree, however the weight of the operator and tree section exceeded the weight limit of the unit causing it to tip over. Despite being connected to the bucket with a safety belt and lanyard, Employee #1 was pinned to the ground when the bucket rotated upon impact. Tragically, the force of the incident resulted in multiple fractures and lacerations, ultimately leading to his death.
Employee #1 fell from a rooftop while taking photos with a camera, resulting in a fractured arm and ankle. He was taken to a medical center for treatment and was later hospitalized.

Employee #1 was using a chain to tow a vehicle. A coworker was operating the John Deere Loader to pull the vehicle. The coworker activated the quick release on the pin disconnect button and the pin caught Employee #1's left hand index finger, amputating it.

Employee #1 was using a chainsaw to cut down trees. His climbing rope was in front of the tree when the tree fell bringing the rope and Employee #1 down.  Employee #1 was crushed and killed by the falling tree.

Employee #1 was using a circular saw to cut a sheet of 3/4 in. particleboard when the saw kicked back, amputating the top half of his left pinkie finger. He was taken to a medical center for treatment and later discharged.

Employee #1 was using a clamp truck to stack large rolls of non-woven fabric in a storage area, as instructed by the warehouse lead. However, Employee #1 placed the rolls in the wrong location, causing them to topple over when he backed out with the clamp truck. While trying to stand the rolls back up, they fell and struck Employee #1 in the head, resulting in hospitalization and eventually his death.

Employee #1 was fatally injured while using a cutting torch on a garbage truck's hydraulic system. The housing compartment was not secured, causing it to fall and crush him. There were no safety measures in place to prevent this tragic accident.

Employee #1 was operating a forklift when he accidentally turned the wheel the wrong way, causing the forklift to swing towards the storage rack. In an attempt to stop the forklift, his left hand got caught between the forklift and the rack, resulting in fractures and lacerations. He was hospitalized and received treatment for his injuries.

Employee #1 was using a high speed mixer to mix hair care products. The employee sustained burns to his upper torso and face when the hot liquids from the mixer struck him on his upper torso and face. Employee #1 was hospitalized for second degree burns to his back, arms, and face.

Employee #1 was injured while using a nail gun to tack rafters in a residential home. A nail ricocheted off another object and pierced through his nostril, lodging behind his right eye. The employee required hospitalization for his injuries.

Employee #1 was using a Hobart band saw to cut frozen meat when she accidentally amputated a section of her pinky and ring finger. The guard on the band saw was not in use or adjusted to the meat height, causing the meat to move and the employee to pass her finger through the saw. She was hospitalized and treated for her injuries, which also included cutting into, but not amputating, the middle finger of her right hand.
Employee #1 was using a ladder. The employee fell from the ladder and was struck by it. Employee #1 sustained a contusion to his neck, scrapes to his finger and a bruise to his leg.

Employee #1 was using a loader to clean up driveways and intersections behind a snow blower. The shoot of the snow blower became clogged, so the employee went over to it to remove the snow.  His right foot fell into the impeller, causing a partial amputation to his right foot.

While installing hardwood flooring at a private residence, Employee #1 was operating a manual-fed electric table saw in the backyard. Unfortunately, his left hand made contact with the saw blade, resulting in the amputation of his left thumb, index, and middle fingers, as well as nerve damage to his ring finger. Employee #1 was hospitalized and underwent surgery to reattach his thumb and middle finger.
Employee #1 was using a meat slicer. He was wearing gloves and slicing ham. The employee's glove got caught in the blade, and his left thumb tip was amputated.

Employee #1 was using a MIG welder to repair a leak on a locomotive diesel fuel tank when the tank exploded. The employee suffered burns over 95% of his body and unfortunately passed away the next day due to his injuries. The tank contained hazardous chemicals, making the situation even more dangerous.

Employee #1 was using a band saw to dismantle a small pallet when the pallet suddenly kicked back, causing their right hand to make contact with the blade. This resulted in lacerations to the little and index fingers of their right hand.
Employee #1 was using a pendant control to move and store a die, weighing 12 tons. He was killed when crushed between two dies.

Employee #1 was using a pipe cutting saw to cut a section of 8 inch cast iron pipe when the pipe dropped slightly, causing the saw to bind and kick back. In the process of trying to control the saw, he accidentally cut his own neck, severing his carotid artery and esophagus. Despite immediate medical attention, Employee #1 unfortunately succumbed to his injuries and died as a result of the accident.
Employee #1 was using a pitch fork to spread mulch when he collapsed and died due to a heart attack.

Employee #1 was using a plasma torch to cut the top off a drum that contained old brake fluid.  He was found unconscious but breathing with the plasma torch still operating in his hand. Employee #1 was hospitalized and died on June 16, 2017.

Employee #1 was using a Powermatic belt/disc sander to sand metal parts when his glove got caught in the machine, resulting in lacerations to two fingers and the amputation of the tip of his left thumb. The incident occurred when he raised the metal part to increase contact with the abrasive wheel, causing it to be pulled towards the table.

Employee #1 was operating a press brake to bend parts when he lost his balance and accidentally placed his right hand in the machine dies, resulting in the amputation of his right index and middle fingertips. He did not require hospitalization for the injury.

Employee #1 was using a pressure washer to clean support angles inside a cargo tank when he tripped and fell, causing the pressure washer to strike his right leg and create a deep laceration. He was hospitalized after receiving treatment at a medical center.

Employee #1 was tragically found drowned in a hole filled with water while attempting to hand trace a trace wire for a pipeline using a sand spade. The hole was 47 inches deep, and he slipped in head first, unable to push himself out. Despite efforts to rescue him, he did not survive.

Employee #1 fell and hit his head in a restroom, but no one saw the incident happen. Despite a thorough inspection showing no hazards, he was still transported to the hospital. Later that day, he had seizures at home and had to be readmitted to the hospital for over 24 hours for further treatment.
Employee #1 was using a table saw without a guard. The employee cut off his fingers with the saw.

Employee #1 was using a torch to cut out material for a water filtration system. As he took a break and while resting, he collapsed and became unresponsive. Employee #1 was transported to a medical center, where he died. The cause of death was due to a possible heart attack.

Employee #1 was injured while using a tree branch to remove debris from a wood chipper. The tree branch was grabbed by the drum and pulled into the chipper, causing the employee to hit his hand on the opened lid. He suffered lacerations and broken bones in his right hand pinky finger and had to be hospitalized.
Employee #1 was using a welding type gouging rod to cut and remove the top of a sealed 3 phase transformer. Combustible gases within the transformer ignited and exploded, and Employee #1 was killed.

Employee #1 was using a forklift to load Gaylord containers into a box truck for recycling. The forklift fell out of the truck, pinning him and causing fatal injuries. It is believed that the box truck may have shifted or tipped during the incident.

During a label change, Employee #1's right hand was pulled into a rotating ink roller after the acetone rag or glove he was using got caught in the machinery. The employee suffered severe damage to the soft tissue on his right hand and needed skin grafts and vessel transplants as a result of the incident.

Employee #1 was operating a four-wheeler while spraying weeds on rough terrain with a slight grade. The vehicle tipped over and pinned him to the ground, resulting in his death as he was unable to free himself from underneath it.

Employee #1 was using an AMFEC 510 mixer to mix and cool the product for packaging. When trying to push the product out through the exit doors using the rotating paddle, the employee lifted his hands off the controls to wipe product off the door. His right middle finger got caught in the rotating paddle, resulting in an amputation of the first digit. Employee #1 did not require hospitalization.

Employee #1 was removing the steel top cover of a natural gas fuel filtration skid using an eight foot A-frame ladder when the cover exploded and struck him. The employee did not follow proper safety procedures by locking out/tagging out or de-energizing/purging the vessel before starting the maintenance work. As a result, the employee suffered blunt force trauma, leading to the complete amputation of both arms and ultimately causing his death.

Employee #1 was injured while operating a machine that involved releasing air from a roll. His right index finger got caught between the shaft and the roll core, resulting in the amputation of his fingertip. He was hospitalized as a result of the incident.

Employee #1 was attempting to unclog a hopper filled with feathers using pressurized hot steam when the pressure blew him off the auger, causing him to fall 10 feet to the cement floor below. As a result, he sustained a fracture to his forehead and first and second degree burns.

Employee #1 was injured while using the chamfer press to work on clevis parts. His ponytail became caught in the rotating spindle of the press, resulting in severe scalping and partial ear and cheek injuries. The accident occurred due to lack of a guard on the press and there were no immediate witnesses to the incident.

While using the Eubanks tube cutting machine, Employee #1 attempted to release clumped plastic tubing by tapping the metal chute to discharge static electricity. In the process of sweeping the cut tubing away from the machine, her right index finger entered the point of operations, resulting in the amputation of the pad of her finger.

While using the hydraulic brake press to bend metal, Employee #1 accidentally crushed his left ring fingertip in the second bend slot. Despite wearing protective rubber gloves, he did not realize his finger was in the way when activating the machine. The incident resulted in the amputation of his fingertip.

Employee #1 was using the printer to print "JPL" on the duct work. The tape on the machine was becoming loose, so the employee tried to press it down while the machine was running. Employee #1's ring finger tip was amputated.

Employee #1 was vacuuming water out of a casement pvc pipe, that was around a bridge pylon support in preparation for pouring of cement.  A vehicle, a Ford Bronco, crashed through the barricades and traveled 60 foot in the air and struck Employee #1, killing him.

Employee #1 was waiting for an elevator. As he waited, he lost consciousness and fainted. Employee #1 fall and struck his head upon the floor. He sustained unspecified head injuries. Employee #1 was transported to a medical center, where he received treatment and was then hospitalized.
Employee #1 was waiting on an oversized load to remove cones.  Employee #1 was killed when a construction vehicle backed up and ran over him.

Employee #1 was operating a pallet jack when it collided with another stationary pallet jack in a warehouse setting. In an attempt to avoid further collision, Employee #1 jumped onto the deck of his own jack, resulting in his right foot being crushed between the two machines. Fortunately, Employee #1 did not require hospitalization for the injury.
Employee #1 was walking adjacent to an exhaust fan. The blade of the fan was unguarded.The employee's hand came into contact with the fan blades and his index finger was amputated.

Employee #1 was struck by an industrial powered forklift truck carrying two bins of onions while walking in front of a semi-truck. He suffered unspecified injuries and was transported to a medical center for treatment and hospitalization.

Employee #1 was walking backwards while handling a big box. The employee tripped on a pallet jack that was not secured in place, and fell onto the concrete floor. Employee #1 sustained a fracture to his left wrist.

Employee #1 was walking counter clockwise on the safety lane beside the raceway. The employee was struck in the chest and head by the extended right edge of the starting gate vehicle that was moving clockwise on the raceway. He was killed from the injuries that he sustained.
Employee #1 was walking down an isle in a warehouse. A double stacked skid of air conditioning motors, weighing 11 pounds, fell and struck Employee #1 on the head, resulting in fatal head injury.

Employee #1 was struck by a Nissan forklift in a parking lot, causing his left foot to become wedged between the pallet and the floor. He fell and rolled approximately 3 feet away from the forklift, sustaining fractures to his left ankle and shoulder. He was hospitalized for his injuries.

Employee #1 attempted to jump onto a trailer being pulled by a farm tractor but lost his balance and fell off, with the trailer subsequently running over his right leg. He sustained a smashed leg, bruises, and scrapes, resulting in hospitalization.

Employee #1 was walking in a parking lot. While he was walking, he slipped on ice and fell. Employee #1 struck his head against the ground and suffered an unspecified head injury. Employee #1 was transported to a medical center, where he received treatment and was then hospitalized.
Employee #1 was walking in the parking lot/driveway area. The employee was struck and run over by a 2010 F-350 super duty pickup truck. He sustained crushing injuries to his torso and was killed.

Employee #1 was walking on a beam at a rig when the air-driven oil pumping unit engaged, causing the beam to move upward quickly. He was not connected to an anchor point with his safety harness and fell approximately 17 ft, resulting in fatal injuries.
Employee #1 was walking on a plank, missed a step and fell hitting his head.  The employee sustained a head injury.

Employee #1 was walking on the roof of a three story apartment building under construction without fall protection. He stepped on a piece of metal edging that was not secured and he slid off the roof to the ground below, and was killed.

During the incident, Employee #1 fell through a hole in the roof while walking on it. The temporary wood decking was not in place on certain areas, and the markings indicating the holes were washed away by rain. Employee #1, who had just returned from a previous injury, was unaware of the holes and tragically fell through, resulting in fatal injuries.

Employee #1 was injured when Employee #2, operating a standup forklift, failed to honk the horn or look before making a U-turn, resulting in Employee #1's right foot being run over. Employee #1 sustained two broken toes as a result of the incident.

Employee #1 was walking out of the aisles toward the front dock at building D2 and Employee #2 was downsizing pallets using a stand-up forklift. Employee #2 made a U-turn with the forklift. Employee #1 was run over by the forklift and sustained multiple fractures of his right toes.

Employee #1 was feeding chickens outside when he complained of chest pains and stepped away to make a phone call for help. When his coworker couldn't find him, he discovered Employee #1 unresponsive on the ground, having suffered a suspected heart attack. Tragically, Employee #1 passed away as a result of the incident.
Employee #1 was walking past a stack of baled recycled plastics, weighing approximately 900 pounds.  A bale fell over and struck Employee #1, killing him.
Employee #1 was walking the work site that was being graded and he was struck and killed by a Maintainer truck.

Employee #1 was walking through the jobsite. There was a bulldozer that was backing up. The employee was struck by the bulldozer and his right leg was crushed and his hip was dislocated. He was hospitalized.

Employee #1 was walking to a golf cart in the yard when he suddenly fainted, fell, and became unconscious. The fall resulted in a fractured skull, internal head injuries, and internal bleeding, ultimately leading to his death. It was later discovered that he may have had pre-existing health issues.

Employee #1 was walking to his truck when he suddenly experienced breathing difficulties and lost consciousness. Emergency medical services were called and he was transported to a hospital, where he ultimately passed away from cardiac arrest. The autopsy revealed that he died from a heart attack caused by blocked arteries and an enlarged heart.
Employee #1 was walking to the bathroom. A tree limb broke from a tree due to snow and high winds, and fell on the employee. Employee #1 was struck in the head and killed.

Employee #1 was walking towards a belt man lift as 2 coworkers were pulling in to park on the 6th floor. The coworkers heard a noise and went to the lift opening and yelled for Employee #1 but there was no response. Employee #1 was found below dead.

Employee #1 was caught between a swinging ram and a forging hammer while attempting to change out a key/drift pin. Despite giving signals to place the ram on the ground, the crane operator misunderstood and continued swinging it towards the forging hammer. A coworker saw the danger and pushed Employee #1 out of the way, but he still suffered a fractured left femur and required surgical treatment at a medical center.

Employee #1 was walking up an exterior staircase at a single family residence. The decking collapsed and Employee #1 fell, landing on the ground, fracturing his hip.  The employee later died from the injury.
Employee #1 was walking when he was struck by a powered industrial truck.  Employee #1 was hospitalized and treated for a fractured leg.
Employee #1 was washing dishes. As she worked, Employee #1 fainted and fell. She was transported to a medical center and later died from a blood clot in her heart.
Employee #1 was washing or preparing to wash out the hopper on his truck. As he worked, his truck ran over and killed him. One of the truck's wheels caused multiple injuries over his body.

Employee #1 was cleaning the inside of a polenta filler machine while it was running. After finishing, he began wiping down the outside of the equipment without realizing it was still running. As he tried to remove something from the bottom opening, his left middle finger was caught, resulting in a laceration and distal tip amputation. Employee #1 did not require hospitalization.

Employee #1 was watching a coworker cut down a tree. As the tree was cut, a hanger tree slid down, breaking off a large limb from the hanger tree stump. The tree limb fell, striking Employee #1 and fracturing four of his vertebrae. The employee was hospitalized for his injuries.

Employee #1 was watering plants when he stubbed his toe on a cinder block, causing him to fall and fracturing his hip. He was hospitalized and underwent surgery, but unfortunately, he succumbed to his injuries and complications during the procedure.

Employee #1 was wearing plastic gloves, using an oil can to oil a chain and gear. The machine was energized and the guard was off. The glove and finger of the employee got caught in the nip point at the gear, amputating his fingertip.
Employee #1 was welding and he was found dead. Death was determined to be non-work related.
Employee #1 was welding on a boat dock when he was electrocuted.

Employee #1 welded together eleven pieces to create an intermediate product. After finishing the welding, Employee #1 used an angle grinder without a guard to clean the flange and inlet. The angle grinder kicked back, cutting Employee #1's leg while he was using it in an incorrect position between his legs upside down.

Employee #1 was struck by a tree in his mid-section while retrieving his chainsaw near a skidder during a tree-cutting operation. Despite being airlifted to a local hospital, he tragically passed away on September 21, 2015.

Employee #1 was working on a sheet metal piece when his right middle finger got caught in a pinch point between the worktable and the metal piece, resulting in the amputation of his fingertip. He was promptly taken to a medical center for treatment and was later discharged.

While working alone in the basement of a residential rental property, Employee #1 was standing on an unstable A-frame ladder attempting to fix wiring on an electrical junction box. The ladder was not secured and began to slip, causing Employee #1 to jump off in an attempt to prevent falling. Unfortunately, his wedding ring caught on a screw, resulting in the amputation of his finger.

While hanging drywall from a mobile scaffold inside a building, Employee #1 fell approximately 5.7 feet to the concrete floor, causing severe head injuries. Despite emergency medical services being called, Employee #1 passed away at the hospital from craniocerebral injuries.

Employee #1, a full-time employee for a framing contractor, was at a new residential construction site in Phase 3, working on the ground level. While pushing a wheel barrel air compressor, he was struck by a coworker driving a forklift. The backup alarm of the forklift was sounding, but the coworker did not see Employee #1. Employee #1 sustained serious leg fractures and required hospitalization for over 24 hours as a result of the incident. The employer reported

Employee #1 was working as a mason tender on a hot and humid day for 10 hours without a break. He provided 30 pound concrete blocks and motor to the masons on a scaffold.  Employee #1 died from heat exhaustion.
Employee #1 was working as a sewing machine operator when she suffered a heart attack and died. The company failed to report the incident in the allotted time frame.

Employee #1 was part of a tree trimming crew when a tragic accident occurred. While on the ground manning a rigging rope, he positioned himself below a limb being cut by a coworker in a tree. Despite being warned by other coworkers, Employee #1 was struck by the falling limb and tragically passed away while being transported to the hospital.

Employee #1 was struck by a vehicle at a car wash facility, resulting in a partial amputation of both legs. Despite being admitted to the hospital for treatment, the worker tragically passed away the following day due to his injuries.

Employee #1 was killed while putting a plug in a spill bucket at a gas station. He was on his hands and knees wearing a reflective vest and placing cones when a customer in a truck did not see him and ran him over.

Employee #1 was found unresponsive while working in the shipping and receiving area of a grocery distribution facility, where he was stacking packages of grapes onto pallets. Despite coworkers' efforts to administer CPR, Employee #1 passed away at the hospital due to a suspected heart attack.

Employee #1 was working in a packaging room for Eryngii mushrooms at a jobsite. While cleaning the waist-high set rollers on the conveyor, her towel got caught in the unguarded chain and sprocket drive underneath. In an attempt to free the towel, her left middle finger was partially amputated. The incident was caused by the unguarded machinery, failure to use lockout/tagout procedures, and wearing gloves in an area with entanglement hazards.

Employee #1 was troubleshooting a conveyor that had stopped working at a manufacturing facility when he was found unconscious and lying under the conveyor by his co-workers. A screwdriver, flashlight, and an unplugged 460-volt cord were found near him, and it was determined that he was electrocuted by the still energized cord.
Employee #1 was working at a tire company. The employee was using an incorrect position during a change over and was caught between equipment and killed.
Employee #1 was struck by a loaded Toyota Electric Forklift driven by Employee #2 while transporting a rebuilt case of beer. Employee #1 suffered head trauma and later died at the hospital.

Employee #1 was found unresponsive under a trailer while conducting yard trailer checks at a baking company. It is believed he was pinned between two tractor trailers, sustaining serious injuries including fractures, contusions, and hemorrhages. The incident was initially reported as a non-accidental death, leading to an investigation involving police, firefighters, and a homicide detective. The employer was notified by the employee's family in a meeting with the plant manager, who has since left.

Employee #1, who was working for a company involved in tractor operation and waste removal, was stung by multiple bees while cleaning up debris. The bee stings triggered an allergic reaction that quickly escalated into anaphylactic shock, ultimately leading to his untimely death.

Employee #1, working for a grading subcontractor at a construction site, was evaluating ground conditions when he was struck and run over by a John Deere 672G motor grader. Despite wearing a safety vest, the employee was killed in the incident. Both the employee and motor grader operator had received training, and there was communication between them prior to the accident. It is unclear why the employee changed paths and there were no eye-witnesses to the event.

Employee #1, a landscaping service worker, was mowing lawns in a residential subdivision alongside a coworker. While operating a SCAG Turf Tiger riding mower near a pond, the mower slid off the grass and rolled into the water, pinning Employee #1 beneath it. Despite the roll-over protection system being engaged, Employee #1 was not wearing a seat belt and tragically drowned in the 30-inch-deep water.

While working for a logging company, Employee #1 was carrying an empty bucket away from a tree felling area to prevent it from rolling into a creek. As he returned to the felling area, a coworker manually felling a tree above him cut through the back of the tree, causing it to fall towards the creek. Despite warnings from the employer, Employee #1, who was deaf and could only read lips and observe hand signals, did not take evasive action and was struck and killed

While installing a new light fixture in a hotel, Employee #1 used a 16 ft extension ladder on artificial grass against an exterior wall. The ladder slipped out from underneath him causing him to fall and strike a concrete surface. Employee #1 suffered a fractured right femur and right wrist, requiring treatment, surgical procedures, and hospitalization at a medical center.

Employee #1 started working for Ozark Stave as a wood stacker and later became the debarker operator. His job involved operating the Fulghum brand debarker, serial number 127758, to remove bark from logs. While attempting to realign logs that had fouled along the second log deck, he was found lying on the ground bleeding from his head with a cane hook lying across his chest. He was hospitalized and unfortunately succumbed to his head injuries.

Employee #1 was working on trim caulking on a fifth-floor balcony of a commercial building from a 12-foot step ladder. He lost his balance while reaching out to apply masking tape to the ceiling, falling over the railing to the concrete pavement below. Employee #1, who was not wearing fall protection equipment, was killed in the fall.

Employee #1 was working from a bucket truck without her harness anchored to the bucket. The door of the bucket was opened and she fell approximately 14 feet to the ground, landing on her face. She was hospitalized for facial injuries and tragically passed away shortly afterwards.

Employee #1 was installing a fabricated header from a ladder when the wooden post holding it in place came loose, causing the ladder to be struck. Employee #1 fell from the ladder and was fatally injured when he struck his neck against a piece of wood. The wood punctured his carotid artery, leading to his death.

Employee #1 was working from a ladder, performing demolition work. The employee was removing ceiling tile materials and fell from the ladder. The employee sustained injuries to his back in the fall and was hospitalized.

Employee #1 was working from a ladder. The employee came in contact with live electrical wires and received a shock. The employee then fell off the ladder, sustained injuries associated with the fall and was hospitalized.

Employee #1 was working on a mobile scaffold at a height of five feet, removing nailed boards from a wall with a hammer/crowbar. While pulling back on the boards, the employee lost balance and fell five feet to the concrete floor, resulting in a fatal injury.

Employee #1 was working from a scaffold. The employee tried to move from one board of the scaffold to another board. The board slipped, and Employee #1 fell 12 feet to the ground below. The employee sustained scrapes and bruises and was hospitalized for his injuries.

Employee #1 was working from a scissor lift to install a couplet on a pipe. During work, the employee drove the lift into a floor opening, causing the lift to roll over. Employee #1 sustained broken bones to his ribs and back, and was hospitalized for his injuries.

Employee #1 was working on an aerial lift spraying fire proofing materials on structural beams of a warehouse under construction. The lift fell off an uneven surface, throwing Employee #1 to his death.

While transferring tubes filled with nitric acid for a lead content analysis in a chemical lab, Employee #1 accidentally bumped the tray against a hot plate, causing nitric acid to splash onto her face and neck. Despite wearing proper protective gear, the acid caused chemical burns that required immediate medical attention and hospitalization.
Employee #1 was working in a confined space repairing a check valve on a gasoline distribution pump. The employee lost consciousness, was potentially asphyxiated and killed.
Employee #1 was working in a foundry.  This was his first day and he became flushed and overheated. Employee #1 suffered heat exhaustion and was hospitalized.

The owner and employee were waiting for a dump truck to unload asphalt into an asphalt paver. The dump truck made contact with an overhead power line, electrocuting and killing the employee who was observing from the other side of the paver.

The superintendent of a new home construction site was inspecting a roof with the city building inspector. The superintendent was pulled off the roof while attempting to rescue the building inspector who lost balance when climbing a ladder. The superintendent sustained a head injury.
There was a power outage.  A lineman touched a 7,200 volt line, and was electrocuted. The employee died immediately.

Two vehicle spotters were on site, with Employee #1 finishing backing up a dump truck. Employee #1 then walked behind a semi truck trailer being backed up by Employee #2, resulting in Employee #1 being run over by the trailer and killed.

Three employees were preparing to start rolling trusses on a construction site when they took a break. Employee #1 did not show up for the break and was later found on the ground. He was rushed to the hospital but sadly passed away from medical complications related to blunt cervical trauma.

Three employees were working to install three speakers on a new lower level ceiling platform of a movie theater. Employee #2 fell through the platform while handing a speaker to Employee #1, causing the ceiling to collapse and injuring both employees. Employee #3, who was holding the ladder, was also injured. The incident was attributed to the lack of tap gun screws to secure the ceiling, leading to an unstable work surface.

While changing out a TMI bubbler in an enclosed cabinet of an OE Reactor, three employees were injured in an explosion. Employee #1 sustained multiple injuries including a laceration to his artery on the right wrist, a broken right middle finger, and burns to his left arm. Employee #2 experienced ringing in their ears, while employee #3 suffered a fractured left index finger, lacerations, and ringing in their ears.

Three employees were climbing down from an elevated pipe rack.  As they were climbing down, the stainless steel Foul Condensate tank exploded, striking the employees and tossing their bodies 200 yards from the explosion.  All three employees were killed.

Three employees were drilling for water and installation of a well when the rig struck a patch of natural gas, causing an explosion. The employees suffered severe burns to various parts of their bodies and were hospitalized for treatment.

Three employees were installing a 4 inch sewer line in a 12 ft. trench.The employee a 33 year old male, was inside the trench leveling out the bottom when the walls of the trench collapsed, trapping and killing the employee underneath.

Three employees were attempting to place a 40 foot aluminum ladder against an exterior wall to access the roof of a building when they lost control of the ladder. The ladder fell backwards and struck a 7,200 V power line, causing electrical current to flow through the three employees. Two employees suffered serious injuries from the shock, while the third employee was electrocuted and killed in the incident.

While three employees were preparing to enter a confined space, Employee #1 was being lowered down a wastewater well using a mobile mini crane to clean out mud and debris at the bottom. Tragically, Employee #1 lost consciousness and fell 50 feet to the bottom of the pit, where he was pronounced dead at the scene by the Los Angeles City Fire Department Urban Search and Rescue team.

During a warehouse operation, a turret and a cherry picker collided, causing the turret operator to be thrown from the vehicle and the cherry picker to overturn with two employees tied off in the cage. All three employees sustained injuries and were hospitalized for treatment.

Three employees were cleaning a parking lot when a forklift truck operated in reverse exited a nearby cable shop, hitting and killing one of the employees. The forklift truck, which weighed approximately 28,850 lbs, did not slow down or sound its horn before striking the employee. The back-up alarm on the forklift was also inoperable at the time of the incident.

Three employees were using a crew boat to remove chains from a Yokohama ship fender. The rough conditions caused the boat to hit a barge, capsize, and sink. Employee #1 jumped off the boat and was found dead the next day. Employees #2 and #3 were able to swim to the surface and hold onto the boat until help arrived.

Three employees were working on upgrading a sewer line when the trench collapsed, pinning Employee #1 from the chest down. Despite noticing the cave-in, Employee #1 could not escape in time and suffered fatal injuries. The trench, which was over 6 feet deep and 2 feet wide, did not have a protective system that could fit in it.

During a windstorm at a jobsite, three employees were injured by flying debris. Two employees suffered concussions after being struck by large pieces of plywood and roofing insulation, while a third employee was hit by a smaller piece of plywood. Only one of the employees required hospitalization for their injuries.

Three employees in a restaurant kitchen were injured when a pressure fryer's latch gave way, causing the lid to fly off and spray hot oil onto Employees #1, #2, and #3. Employees #2 and #3 were treated for burns and released from the hospital the same day, while Employee #1 was taken to a burn unit for further treatment.

Three employees at Parkrose Hardware Store experienced symptoms of dizziness, burning noses, and headaches while working in the upper area. After closing the office and turning off the heating system, they replaced the heat exchanger as a precaution. One employee was found to have elevated levels of carbon monoxide in her blood after going to the hospital. Normal work has resumed with no further issues.

Three workers were hanging Densi Glass when the scaffold they were working on tipped over, causing Employee #3 to be crushed underneath and Employee #1 and Employee #2 to fall. All three employees were hospitalized with non-life threatening injuries including a bruised knee, a concussion, and a fractured rib.

Two employees were taping sheet rock inside an elevator shaft at different levels. Employee #2's platform collapsed, causing them to fall onto Employee #1. Both employees, along with 26 pieces of sheet rock, fell to the basement, resulting in the death of both workers.

Two employee were installing metal roof trim and both employees fell off platform. One employee was killed from blunt force trauma to head and the other employee was hospitalized for unspecified injuries.
Two employee were transporting two inmates back from the Pottawattamie County courthouse to Pottawattamie County Jail.  Both employees were shot by an inmate with a firearm.

Two employees were cleaning combustible wood fiber/dust surrounding reversing belt #3 when a dust explosion occurred, resulting in severe burns for both workers. Tragically, one of the employees did not survive his injuries.

While assisting a cow with birthing a calf, Employee #1 at Swisher Country Cattle Company injured their knee when trying to flee from the cow that turned around and approached them. Employee #2 was also present during the incident.

Two employees were working together to replace damaged metal roof sheets on a farm building. Employee #1 lost his balance and fell approximately 21 feet to the concrete surface, resulting in his death.

During an inspection of the I-beam supporting a swing-stage scaffold system, one employee fell approximately 40 feet to their death when the scaffold collapsed. Another employee was left suspended from his lifeline and suffered minor injuries. The investigation revealed the I-beam exceeded its load capacity, causing the scaffold system to collapse.

During a tire maintenance task on a John Deere 644C Front-End Loader, one employee had another employee lift the front tires off the ground so the bead could be set on the left tire. The employee used a chain and a come-a-long tool to apply pressure to the tire, but a chain link or the come-a-long hook broke and struck the employee in the head, leading to a fatal skull fracture and traumatic brain injury.
Two employees were cleaning the edge of an interior wall.  The block wall collapsed on top of the two employees.    Both employees were crushed, one fatally and one was hospitalized.

While clearing a fallen tree from a road, two employees were struck by a passing vehicle. Unfortunately, Employee #1 was thrown 17 feet and pronounced dead on the scene. Employee #2 was rushed to IU Health Bloomington with no further information provided on their condition.

While cutting through a concrete floor to replace a sewer pipe inside a condominium complex, two employees using a gas powered concrete saw equipped with an exhaust purifier began to experience symptoms of carbon monoxide exposure. Despite the purifier only reducing carbon monoxide levels to 5,000 ppm, the employees were exposed to levels exceeding 50 ppm within just 30 minutes. The fire department measured levels over 300 ppm, and carboxyhemoglobin levels two hours after exposure were 19.5%

Two employees were dismantling a lane closure along a major interstate highway.  While removing the last remaining temporary sign, both employees were struck by a motor vehicle.  Employee #1 was hospitalized with a broken right leg and severely lacerated right arm and Employee #2 was killed.

Two employees were filling out employment paperwork sitting on desk.  At approximately 500 feet way, a part of a boiler (CSR) exploded, flew 500 feet and went through the roof of the employer where two new employees were sitting. Both employees were struck and crushed to death.
Two employees were fishing from a boat on a lake. However, the employees never returned to the dock at quitting time. For an unknown reason, the employees drowned.

While two employees were positioning a cylindrical concrete manhole midsection onto a base section, one side of the form became detached from the lifting bar system, swinging into the excavation wall and then the base section. The form subsequently fell on top of the base section, fatally injuring Employee #1 with severe whole body trauma.

Two employees were handing a door through a window from a platform elevated by a forklift and the platform tilted.  Both employees fell with the platform and Employee #1 was killed and Employee #2 was hospitalized.

Two employees were hitching a trailer to a truck when a vehicle crashed into the trailer, crushing them between the trailer and the truck. One employee died at the scene from his injuries, while the other sustained multiple fractures and was hospitalized.

Two employees were in the process of removing a refractrometer.Both employees were sprayed with caustic black liquid while removing the refractrometer, and both received chemical burns and were hospitalized. lized.

Two employees fell 24 feet from ladders while installing a light fixture on a pole barn. They were working on a mobile scaffold platform that tipped over due to instability, lack of proper bracing, and failure to secure it to the building. Employee #1 tragically died from head trauma after falling on concrete, while Employee #2 sustained a shattered elbow and was hospitalized.

Two employees were installing black fiber board onto bridge cap #5 when the employee stepped off the bridge cap losing his balance and fell 50 feet. The coworker working with him was bending down and looking down.  The employee was killed from the fall.

Two employees were unloading materials from a trailer on a narrow street when another vehicle struck the trailer from behind. Both employees sustained severe injuries to their abdomen and rib cage and were hospitalized for treatment.

Two employees were replacing old sky lights on the roof of a truck shop building when one of them stepped on a skylight that could not support their weight. The employee fell 19 feet through the skylight and struck the concrete floor, resulting in head trauma and tragically, their death.
Two employees were operating a pump truck, when a vessel exploded.  Both employees were hospitalized and one was treated for a burst eardrum.

Two employees were operating a truck mounted articulating boom to change lights on light poles.  The hydraulic system on the boom mechanically failed.  The employees were secured to the lift, but were ejected from the basket during the failure, fell 50 feet to the ground, and were killed.

Two employees were performing a rubber asphalt 109 test for Caltrans.While pumping oil into a test tank, both employees suffered burns of varying severity on their hands when there was an overspill of oil and tar. Both employees were hospitalized and treated for their injuries.

Two employees were cleaning up a golf course when one employee jumped on the back of a moving golf cart and fell off, fracturing their right ankle. Despite initial refusal of medical treatment, the employee later discovered the fracture had caused a blood clot that traveled to their heart, leading to their passing away a week later due to a pre-existing heart condition.
Two employees were pollinating palm trees using an aerial basket.  The basket contacted high voltage (12KV) power lines 33 feet high and the employees were electrocuted and killed.

During plastic piping fusion preparation, employees were connecting steel piping to a crude oil tank that had not been properly emptied or vented. Flammable vapors ignited, causing three tanks to explode and a flash fire that resulted in severe burns. One worker was killed, while others were hospitalized for burns of varying degrees.

Two employees were preparing to wash the interior of a tanker truck.  The confined space was not ventilated and the employees become unconscious by inhaling naptha fumes.  Both employees were killed when found.
Two employees were removing a failed sump pump from a wet well and both were killed by hydrogen sulfide exposure.

Two employees were removing road tar and a vehicle lost control and struck the two employees while they were working alongside the road. Both employees sustained multiple fractures and blunt force trauma and were killed.

During a tire replacement on a 2009 CTM Commander Tomato Harvester, a jack slipped, causing one employee to be pinned between the tire and undercarriage. The employee suffered upper torso crush injuries and tragically lost their life as a result of the incident.
Two employees were riding in a self-propelled scaffold.  The platform hit an an overhang, and as a result, one employee fell to the ground, and sustained a fatal head injury.

Two employees were securing a generator in place. As they used cordless, battery-operated drills to tighten bolts into place, a spark occurred. A flash fire resulted, engulfing the two employees. The two employees were hospitalized where they were treated for first, second, and third-degree burns.

Employee #1 was tragically killed when he was struck by a flatbed pickup truck driven by his co-worker while setting drums for a lane closure on I-40 westbound. The driver accidentally ran over Employee #1, who was standing at the rear of the truck, causing blunt head trauma.

Two employees were setting up a 40 foot extension aluminum ladder. As the employees leaned the ladder onto a 13,800 volt power line, one employee was electrocuted, while the other sustained an electric shock, which he was hospitalized and received treatment for burns to his feet and legs.

Two employees were transporting a loaded potato truck from the field to the office when it was struck by a freight train at an uncontrolled railway crossing. The driver, Employee #1, was killed in the accident while Employee #2, a passenger in the truck, was taken to the hospital with serious injuries.

Two employees on a farm were using a Utility Task Vehicle (UTV) to check flooded fields. They were hit from behind by a truck while trying to cross the highway to reach another area of the farm. Employee #1 died and Employee #2 was injured in the incident. The employees were not wearing seatbelts or helmets as recommended by the manufacturer, and the UTV's roll-bar lights were on.

During the installation of a 2-ton AC unit on a two-story building, two employees used a winch to lift the condenser onto the roof. When the condenser did not clear the eve of the roof, Employee #1 leaned out to push it using the wire rope of the winch. The wire rope broke, causing both Employee #1 and the condenser to fall approximately 18 feet. Tragically, Employee #1 was killed when he struck his head on the concrete below

Two employees were weeding a melon field and exhibited symptoms of heat illness.  One employee fainted but both were taken to the hospital.  The employee that fainted was treated for work-related heat illness.  Neither employee was hospitalized.

Two employees, one being the owner of a landscape architectural firm and the other a 17-year-old minor, were trimming trees at a residential site in South Tampa, FL. The trees were near overhead power lines owned by TECO, with energized phase conductors at 7,620 volts. While using a 9.8-meter aluminum extension ladder, the ladder made contact with a phase conductor, resulting in both workers sustaining an electric shock and being knocked to the ground. While working in a field harvesting wheat, two employees were attempting to tow a semi truck up a hill when the water tender truck they were using rolled backwards, striking them. Sadly, one employee was pinned between the vehicles and died at the scene, while the other suffered injuries to the left side of his face and was taken to the hospital for treatment. He was later transferred by air ambulance to another medical center for further care.

Two employees were working inside a boiler / incinerator removing build up when hot material fell on both of them.  They were both wearing full face respirators and suits. The medic stated that one employee received possible third degree burns over 80% of his body.

Two coworkers were working together to remove a finished product from a mold, with one operating the forklift and the other positioning the product on the forks. The forklift operator accidentally pressed on a pedal, causing the forklift to pin the 23 year old employee between the forklift and the mold machine, resulting in fatal crushing injuries to the head.

While working to install a bearing on a powered industrial truck indoors in the Maintenance Shop, two employees used a 6 riser Mobile Ladder Stand positioned sideways next to the forklift. Employee #1 stood on the top step to install the bearing while Employee #2 stood on the lower steps and pried the mast apart with a screwdriver. The lateral force caused the ladder stand to kick out, resulting in both employees falling.

Two workers were killed in a tank explosion. The tank was from the World War II era. Upon receiving report of the explosion, emergency services arrived onsite to provide rescue efforts; however, the two workers could not be saved. workers could not be saved.

During the process of removing the baler machine from the production area, Employee #1 attempted to remove plastic pallets from in front of the machine while it was leaning forward. The baler swung unexpectedly, hitting Employee #1 against the pallets. As a result, Employee #1 suffered a forearm laceration and head concussion.
Upon returning from lunch, an employee took a manager hostage and held a gun to his head. The employee was shot by  a SWAT team with a 9 mm bullet.

While conducting logging activities, an employee was crushed by felled trees that were attached to a cable and being removed by a skidder. The employee died at the scene by the time emergency services arrived at the site.
While Employee #1 conducted welding and grinding activities on a piece of structural steel, a piece of metal shaving lodged into his eye, resulting in an eye infection.
While pruning trees and removing weeds, an employee died after being stung by a wasp on the throat, causing swelling and asphyxiation.

During a structure fire response, a firefighter pulled on a charged fire hose to move it to a different side of the building. The force caused the nozzle to open and water to flow, leading to it hitting the firefighter on the left wrist and hand, knocking off their helmet. The firefighter was taken to the hospital with a concussion and bruised wrist.

During the construction process on site, an employee was working on erecting form work for concrete pouring. While standing on a ladder, the employee attached his fall harness to a wooden brace for support. However, the brace failed, causing the employee to fall onto the concrete slab below and sustain facial and head injuries. The employee was hospitalized and received medical treatment for his injuries.

During a drilling operation to replace an anode on an underground gas supply line for corrosion control, an employee was struck in the abdomen by the drilling rig and knocked to the ground. The employee suffered an abdominal injury and had to be hospitalized as a result of the incident.
